GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTIONNO 3500 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
CONSERVATION OF NATIONAL CULTURE HERITAGE UNDER NCF AND AMASR 
ACT 
 
†3500 SHRI TARIQ ANWAR 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has made a state wise assessment of the progress of conservation, 
renovation and development works of monuments and cultural heritage sites protected under 
the National Culture Fund and the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and 
Remains Act, 1958 from the year 2023-24 till date; 
 
(b) If so, the details thereof; 
(c) Whether the Government has reviewed visitor facilities, digital documentation, conservation 
works and heritage promotion programmes at monuments under the protection of the 
Archaeological Survey of India; 
(d) If so, the major findings thereof; 
(e) Whether the government is considering to approving additional central initiatives or projects 
to promote the conservation of lesser known cultural and archaeological heritage of the 
country and for the conservation and development of sites associated with the historical and 
cultural heritage of Bihar, especially the Seemanchal region; and 
(f)  If so, the details thereof; 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a)  
& 
(b) 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has made a state wise assessment of the progress of 
conservation, renovation and development works of monuments and cultural heritage sites 
protected by the ASI. 
 
Conservation and maintenance of these monuments is a regular process and is taken up as per 
the need of monument and availability of resources. Regular Inspections are carried out by the 
Officers of ASI for assessing the conservation and renovation works of monuments and 
cultural heritage sites. 
 
ASI takes up conservation and maintenance works of protected monuments every year. Details 
of allocation and expenditure made on the conservation of protected monument from 2023-24 
to 05.08.2026 are attached at Annexure-A. 
 
Monuments and heritage sites are not protected under the National Culture Fund (NCF). NCF 
only provides financial assistance for conservation, renovation and development works of 
some monuments and cultural heritage sites protected by the ASI. The list of works taken up at 
ASI protected monuments under the NCF during the last three years is placed at Annexure-B. 
 
  

(c) 
& 
(d) 
ASI regularly reviews the visitor facilities, digital documentation, conservation works and 
heritage promotion programmes at monuments under its jurisdiction across the country. 
 
The details of visitor facilities available at ASI monuments and sites are placed at the 
Annexure-C. 
 
Besides, ASI, through its field offices, organizes community-driven and people-centric 
heritage promotion programmes on protected monuments/sites, such as walkthroughs, talks, 
drawing and painting competitions for school and college students, photo exhibitions for 
visitors, and consultative meetings with locals and community stakeholders on various 
occasions such as World Heritage Day, World Tourism Day, Museum Day, International 
Women’s Day, World Heritage Week and International Day of Yoga among others, and at the 
time of various other national celebrations as and when entrusted with, to raise awareness 
about the need for sensitization toward the protection of the country's heritage. 
 
(e) 
& 
  (f) 
ASI undertakes conservation and maintenance of all centrally protected monuments including 
lesser-known monuments as per requirement and availability of resources. 
 
The details of approved Conservation works in respect of ASI protected monuments in the 
state of Bihar, including one monument located in Seemanchal region namely Kanhaiya Ji ka 
Mandir at Dist. Kishanganj, for Financial Year 2026-27 are attached at Annexure-D.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3501 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 10, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
CSR EXPENDITURE THROUGH IMPLEMENTING AGENCIES  
QUESTION 
 
 
3501. Shri  Radhakrishna:  
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the total Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) expenditure incurred by 
companies through Implementing Agencies (IAs) registered under Form CSR -1, 
year-wise since April 2021, distinguishing between (i) IAs established by the 
funding company itself or jointly with other companies and (ii) independent public 
trusts, societies or Section 8 companies;  
 
(b) the CSR funds allocated, sanctioned, released and actually spent by such self-
created implementing agencies during each of the last five financial years, year-
wise;  
 
(c) the number of instances where unspent CSR funds held by any implementing 
agency, including self-created ones, remained unutilised beyond the permissible 
three-year ongoing project period and the action taken thereon; and  
 
(d) whether the Government now maintains a consolidated database of CSR -1 
registered agencies showing common directors/trustees with the funding 
company and if not, the reason for this persisting gap? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS   AND MINISTER 
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a) & (b):  The entities covered under Rule 4(1) of the Companies (CSR Policy) 
Rules, 2014 are required to fill the relevant information in CSR-1 form which is for 
the sole purpose of registration for undertaking CSR activities. CSR -1 form 
captures the details of Implementing Agencies established by any company or 
group of companies registered through CSR -1 and independent public trusts, 
societies or Section 8 companies  and does not have the details of utilisation of 
CSR funds by them.  On the basis of filling by these entities , the details of 
registration of such entities in last five financial years (FYs) i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-
26 is attached at Annexure. There is no provision of allocation, sanction and 
release of CSR funds in CSR legal framework. 
Contd…2/- 

 
-2- 
(c): Section 135 (5) & (6) of the Act provides for treatment of unspent CSR amount. 
In the case of an ongoing project, the company is required to transfer the unspent 
amount to a special account of the company i.e ‘Unspent CSR Account’, within 30 
days from the end of financial year and spend the same in pursuance of its CSR 
policy within the next three financial years from the date of such transfer. After 
the lapse of three financial years, the amount remaining unspent, if any, is 
required to be transferred to any Fund mentioned in Schedule VII of the Act within 
a period of thirty days from the date of completion of the third financial year. The 
Ministry has notified the Companies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2020, (“CARO, 
2020”) which requires auditors to stat e details of any unspe nt CSR amount . 
Whenever violation of CSR provisions is reported, action against such non -
compliant Companies is initiated as per provisions of the Act after due 
examination of records and following due process of law. 
(d): The Ministry maintains database of directors/trustees of the entities covered 
under Rule 4(1) of Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014 as reported by respective 
entities while filing of CSR -1 form. As regards the details of directors of funding 
company, the same is also available on public domain which can be accessed at 
www.mca.gov.in.

INCREASE IN DIRECT AND INDIRECT TAX COLLECTIONS 
 
 †3502. SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
SHRI OMPRAKASH BHUPALSINH ALIAS PAVAN RAJENIMBALKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be please to state: 
 
(a) the details of direct and indirect tax collections in the country during the last five years along with the categories 
thereof, year-wise; 
 
(b) the details of the changes observed in the revenue accrued to States following the implementation of Goods and 
Services Tax (GST) and whether it has been evaluated; 
 
  (c) the details of the amount disbursed to States as GST compensation during the said period ;  
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to curb tax evasion; and 
 
(e) the extent of increase in the number of taxpayers filing Income Tax Returns during the last five years along with 
the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
 
 
(a): The details of direct and indirect tax collections in the country during the last five years along with the 
categories thereof, year-wise, are at Annex ‘A’. 
(b): The details of the changes observed in the revenue accrued to States following the implementation of Goods and 
Services Tax (GST) are at Annex ‘B’. 
(c): The details of GST compensation released during the last Five Years are at Annex ‘C’. 
 
 

2 | P a g e 
 
 
(d): The steps taken by the Government to curb tax evasion are as under: 
Direct Taxes 
i. Mandatory Quoting of PAN and linking of PAN Aadhaar– Quoting of PAN has been mandated for specified 
transactions and linking of PAN and Aadhaar has also been made compulsory. 
ii. Annual Information Statement (AIS): It is a statement that provides complete information about a taxpayer for a 
particular financial year. It contains information about taxpayers' incomes, financial transactions, tax details, etc. 
This transparency curbs evasion by making under-reporting or omission of income easily detectable. 
iii. NUDGE Campaign– NUDGE stands for Non-Intrusive Usage of Data to Guide and Enable, which focuses on 
compliance and correcting filing of the ITRs and related Schedules. Taxpayers are nudged via SMS/email to self-
correct, using the facility of revised returns, updated returns which allows reporting of earlier undisclosed income 
even after the due date of filing original. 
iv. Prohibition of cash transactions– Cash receipt of rupees two lakh or more otherwise than by electronic modes has 
been prohibited under section 186 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. 
v. Black Money Act– In order to curb the flow of black money stashed abroad, the Black Money (Undisclosed 
Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015 (the Black Money Act) has been enacted. 
vi. Benami Law– The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 was comprehensively amended by the Benami 
Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act, 2016 to enable confiscation of Benami Property and prosecution of 
benamidar and the beneficial owner. 
Indirect Taxes 
i. In order to further streamline auto-population of ITC data in returns, the Invoice Management System (IMS) 
facility has been introduced on the GST portal in late 2024, to help recipient taxpayers manage incoming invoices 
more effectively. It allows recipients to accept, reject, or mark invoices as pending when these are saved or filed by 
their supplier taxpayers. With the implementation of IMS, registered recipients can now cross-verify and reconcile 
invoices reported by suppliers in their GSTR-1, thereby streamlining and strengthening the ITC claim process. 
ii. Two special drives, respectively for the period 16.05.2023 to 14.08.2023 and 16.08.2024 to 30.10.2024, were 
launched on all India basis, both by Central as well as State tax administrations, for a concerted and coordinated 
action against fake registrations and fraudulent passing of ITC. The drive against non-existent/ fake registrations 
involved physical verification of the business premises of the taxpayers by duly constituted teams of tax officials. 
The field verification was accompanied by preparation of necessary reports bringing out the outcome of the 
verification.

IMPACT OF STAGNANT REAL WAGES 
 
3503. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY: 
  SHRI SUNIL BOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of average real wages of workers in rural and urban 
areas, including regular  salaried workers, casual labourers and 
self-employed workers since year 2015 and category wise; 
(b)whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding 
the impact of stagnant real wages on household consumption and 
living standards in the country and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)the details of measures taken or proposed to improve wage 
growth, job quality and income  security by the Government for 
workers in both organised and unorganised sectors? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (c): Labour Bureau, an attached office of Ministry of Labour & 
Employment compiles and maintains average  nominal daily wage 
rates for selected agricultural and non -agricultural occupations, 
based on information collected by the National Sample  Survey 
Organisation from a fixed set of 600 sample villages across 20 States, 
up to June 2025.  
  The minimum rates of wages for employments under the 
Central Sphere are notified by the Central Government and are 
revised periodically based on increase in Consumer Price Index for 
Industrial Workers (CPI -IW). The details of the minimum wages 
notified by the Central Government as on 30.03.2026 are available at 
https://clc.gov.in/clc/sites/default/files/mygov_17751372721.pdf

effect from 21.11.2025, has subsumed the provisions of the Minimum 
Wages Act, 1948; Payment of Wages Act, 1936, Payment of Bonus

the Code on Wages 2019, both Central an d the State Governments 
are empowered to enforce the provisions of the Code by appointment 
of various authorities as prescribed under the Code such as 
“Authority to hear and decide claims”, “Appellate Authority”, 
“Inspector-cum-facilitator” and “Enquiry Officer”.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3504 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
  
ASSESSMENT OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES 
†3504. SMT. JYOTSNA CHARANDAS MAHANT: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of candidates trained and placed in employment across the country under 
the major skill development initiatives since 2019, year and scheme -wise, State/UT-wise including 
Chhattisgarh; 
 
(b) whether the Government maintains any data on the average salary of candidates securing 
employment after completion of training and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government maintains data regarding retention in employment for six months 
and one year after securing employment and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the effectiveness of these skill 
development initiatives in improving employability and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) to (d) : Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS),  National Apprenticeship Promotion 
Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), 
to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Chhattisgarh. The SIM 
aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills.  
  
State/UT-wise, year-wise and scheme -wise details of the number of candidates trained across the 
country under the major skill development schemes of MSDE during the period from 2019 –20 to 
2026–27 (as on 30.06.2026) are given at Annexures I to IV.  
  
Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short -Term Training 
component of PMKVY only in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) 
implemented from 2015 -16 to 2021 -22. Under PMKVY (1.0 to 3.0), 28,142 candidates have been 
reported placed in Chhattisgarh. Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates 
to choose their varied career path with orientation through industry relevant skill courses that 
include the On-the-Job Training (OJT).  
 
The Government undertakes periodic reviews of skilling initiatives under the Skill India Mission, 
assessing enrolment, certification, placement, self-employment outcomes and employer feedback to 

gauge their effectiveness in strengthening employability and future skills. These reviews support 
continuous curriculum updates, industry collaboration and improvements in implementation 
modalities, ensuring that skilling programmes remain aligned with evolving technology trends and 
labour-market requirements. The effectiveness of broader skill development schemes is also 
evaluated through MIS-based monitoring, third-party assessments and beneficiary feedback.  
  
All schemes presently being run by MSDE have gone through third party evaluation exercise 
generally and also in particular, at the time of grant of extension of the respective schemes. Details 
of the evaluation of the Schemes implemented by MSDE are as under: 
  
PMKVY 4.0: An independent third -party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted 
by Arun Jaitley  National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a 
measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined 
share of employed and self -employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 
45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income - related 
outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition 
of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and 
certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and 
certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment 
participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. 
  
JSS: A third -party evaluation of the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme was conducted by the 
Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management, an autonomous Institution of Ministry of 
Finance, Government of India, in 2025 to assess the scheme’s outreach, effectiveness and 
livelihood outcomes. The evaluation highlighted significant achievements of the scheme, with 33.94 
lakh individuals enrolled, of whom 32 lakh were trained and 31.52 lakh  certified, reflecting an overall 
success rate of 99 percent. Women constituted a dominant 82 percent share of total participants, 
while 73 percent beneficiaries belonged to marginalized sections, including SC/ST (36 percent) and 
OBC (37 percent). The livelihood impact has been noteworthy, with 90 percent alumni utilising  
acquired skills for income generation, 82 percent becoming economically engaged within six months 
of training, and 60 percent of previously non -earning individuals starting to earn post -training. The 
average monthly income of beneficiaries recorded a four-fold increase. 
  
NAPS: A third-party evaluation study of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(PMNAPS-2) from 2022 -23 to 2025 -26 (Data up to 30 th November 2025) was  conducted by the 
Arun Jaitley  National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMNAPS -2 achieved significant scale 
during the evaluation period, engaging 34.69 lakh apprentices against a cumulative target of 46 
lakh, translating into an overall achievement of approximately 75 percent. The institutionalization of 
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) has improved financial transparency and predictability.

       GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
                  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
                 LOK SABHA 
                     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3505 
                    TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
          Capturing of Violent Wild Animals 
 
3505. SHRI TRIVENDRA SINGH RAWAT: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any special scheme or action plan is being implemented by the Government and the 
State Forest Department for capturing violent and man-eating wild animals like leopards, tigers, 
bears and other such wild animals and for preventing  incidents  of human-wildlife conflict; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of funds allocated and expenditure incurred for the purpose during the last two years, 
year-wise; 
(d) the details of number of wild animals captured, translocated or other necessary action taken in 
such cases, State/UT and wildlife-wise; and 
(e) the extent to which aforesaid schemes and measures have reduced the  incidents of human-
wildlife conflict and loss of human lives along with the major outcomes thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): The management of wildlife including the mitigation of human-wildlife conflict is 
primarily the responsibility of the concerned States/UTs. The State Governments & Union 
Territory Administrations are the first responders to any conflict situation and they maintain 
the details of the conflict along with the species involved.  
 
The Ministry provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the Centrally Sponsored 
umbrella scheme, ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’, comprising the sub-schemes 
‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’ and ‘Project Tiger and Elephant’, for managing human-
wildlife conflict. The assistance covers, inter-alia, the capture and relocation of problematic 
wild animals, creation of infrastructure for translocated animals, monitoring and driving away 
such animals, compensation for loss of human life and damage to crops and property, insurance 
coverage, public awareness, and capacity-building of Forest Department staff. Details of the 
funds released under the scheme during the last two years are placed at Annexures I and II.  
 
Section 11(1) (a) of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, empowers Chief Wild Life Wardens 
of the States/Union Territories to grant permission for capturing or translocating any wild 
animal, listed in Schedule-I, that is become dangerous to human life. Such data is maintained 
at the level of the States/Union Territories.  
 

Further, the Ministry has launched a scheme titled “Tiger Outside Tiger Reserves” at an outlay 
of Rs.88.7 crores for mitigating human tiger negative interactions. In addition to diminish 
adverse impacts of Human Elephant Conflict, the Government of India has approved a 
Regional Action Plan for Elephant Conservation for the Southern States. The Ministry has 
established a Centre of Excellence for Human–Wildlife Conflict Management at the Salim Ali 
Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON), WII–South India Centre, Coimbatore, 
to strengthen the scientific and institutional framework for managing human–wildlife conflict. 
The measures taken by the Ministry have strengthened the prevention and management of 
human- wildlife conflict resulting in improved mitigation and adoption of evidence based and 
technology enabled approach.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3506 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
PRESERVATION AND PROMOTION OF SAMBALPURI CULTURAL HERITAGE 
3506. SHRI PRADEEP PUROHIT: 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to document, preserve and promote the 
intangible cultural heritage associated with Sambalpuri handloom weaving, folk music, folk dance 
and traditional festivals of western Odisha; 
(b) whether any proposal has been received for inclusion of these traditions in national or international 
heritage recognition programmes; and 
(c) the details of financial assistance provided for their preservation and promotion during the last five 
years? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The Ministry of Culture, through the Sangeet Natak Akademi (SNA), the nodal agency for 
Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), undertakes measures for the documentation, preservation and 
promotion of India's intangible cultural heritage, including traditional handloom weaving, folk 
music, folk dance and festivals.  
 
  SNA maintains and periodically updates the National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage 
and considers proposals received from communities, State Governments and other stakeholders 
for inclusion of eligible ICH elements.  
 
  With a view to promoting India's living cultural traditions internationally, the Government of 
India has joined the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural 
Heritage.  
 
(b) At present, no such proposal is pending consideration with the Ministry. 
 
(c) No dedicated fund has been earmarked specifically for the preservation and promotion of the 
intangible cultural heritage associated with Sambalpuri handloom weaving, folk music, folk 
dance and traditional festivals of western Odisha. However, the Ministry of Culture implements 
various schemes and programmes for the promotion and preservation of traditional art forms and 
intangible cultural heritage, including the Scheme for Financial Assistance for Allied Cultural 
Activities, the Cultural Function and Production Grant (CFPG) Scheme, and the Scheme for 
Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India. 
 
In addition, organizations such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi, ZCCs extend support for 
activities such as documentation, research, training, workshops, festivals and other measures for 
safeguarding eligible intangible cultural traditions across the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3507 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
PM-VBRY 
 
3507. SMT. POONAMBEN HEMATBHAI MAADAM: 
  SMT. D K ARUNA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) the details of the number of persons getting first -time employment 
under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY); 
(b) the details of the special provisions made under th e said scheme to 
encourage employment generation in the manufacturing sector in the 
country; 
(c) the details of eligibility criteria prescribed for employers to avail 
incentives under Part B of the PM-VBRY Scheme; and 
(d) the details of the steps taken by the Government to ensure that the 
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism under PM -VBRY provides 
timely, transparent and efficient delivery of benefits to all eligible 
employees? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The Union Cabinet, on 1 July 2025, approved the Employment 
Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment generation, enhance 
employability, and strengthen social security across all sectors, with a 
particular focus on the manufacturing sector. The scheme has a 
registration period of two years from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 and a 
budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 Crore for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 2031-
32. 
   The scheme comprises two parts, i.e. Part A and Part B, and 
focuses on providing support to both employees and employers by way 
of incentives.  
   Under Part A of the scheme, the first-time employees of both 
existing and new establishments shall be eligible for an i ncentive 
equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, subject to a maximum of ₹15,000.  
   This incentive will be payable in two instalments during the 
first year of employment. The first instalment, up to ₹7,500, shall be 
disbursed after  completion of six  months  of  continuous  employment. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
Eligibility for the second instalment shall arise after completion of 
twelve months of employment and successful completion of the 
prescribed Financial Literacy Programme. This second instalment shall 
be credited to an appropriate savings instrument/savings account for a 
specified period.  
   Part B incentivizes employers by providing up to ₹3,000 per 
month for each additional employment sustained for at least 6 months 
for two years , with extended benefits for another two years for the 
manufacturing sector.  
  All establishments, including New as well as the exempted 
establishments covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952 (subsumed in the 
Code on Social Security, 2020), are eligible under the scheme, 
provided they file the ECR along with contributions regularly and fulfil 
other conditions of the scheme.  
  Comprehensive Scheme Guidelines, outlining the eligibility 
criteria for incentives to both employees and employers, have been 
issued. The scheme and its pr ovisions have been widely disseminated 
through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme -related processes and for real -time 
monitoring of beneficiaries and sector-wise progress. 
  For effective implementation of the scheme, a robust 
monitoring framework has been instituted. A steering Committee with 
representation from various labour -intensive and related 
Ministries/Department and an internal Executive Committee have been 
constituted to ensure effective monitoring of the scheme.  
  The PMVBRY is a demand -driven scheme. Since the 
implementation of the scheme, an incentive amount of ₹744.58 crore 
has been disbursed to 13.18 lakh first -time employees under Part A, 
while ₹2,068.84 crore has been disbursed to 67,369 beneficiary 
establishments under Part B of the scheme, up to June 2026, across the 
country. 
  The incentives to employees are disbursed through the 
Aadhaar Bridge Payment System (ABPS) under the Direct Benef it 
Transfer (DBT) framework to their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts, after 
due verification, including Aadhaar authentication and validation of 
Aadhaar-bank account linkage. The incentives to establishments are 
disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)  to their PAN -linked 
bank accounts after due verification of the establishment's credentials.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

                     TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
      Scientific and Technology-based Systems for Wildlife Conservation 
 
3508.  SHRI MANOJ TIWARI: 
SMT. SHOBHANABEN MAHENDRASINH BARAIYA: 
SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY: 
SHRI P P CHAUDHARY: 
SHRI ALOK SHARMA: 
SMT. MAHIMA KUMARI MEWAR: 
SHRI MAHESH KASHYAP: 
DR. SANJAY JAISWAL: 
SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any measures to strengthen scientific and technology-
based systems for wildlife conservation, biodiversity protection and effective management of human-
wildlife conflicts, if so, the details thereof including the major wildlife conservation programmes in 
which such technologies are being utilised; 
(b) the present status and progress achieved in utilisation of advanced genetic research facilities, digital 
biodiversity databases and wildlife information systems set up for prevention of wildlife crimes for 
wildlife conservation planning and biodiversity management   including the location of such facilities, 
State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether any institutional mechanism has been established to strengthen research, forensic 
capabilities and evidence-based decision-making in wildlife conservation, if so, the details thereof;  
(d) the manner in which these initiatives are expected to improve biodiversity conservation, wildlife 
monitoring and ecological management across the country particularly in Rajasthan specially in 
Kumbhalgarh area, Sehore district and Bhopal Lok Sabha Constituency; and 
(e) whether the Government is running any special programme to promote wildlife conservation, 
biodiversity management, research, capacity building and technical cooperation in collaboration with 
Forest Departments of States, research institutes, universities and other scientific organisations, if so, 
the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b): The management of wildlife including mitigation of human-animal conflicts is primarily the 
responsibility of the concerned State Government/Union Territory Administration. The State 
Government/UT Administration are the first responders to any conflict situation.  
 
The Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations 
under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development  of Wildlife Habitats for managing 
human-wildlife conflict which inter-alia supports procurement of early warning systems, construction 
and erection of physical barriers such as solar powered electric fencing, bio-fencing, trenches, 

boundary walls, capture and relocation of problematic wild animals, creation of infrastructure for 
translocated animals and monitoring and driving away such animals.  
 
Further, the Government has taken several measures to strengthen scientific and technology based 
systems for wildlife and biodiversity conservation besides for human-wildlife conflicts which include 
camera traps, GPS/satellite based radio telemetry, smart applications like M-STrIPES, geographical 
information systems, remote sensing, drones/UAVs for monitoring and surveillance, artificial 
intelligence based species segregation tools for estimation, hydrophones for dolphin assessment 
besides others. In addition conservation genetics is being utilized to validate wildlife corridors, address 
wildlife crime as well as ascertain the genetic composition of India’s wildlife which facilitates active 
management and translocation operations. 
 
(c) & (d): Wildlife conservation is grounded in science and evidence based information through species 
specific initiatives and action plans besides the All India Tiger Estimations is used in decision making.  
 
(e): The Ministry administers the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of “Integrated Development of Wildlife 
Habitats” which includes the components of “Development of Wildlife Habitats” and “Project Tiger 
& Elephant” to promote wildlife conservation across the country apart from assisting research through 
the Wildlife Institute of India, State Forest Research Institutes and other scientific organizations

3509. Shri Mani A: 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is implementing any welfare schemes 
for retired sportspersons including financial assistance, pensions, 
medical support, insurance coverage and other welfare benefits in 
Tamil Nadu, particularly those from Dharmapuri district and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(b) the details of number of retired athletes from Tamil Nadu, 
including Dharmapuri district,who  have benefited under such 
schemes during the last three years and the current 
year,discipline-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has taken measures to provide post -
retirement support through employment opportunities, coaching 
assignments, sports administration, skill dev elopment and 
livelihood assistance for retired athletes; and 
(d)  whether any additional initiatives are proposed to strengthen 
the social security, healthcare, financial stability and continued 
engagement of retired sportspersons  in mentoring young athletes, 
particularly in Dharmapuri district and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS [DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
(a) To (d): Sports' being a State subject the responsibility for 
promoting sports, including to promote the welfare of 
sportspersons/retired sportspersons rests primarily with the 
respective State Government. However, the Central Government 
supplements through schemes/programs/initiatives, as under: 
 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(i)        Scheme of Sports Fund for Pension to Meritorious 
Sportspersons provides additional financial security to 
sportspersons post retirement from active sports career in the 
form of life -time pension ranging from 12,000/ - to 20,000/ - per 
month. The sportspersons, who are retired from an active sports 
career an d won medals in Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, 
World Cup, World Championships,  Asian Games, Para Asian 
Games and Commonwealth Games, are eligible for life -time 
pension under the scheme. 
 
(ii)      Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Program 
for Sportsp ersons inter alia intends to provide financial 
assistance to retired sportspersons living in indigent 
circumstances; to family members of deceased sportspersons 
living in indigent circumstances; medical treatment; to 
sportsperson or their dependent family members and to Coaches 
and supporting sports professionals living in indigent 
circumstances. The financial assistance ranges up to 10 lakhs. 
 
The above mentioned schemes are implemented through out the 
country including Dharampuri district in Tamil Nadu. The list of 
beneficiaries under the above Schemes is available on the 
Ministry’s website at https://yas.gov.in. 
 
(iii) The Government has also taken initiative for post -
retirement rehabilitation through RESET' (Retired Sportspersons 
Empowerment Training) Programme which aims at facilitating 
retired athletes' career development by providing them tailor -
made education f or their academic enhancement supplemented 
with internship and empowering them with the necessary 
knowledge and skills for their transition into a suitable career 
option.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3510 
ANSWERED ON 10/08/2026 
 
Suicides in IITs 
 
3510.   Shri Selvaganapathi T.M.: 
Shri S Venkatesan: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the numbers of suicides by students, research scholars and staff across 
various Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) that have been reported during the last six years, 
year-wise and institute-wise; 
(b) the details of age, gender, caste, religion, State, date of suicide, place of occurrence, status 
of inquiry etc. of those who have committed suicide during the said period, institution-wise; 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to mitigate the factors contributing to student suicides; 
and 
(d) whether it is a fact that there is an urgent need for institutions to strengthen preventive 
mechanisms, if so, the steps taken by the Government in this regard? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to (d):  Comprehensive analysis of the data related to the accidental deaths and suicides in the 
country is published in the yearly Accidental Death & Suicide in India (ADSI) reports by 
National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB). Year wise and State wise details of student suicides are 
available in the ADSI reports which are accessible at: https://ncrb.gov.in/accidental-deaths-
suicides-in-india-year-wise.html To address the issue of suicide, the Government is taking multi-
pronged measures and provides psychological support to students, teachers and families for 
mental and emotional well-being to avoid incidences of suicide. An initiative of Ministry of 
Education, Manodarpan, covers a wide range of activities to provide psychological support to 
students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-being. 

UGC has issued Guidelines for Promotion of Physical Fitness, Sports, Student’s Health, 
Welfare, Psychological and Emotional Well- being at HEIs on 13.04.2023. The Ministry on 
10.07.2023 has also circulated a broad framework for emotional and mental well-being of 
students in Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) with request to take proactive measures to 
incorporate the same in the institutional functioning and instill a feeling of confidence in the 
student community. These guidelines lay emphasis inter alia on sports, yoga, meditation etc. to 
address the wellbeing and mental health concerns.  
An Integrated approach for Promoting Positive Mental Health, Resilience, and Wellbeing 
has been conceptualized under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme. Under this 
integrated approach, two fortnightly sessions are being held with faculty of higher education 
institutions to empower them to address student mental health concerns for early intervention. 
Annual National Wellbeing Conclaves were organised at IIT Hyderabad in November, 2024 and 
at IIT Bombay in November, 2025. A Regional Workshop on Mental Health was organized on 
12-13 July 2026 at IIT Madras, which brought together institutional leaders, faculty, students, 
and mental health professionals to share best practices and strengthen campus wellbeing 
ecosystems. 
At the institutional level, several HEIs are operationalising the framework through 
proactive, multi-layered models. For instance, IIT Kharagpur has implemented a comprehensive 
SETU (Support, Empathy, Transformation & Upliftment) framework, moving from reactive care 
to preventive, round-the-clock support. Adhering to the Ministry's guidelines, IIT Madras, IIT 
Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Gandhinagar and IIT Roorkee have conducted workshops on Mental 
Wellness & Stress Management. 
IITs have put in place mental health Counselling Centres /Wellness Centres within their 
campuses, staffed with full-time or visiting professional counsellors, clinical psychologists, and 
in some cases, psychiatrists. The institutes often host mental health training sessions to raise 
awareness, reduce stigma, and educate students about mental health issues.

3511. SHRI CHINTAMANI MAHARAJ: 
SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI: 
SHRI LUMBARAM CHOUDHARY: 
SHRI BIDYUT BARAN MAHATO:

SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
SHRI MANISH JAISWAL: 
SHRI RAHUL SINGH LODHI: 
DR. RAJESH MISHRA: 
SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI: 
SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation, achievements and 
environmental impact of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of saplings planted and their survival rate, along with the progress achieved, 
State/UT and Block-wise particularly in Rajasthan, Surguja District of Chhattisgarh, 
Nabarangpur and Sidhi Lok Sabha Constituencies including the details of participation of 
tribal communities, Gram Panchayats, Schools, Self Help Groups and other institutions; 
(c) the specific measures taken to boost public participation and institutional collaboration 
involving Panchayati Raj Institutions, Urban Local Bodies, schools and corporate entities; 

(d) the details of special mechanism established for geo-tagging of plantations, digital 
monitoring, survival assessment, long-term protection and maintenance to ensure effectiveness 
and sustained environmental benefits under the campaign; 
(e) the details of contribution of the campaign towards increasing green cover, restoring 
degraded landscapes, conserving biodiversity and achieving India's climate commitments; and 
(f) whether any special action plan or financial and technical assistance is being provided to 
promote indigenous species and water conservation in arid and desert regions like Kutch, if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): The 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign launched on 5 June 2024 on the occasion of 
World Environment Day promotes tree plantation as a people's movement to enhance 
environmental awareness and increase green cover across the country. The campaign is 
implemented through a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach with the active 
participation of Central and State Governments, educational institutions, business 
establishments, non-governmental organisations, environmental groups and the general public. 
Plantation and maintenance activities are primarily undertaken by the State Governments. 
State-wise details of saplings planted during 2026–27 (as on 05.08.2026) are at Annexure-A.  
 
As informed by the State Forest Department of Madhya Pradesh, 9,16,563 saplings have been 
planted in the Sidhi Lok Sabha Constituency under the campaign. As per data uploaded on the 
Meri LiFE Portal by the State Forest Departments, 29,773 saplings have been planted in 
Surguja district of Chhattisgarh and 7,28,062 saplings in Nabarangpur district of Odisha 
during 2026–27. District-wise details of saplings planted in Rajasthan are  provided at 
Annexure-B. Information regarding survival rate, block-wise plantation details and 
participation of tribal communities, schools, and other institutions are maintained by the 
respective State Governments/UT Administrations and is not maintained centrally. 
 
Plantations undertaken under the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign are uploaded on the Meri 
LiFE Portal. Plantations carried out by the State Forest Departments and Union Territories at 
various sites are geotagged, monitored, and survival assessments are undertaken by the 
States/UTs in accordance with the extant norms and procedures. 
 
The campaign promotes community participation in tree plantation and conservation, thereby 
supporting restoration of degraded landscapes, enhancing green cover, improvement of local 
ecological conditions and strengthening of biodiversity through increased tree cover. It also 
contributes to environmental awareness and citizen participation, thereby supporting India's 
climate commitments. 
 
(f): As informed by the State Forest Department of Gujarat, a Project Management Action 
Plan has been prepared under the JICA-assisted Project for Ecosystem Restoration in Gujarat 
(PERG Project) for undertaking native tree plantation and soil and moisture conservation 
measures in the Vav–Tharad area adjoining the Kutch region. In addition, the State Forest 

Department undertakes plantation of indigenous species and implements soil, moisture and 
water conservation measures as part of plantation activities in the Kutch region.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3512 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
INCREASING THE SALARY LIMIT FOR MEDICAL TREATMENT IN ESI 
HOSPITALS 
 
3512. ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has received any proposal for the increase in 
the salary limit from Rs. 21,000 to Rs. 30,000 for workers in the 
unorganized sector to avail medical treatment at Emp loyees' State 
Insurance (ESI) hospitals/dispensaries; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether the Government likely to consider to set up ESI dispensaries 
at Nedunkandam and Kumily in Idukki due to the presence of large 
number of workers especially in the plantation sector; and 
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The revision of wage ceiling for coverage under the 
Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Scheme is undertaken periodically from 
time to time. The last revision was done w.e.f. 01.01.2017, wherein the 
wage limit was raised from Rs. 15,000/ - per month to Rs. 21,000/ - per 
month (Rs. 25,000/- for Persons with disability). 
  The provisions of the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 
have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which 
came into force with effect from 21 st November 2025. As per the First 
Schedule to the Code, Chapter IV relating to the Employees' State 
Insurance Corporation (ESIC)  applies to every establishment employing 
ten or more persons, other than a seasonal factory. 
  At present, unorganised workers are not covered under the 
ESIC framework. However, Section 45 of the Code on Social Security, 
2020 empowers the Central Government to frame a scheme for extending 
ESIC benefits to unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.  
  Nedumkandam and Kumily in Idukki district do not fulfil the 
prescribed ESIC norms regarding the minimum Insured Persons (IP) 
population required for establishing an ESI Dispensary. Accordingly, there 
is no proposal at present  for setting up ESI dispensaries at these 
locations.

DEVELOPMENT OF COASTAL TOURISM IN AMALAPURAM 
 
3513. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of Initiatives undertaken to promote and develop coastal 
tourism in Amalapuram Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) the details of coastal tourism projects sanctioned, completed and 
ongoing during the last three years in the said Constituency; 
(c) the details of funds allocated, sanctioned, released and utilised for 
coastal tourism projects during the said period, year and project-wise; 
(d) nature of infrastructure created or upgraded under such initiatives, 
including beach development, eco -tourism facilities, cruise and boat 
tourism, connectivity and visitor amenities in the said Constituency; 
(e) the details of capacity -building and skill development programmes 
undertaken to support local communities, including youth, fishermen, 
women self -help groups and other stakeholders, for participation in 
coastal tourism activities in the said Constituency; and 
(f) whether any new proposals for coastal tourism development are under 
consideration in the said Constituency and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (f): Development and promotion of tourist destination and tourism 
products including coastal tourism is primarily done by the concerned State 
Government (SG)/UT Administration (UTA). However, Ministry of Tourism under 
its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan  (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development - CBDD- a sub scheme of 
SD2.0 and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD) etc. provides financial assistance for development of tourism 

infrastructure and experiences to the SGs/UTAs; on receipt of the project 
proposals from them, in synergy with the scheme guidelines, Government 
directions, availability of funds, inter-se priority etc. 
 
In addition, Government of India under its initiative  for ‘Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic 
Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ scheme, has also provided financial 
assistance in the year 2024 -25 to the States for development of tourism 
projects. 
 
Various schemes, programs, and initiatives of the Ministry have been 
actively addressing issues related to the tourism promotion and development, 
including coastal tourism. 
 
Sanctioning of new project under the above -mentioned schemes is a 
continuous process. 
 
The details of projects sanctioned by the Ministry under SD, SD2.0, CBDD, 
PRASHAD and SASCI schemes in the county including coastal tourism projects 
are annexed. 
 
This project sanctioned under the  above mentioned schemes covers 
various components as per project design and requirement.   
 
The Ministry encourages State Governments/ UT Administrations to 
engage with local communities including youth and women and ensure robust 
operation & management (O&M) of completed projects so as to increase 
footfall, generate local employment and enhance overall tourist satisfaction 
along with skill development. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Tourism conducts hospitality and tourism related 
short-term training certificate courses for skilling, up - skilling and re -skilling 
under its “Capacity Building for Service Providers (CBSP)” scheme through 
Government institutes and  empanelled private institutes including Indian 
Institute of Hotel Management, Food Craft Institutes, Indian Culinary Institute, 
etc. In the State of Andhra Pradesh, a total of 411 candidates have  been 
trained/certified from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26 under CBSP.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS

SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA 
 
PRIME MINISTER's INTERNSHIP SCHEME IN MADHYA PRADESH 
 
QUESTION 
 
No. 3514 Smt. Anita Nagarsingh Chouhan 
               
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the target fixed and achievements made so far under the Prime Minister's 
Internship Scheme to provide practical training to youth in industries and 
reputed companies across the country; 
(b)  the number of youth selected under the said scheme in the country as well as 
in Madhya Pradesh during the last two years along with the number of youth 
who have completed their internship and who secured permanent or 
contractual based employment; 
(c) whether the Government is contemplating running any special campaign to 
connect maximum youth with the scheme and increase the participation of 
local industries and establishments in Ratlam-Jhabua-Alirajpur Parliamentary 
Constituency of Madhya Pradesh which is a tribal-dominated and aspirational 
region; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof including the tentative timeline therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY 
OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a) & (b): Presently the Pilot Project of the PM Internship Scheme is under 
implementation. It is targeted to provide 1.25 lakh internship opportunities to the 

youth. Details of internship opportunities posted by the companies, number of youth 
who received internship offers, joined & completed internship in Round I, Round II 
and Round III of the PMIS Pilot Project across the country as well as in Madhya 
Pradesh is attached at Annexure. The process of selection and joining in Round III 
is ongoing. 
The PM Internship Scheme is designed to enhance industry-relevant skills, improve 
job readiness, and foster professional exposure through structured internships in 
India’s top-performing companies and institutions to create job ready, skilled work 
force. The scheme  is not designed to provide permanent or contractual based 
employment.  
(c) & (d): The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is actively working with various 
stakeholders such as state governments, central government ministries & 
departments, and industry associations for promotion and implementation of the 
scheme. 
The Government of Madhya Pradesh has undertaken a focused outreach campaign 
to maximize youth participation across the State, including in the districts of 
Ratlam, Jhabua and Alirajpur. The initiatives include spreading awareness through 
social media and institutional outreach, district -level monitoring by the District 
Collectors, mobilization through Government ITIs, and special registration drives. 
Further, as per the revised Guidelines of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme 
(PMIS) – Pilot Project, issued on 12.03.2026, companies nominated by the state 
government, as well as selected MSMEs through Sectoral Associations are also 
eligible to participate under the PMIS Pilot Project.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3515 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF TOURIST DESTINATIONS 
 
3515. SHRI ARVIND DHARMAPURI: 
          SHRI MAHESH KASHYAP: 
          SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether lesser-known spiritual, eco, rural and heritage destinations, 
including Nizamabad, Basar, Dharmapuri, Kondagattu and forest-based 
circuits of Telangana have been identified for promotion under any 
scheme for sustainable tourism projects; 
(b) the details of steps taken to diversify tourism, reduce pressure on 
overcrowded destinations and generate local employment; 
(c) whether the Government is implementing any specific scheme or 
project for the overall development of Chhattisgarh, especially Bastar 
Lok Sabha Constituency's Chitrakot Waterfall, Tirathgarh Waterfall, 
Kanger Valley National Park, Kutumsar Cave, Danteshwari Temple and 
other natural, cultural, and tribal tourist sites to promote tourism 
infrastructure, eco-tourism, homestay, local handicrafts and cultural 
tourism; 
(d) whether the Government has identified or proposes to support high -
potential but relatively lesser-explored tourism destinations in Andhra 
Pradesh, including Visakhapatnam, Araku – Lambasingi, Gandikota, 
Papikondalu, Ahobilam and the Buddhist heritage circuit for integrated 
tourism infrastructure and destination development; and 
(e) if so, the details of projects sanctioned, under implementation or 
proposed for such destinations along with the financial assistance 
provided and expected timelines? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM      (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 

 
(a) to (e): Development and promotion of tourism including those of lesser-
known destinations is primarily done by the concerned State Government 
(SG)/UT Administration (UTA). However, Ministry of Tourism under its 
various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh  Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) – an initiative 
under Swadesh Darshan and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) etc. provides financial assistance for 
development of tourism infrastructure and experiences in the country, to the 
SGs/UTAs, on receipt of the project proposals from them including proposal 
of development of lesser known destinations, in synergy with the scheme 
guidelines, Government directions, availability of funds, inter-se priority etc. 
 
Further, under ‘Scheme for Special Assistance to States/Union 
Territories for Capital Investment (SASCI) - Development of Iconic Tourist 
Centers to Global Scale’, Government of India has sanctioned 40 Projects in 
the country for Rs.3295.76 Crore during fin ancial year 202 4-25. The 
parameters formulated for examining the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) 
submitted by the States under this scheme covered connectivity to the site, 
existing tourism eco -system at site/destination, carrying capacity, 
availability of utility services, project impact and value envisaged which 
included expected increase in tourist footfall, increase tourist spend, new 
employment opportunities etc. Weightage was given to alternate 
destinations which address the issue of decongestion at major destination. 
 
To address challenges such as overcrowding in high -footfall 
destinations and to improve tourist experience, the Ministry of Tourism has 
sanctioned various interventions under the above-mentioned schemes such 
as Queue management complex, waiting halls, Widening of approach roads, 
CCTVs for tourist safety, Parking, Tourist Information Centre, last -mile 
connectivity, solid waste management systems, illumination, sanitation, 
amenities centres, interpretation facilities etc. 
 
Ministry of Tourism promotes tourism in a holistic manner including 
promotion of various tourism destinations and products of the country i.e. 
eco-tourism, homestay, local handicrafts and cultural tourism etc. through 
various medium including social media,  websites and participation in fairs 
and exhibitions etc. 
 

Details of the projects sanctioned under SD, SD2.0, CBDD, PRASHAD 
and SASCI schemes in the state of Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and 
Telangana is annexed. 
 
******

(a) the details of loans given to farmers since 2014 till 2025 –26 and the amount recovered 
during the same period, year-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(b) the details of farm loan waivers during the said period, year-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(c) the details of loans given to corporates since 2014 till 2025 –26 and the amount recovered 
during the same period, year-wise, State/UT-wise; 
(d) the details of corporate loan waivers/write -offs during the said period, year -wise and 
State/UT-wise; 
(e) whether the Government considers the proportion of loan waivers of farmers and corporates 
to be equitable, if so, the justification therefor and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(f) the steps taken by the Government to ensure balanced and fair trea tment in loan relief 
measures? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b) The year-wise, State/UT-wise details of agriculture credit disbursed from 2013-2014 
till 2025-26 is given at Annexure -I. However, the details of amount recovered thereon is not 
centrally maintained. Further, Union G overnment has not extended any farm loan waiver 
during the said period.  
 
(c) The year -wise details of loans given to corporates since 2014 till 2025 -26 is given at 
Annexure-II. However, State/UT-wise details of loan given and amount recovered thereon is  
not centrally maintained.  
 
(d) As reported by the Reserve Bank of India, the State/Union Territory (UT) - wise details 
regarding total loans waived off or written off in respect of corporates is not maintained by it. 
However, year-wise and category -wise details of loans written -off by Public Sector Banks, 
Private Sector Banks, Foreign Banks and Small Finance Banks, for domestic operations, for 
categories Large (Industries & Services) from 31.03.2015 to 31.03.2026, are at Annexure-III. 
 
(e) Debt write -off is an accounting procedure and does not provide any relief to the debtor 
(whether farmer or corporate). As per RBI - Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions 2025, 
issued for commercial banks, write -off (a major portion of which is due to 
technical/prudential/advances under collection) is an accounting procedure undertaken by a 
bank to adjust its balance sheets. Such write -off does not result in waiver of liabilities of 
borrowers and therefore, it does not benefit the borrower. The borrowers continue to be  liable 
for repayment and banks continue to pursue recovery actions initiated in these accounts. 
 

 
(f) To provide relief to borrowers in distress, Reserve Bank of India has issued Master Direction 
on Resolution of Stressed Assets, 2025 dated 28 November 2025 (updated as on 01 July 2026) 
which, inter -alia, provides lenders the discretion to undertake financial restructuring of 
borrowers under stress, based on their Board approved policies and regulatory guidelines.

ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TOURIST AMENITIES 
 
3517.  SHRI RAJU BISTA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of funds allocated, sanctioned and utilized for upgrading 
tourist amenities, view - points, pedestrian tracks and other tourist 
amenities in Darjeeling and Kalimpong districts during  the last three 
years; and 
(b) the details of total number of village clusters and rural pockets 
identified for development under the Vibrant Villages Programme in the 
border areas of the said districts?

and products, including tourist amenities, view -points, pedestrian tracks and 
other tourist amenities, is primarily undertaken by the concerned State 
Governments (SG)/Union Territory Administra tions (UTA). However, the 
Ministry of Tourism through its central sector schemes of 'Swadesh Darshan 
(SD)', 'Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)', 'Challenge Based Destination

and Spiritual , Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)' complements the

(DPRs), availability of funds, Government directions, inter-se priority etc. 
 
In addition, Government of India under its initiative  for ‘Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic 

Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ scheme, has also provided financial 
assistance in the year 2024 -25 to the States for development of tourism 
projects. 
 
Ministry of Home Affairs is implementing the Vibrant Villages

programme, 662 villages have been identified for priority development and

Crore, of which 316 projects have been completed. 
 
Further, Vibrant Village Programme is one of the four categories — along

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3518 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
RESPIRATORY TRACKING SYSTEM FOR WORKERS OF MINING 
SECTOR 
3518. SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
  SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
  SHRI RAJESH VERMA: 
  DR. D. PURANDESWARI: 
  SHRI ATUL GARG: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has operationalised the National 
Occupational Health Registry to track respiratory and long -term 
health metrics among mining workers and if so, the details thereof; 
 (b)the details of the non -intrusive wearable sensor systems deployed 
in May 2026 to track toxic gas exposures in real-time; 
 (c)the details of structural checks established within the central health 
portal to instantly alert regional medical units during high -risk 
environmental shifts; 
 (d)the details of criteria used to disburse targeted performance -linked 
health infrastructure grants to mining cooperatives managing 
localized medical check-up hubs; 
 (e)the details of measures taken by the Government to integrate the 
said worker health records with the central ESI database for 
seamless specialized hospital transfers; and 
 (f)the details of projected reduction in peak occupational health 
incidents following the nationwide deployment of the said proactive 
digital monitoring network? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Central Government has enacted the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020, which 
has come into force with effect from 21.11.2025 to regulate 
occupational safety, health and working conditions of the persons 
employed in m ining. The Central Government has also notified OSH & 
WC (Central) Rules 2026 on 08.05.2026.  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  The third schedule of the code specifies the list of twenty -
nine (29) notifiable diseases including Coal miners' pneumoconiosis, 
silicosis etc. 
  Rule 8 of the OSH&WC (Central) Rules mandates that the 
employer shall send a notice to the Inspector -cum-Facilitator or the 
Chief Inspector -cum-Facilitator whenever a worker contracts any 
disease specified in the Third Schedule to the Code. 
  Rule 109  of the OSH&WC (Central) Rules, 2026 also 
mandates that the employer of every mine shall arrange for the initial 
medical examination of every person seeking employment, as well as 
annual periodical medical examinations. In cases where the medical 
examining authority confirms suspected dust -related diseases, the 
employer shall also arrange for medical examinations at frequent 
intervals, including x -rays or both, as required. In case of worker 
affected, the employer shall be liable to pay compensation in 
accordance with the provisions of Code on Social Security, 2020. 
  The OSH&WC Code, 2020 mandates employers to provide 
training and supervision, safe and without risk workplace, maintain 
occupational safety and health standards, personal protective 
equipment (PPE), welfare facilities, emergency preparedness, first -aid, 
firefighting arrangements and other safety measures as prescribed. 
  The health record of workers registered with ESIC are 
maintained in Dhanwantri portal of ESIC.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3519 
                                         TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
SOP for Scientific Identification of threatened Species 
 
3519. SHRI MANISH TEWARI:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of the 159 plant and 173 animal species currently officially designated and notified 
as threatened under Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 across the identified 17 
States and 3 Union Territories, State-wise; 
(b) the targeted execution timeline, structural budgetary allocations and implementation 
guidelines provided in the new Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to assist State Biodiversity 
Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils in launching mandatory species recovery and 
conservation action plans; 
(c) the precise scientific validation criteria and field-assessment methodologies deployed by the 
Botanical Survey of India and the Zoological Survey of India to authenticate local field data and 
traditional ecological knowledge during the local identification process; and 
(d) the specific statutory enforcement mechanisms under the 2025 Benefit-Sharing Regulations 
that mandate differential financial obligations and benefit-sharing collections for biological 
resources derived exclusively from these newly notified threatened species? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): As per Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023), the 
Central Government, in consultation with the concerned State Government, may from time to 
time notify any species which is on the verge of extinction or likely to become extinct in the 
near future as a threatened species and prohibit or regulate collection thereof for any purpose 
and take appropriate steps to rehabilitate and preserve those species.  
 
So far, 159 plant and 174 animal species have been notified as threatened species under Section 
38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023), and the list of threatened species 
notified under Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023) across 
17 States and three Union Territories is published on the National Biodiversity Authority 
website www.nbaindia.org. 
 
As per the recently published Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) of the National Biodiversity 
Authority on 16.06.2026, the State Biodiversity Board or Union Territory Biodiversity 
Council, in association with the Botanical Survey of India, Zoological Survey of India, Forest 
Departments, scientific institutions, or any other organization, shall undertake a scientific 

assessment that shall include population trends, geographic range, habitat quality, habitat 
fragmentation, exploitation pressures, reproductive biology, ecological requirements, and 
extinction risk. The objective of the SOP is to establish a transparent, science-based, 
participatory framework for the identification, assessment, notification, conservation, 
rehabilitation, monitoring, and periodic review of threatened species under Section 38 of the 
Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended in 2023).  
 
In the SOP, there is no mention of execution timelines, structural budgetary allocations, or 
implementation guidelines to assist State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity 
Councils in launching mandatory species recovery and conservation action plans, as the Central 
Government, in consultation with the concerned State Government, may from time to time 
notify the threatened species under Section 38 of the Act.  
 
The Access and Benefit Sharing Regulations, 2025 under regulation 4 and 5 states that in case 
of biological resource having conservation value or high economic value such as red sanders, 
sandalwood, agarwood or any other items as decided by the Authority from time to time, and 
including threatened species notified under section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as 
amended in 2023), the benefit sharing shall not be less than five percent of the proceeds of the 
auction or sale amount or the purchase price, as the case may be, as determined by the Authority 
on case to case basis, as upfront payment.

          Dr. Shrikant Eknath Shinde:

(a) whether the Government has undertaken an assessment of the interaction 
between the data -related obligations proposed under the draft Digital 
Competition Bill, including those relating to consent, restrictions on 
intermixing of data and data portability and  the obligations under the Digital 
Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(c) whether any coordination mechanism, guidance or framework has emerged 
from the consultations held between the Competition Commission of India and 
the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology on the interface

(a) & (b): No, Sir. At present, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has

(c): The deliberations between Competition Commission of India (CCI) and the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

Irregularities in Appointments of Teachers in Delhi University 
 
†3521. Shri Murari Lal Meena: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of complaints received regarding fake research papers, fake publications, 
forged certificates or other documents related to the appointment of teachers in Delhi 
University and its affiliated colleges since the year 2020;  
 
(b) the number of cases out of the said complaints in which inquiry committees were 
constituted along with their present status;  
 
(c) the number of cases in which appointment were cancelled or other administrative and 
disciplinary actions were taken following the inquiry; and  
 
(d) the number of cases handed over to the police, Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or 
other investigative agencies along with the steps taken or being taken by the Government to 
prevent such irregularities in the future, including mandatory digital verification of research 
papers, publications and certificates? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): University of Delhi is a statutory autonomous organization established under Delhi 
University Act 1922 and governed by provisions of the Acts and Statutes, Ordinances, 
Regulations made thereunder. The University has informed that no case regarding fake 
research papers, fake publications, forged certificates or other documents related to the 
appointment of teachers has been reported in the departments of University of Delhi. 
However, two cases have been reported in Zakir Husain Delhi College (Evening) and Bharti 
College respectively. In case of Zakir Husain Delhi College (Evening), the matter is subjudice 
before Hon’ble High Court of Delhi. In case of Bharti College, complaint has been submitted 
to the SHO for registering FIR and the faculty was terminated after following the due 
administrative process by the Governing Body of the College on recommendation of Enquiry 
Committee.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
                  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
                 LOK SABHA 
                     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3522 
            TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Complaints regarding Karhi-Chandi Limestone Mines 
 
3522. SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that complaints regarding environmental irregularities, the Karhi 
reservoir and tribal land pertaining to the Karhi-Chandi Limestone Mines (Shree Cement), 
District Balodabazar, have been received by the Government during the last five years; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the response of the Government thereto; 
(c) whether the Government had issued directions on 12.09.2025 to the Mineral Resources 
Department, State Government of Chhattisgarh, and the Chhattisgarh Environment 
Conservation Board to investigate the said complaints, take necessary action and provide a 
report thereof to the Government and the complainant; 
(d) if so, the details of action taken reports received from the State Government so far in 
compliance with the said directions;  
(e) whether the final investigation or action has not been completed, if so, the reasons therefor; 
and 
(f) whether the Union Government is likely to fix a time limit for the time-bound resolution of 
this matter or ensure early action by the State Government and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (f): The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) received a 
Public Grievance bearing Registration No. MOEAF/E/2025/0003275 dated 02.09.2025 
regarding alleged encroachment on Karhi reservoir and tribal land in respect of the Karhi-
Chandi Limestone Mine of M/s Shree Cement Ltd., including allegations related to allotment 
of Khasra beyond the scope of the Letter of Intent. 
 
The grievance was forwarded by the Ministry to the Directorate of Geology and Mining 
(DGM), Government of Chhattisgarh and the Member Secretary, Chhattisgarh Environment 
Conservation Board (CECB) on 12.09.2025 for examination and appropriate action, as per the 
provisions of the applicable laws. 
 
As per the information received from the CECB and DGM, the Environmental Clearance (EC) 
was initially granted for a mining lease area of 242.127 ha on 15.05.2020 and subsequently 

 
 
amended on 29.10.2021, reducing the lease area to 225.719 ha by excluding 16.408 ha 
pertaining to the Karhi reservoir and rectifying the ambiguity relating to the land schedule in 
the Letter of Intent (LoI). Also, no instance has been reported of Government land pertaining 
to the Karhi Reservoir being claimed as private land. It has also been reported that there has 
been no encroachment upon the reservoir area, nor has the project proponent commenced any 
mining operations in the said area. It has been further informed that a number of joint 
inspections have been done by the officials of DGM and CECB on the similar complaints 
before the directions of MoEF&CC dated 12.09.2025 and the complaints were not found 
genuine. Further, a joint inspection was also carried out in the presence of the complainant on 
06.03.2026, during which ambient air quality, noise levels and groundwater samples from 
nearby villages were collected and analysed, and all monitored environmental parameters were 
found to be within the prescribed standards.

INTEGRATED CLAIM SETTLEMENT SYSTEM UNDER IEPFA

           Dr. Manna Lal Rawat: 
          Smt. Mahima Kumari Mewar:  
          Dr. Sanjay Jaiswal: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken measures to strengthen the claim 
settlement mechanism under the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority 
(IEPFA);  
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of claims received, approved and disposed of through the Integrated 
IEPFA Portal since its operationalisation;

processing and settlement timelines following the integration of MCA -21, National 
Securities Depository Limited/Central Depository Services (India) Limited 
(NSDL/CDSL) and Public Fin ancial Management System (PFMS), if so, the details 
thereof;  
(e) the number of grievances received and resolved through the dedicated IEPFA Call 
Centre since its operationalisation, including the average grievance resolution time; 
and  
(f) whether the Government proposes further reforms, including automation, digital 
verification, simplified documentation, enhanced investor awareness and technology-
enabled monitoring, to improve transparency, efficiency, accessibility and timely 
settlement of claims under the IEPFA framework and if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY OF 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(HARSH MALHOTRA)
