OIH 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3545 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Industrial Pollution in Ramganga River, Uttar Pradesh 
3545. MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any assessment has been conducted to evaluate industrial pollution affecting the 
Ramganga River in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether any investigation has been conducted into heavy metal contamination caused by metal 
processing industries; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action taken against the industrial units found responsible 
during the last five years; and  
(d) whether any river restoration programme has been prepared for the Moradabad stretch of the 
Ramganga River? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (d): Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) monitors water quality of aquatic resources in 
the country in association with the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control 
Committees (PCCs) at 4922 locations including 2265 locations on rivers under National Water 
Quality Monitoring Programme (NWMP), to regularly assess status of water quality of water 
resources to facilitate prevention and control of pollution in water bodies.  
 
Ramganga River is presently being monitored at three locations under NWMP, including one 
monitoring location each at Bijnor, Pauri Garhwal and Farrukhabad.The water quality data under 
NWMP is utilised for identification of Polluted River Stretches (PRS), the location / stretches of 
rivers that are not meeting the Primary Water Quality criterion for outdoor bathing for 
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) parameter (indicator of organic pollution) are identified as 
polluted location/ stretches. The PRS are classified under Priority Class I to V, Priority I being 
most polluted and Priority V least polluted.  
 
Under NWMP, in 2018, CPCB identified total 351 PRS including one PRS of Ramganga river 
from Muradabad to Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh under Priority class IV (BOD 6 mg/L – 10 mg/ L).  
The comprehensive action plans including plan for Industrial pollution control were prepared for 
bringing the water quality of polluted river stretches to the quality level fit for bathing purposes 
(i.e. BOD ˂ 3 mg/L). Progress of implementation of action plans is reviewed by the River 
Rejuvenation Committees (RRC) at State level and Central Monitoring Committee (CMC) 
constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Jal Shakti at Central Level. With 

concerted efforts, the total number of PRS in 2025 has been reduced to 296, which include one 
PRS of Ramganga river from Kalagarh to Bijnaur under Priority class IV. 
 
Further, CPCB organizes annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) operating in 
river Ganga and Yamuna main stem States having potential to discharge into river Ganga & its 
tributaries, by joint teams of officials from third party technical institutes and State Pollution 
Control Boards/ Pollution Control Committees (SPCBs/PCCs) since 2017. Inspection also 
includes the GPIs discharging into river Ramganga. The Online Continuous Effluent Monitoring 
Systems (OCEMS) are installed by Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) in the country as per 
directives issued by CPCB. Based on the alerts generated from OCEMS, CPCB also conduct 
surprise inspection of selected industries. 
As informed by CPCB, Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) in the Metal Processing sector located 
in Moradabad were inspected by joint team from third-party technical institutes and concerned 
SPCB. During 2021 and 2022, no Metal Processing units has been listed under GPI category in 
Moradabad District. However, 55, 51 and 23 Metal Processing units were found to be non-
compliant during inspections conducted in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Out of the total 129 
non-compliant units, Show Cause Notice has been issued to 124 units and 05 units have been 
closed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3546 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Preservation and Protection Measures for Rushikulya River Estuary 
 
3546. DR. PRADEEP KUMAR PANIGRAHY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of specific conservation and monitoring measures undertaken by the Government to 
protect the sensitive coastal eco-system of the Rushikulya River estuary, particularly for the mass 
nesting of Olive Ridley sea turtles; 
(b) the details of funds allocated and utilized under the Integrated Coastal Zone Management 
(ICZM) project in Odisha during the last three years; and 
(c) whether any technical studies have been conducted on the impact of coastal climate change along 
the Ganjam coast and if so, the details thereof along with the mitigation strategies adopted? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a)  Management and protection of wildlife including Olive Ridley turtles is carried out by the 
concerned States and Union Territories. During the Olive Ridley turtle nesting season, the Forest 
Departments, in coordination with relevant stakeholders, undertake various measures for the 
protection of turtles, which include seasonal restrictions on mechanised fishing in nearshore waters, 
patrolling, surveillance in coordination with the Indian Coast Guard and Fisheries Department, 
besides curtailing public access to nesting beaches to minimize disturbance. In addition, regular 
monitoring of nesting activity, hatchling emergence and turtle strandings are also undertaken, along 
with awareness generation and community participation programmes. 
The Zoological Survey of India and Wildlife Institute of India have undertaken scientific studies, 
including flipper tagging and satellite telemetry, to assess turtle movement ecology and habitat use, 
thereby supporting scientific conservation and management of Olive Ridley turtles. 
(b) The Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) Project implemented in the State of Odisha 
ended in 2020. 
 
(c) The Ministry has not undertaken any specific study on the impact of coastal climate change 
along the Ganjam coast.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3547 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
  
LOW EMPLOYMENT RATE UNDER PMKVY 
  
†3547. SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
            SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA: 
            SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
            SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state:- 
  
(a) the main reasons for 22 lakh youth dropping out midway from their training under 
the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) between the years 2015 and 2022; 
  
(b) whether out of 1.10 crore certified youth, only 23 lakh could secure verified placements, 
and the reasons for 87 lakh youth not getting employment even after receiving training; 
  
(c) the reasons for the extremely low employment rate of about 21 percent, along with the 
reasons for the failure of the massive budgetary amount spent on these 87 lakh youth; 
  
(d) the fundamental changes the Government proposes to bring into its policy to 
ensure hundred percent employment as per industry demands in the future, rather than 
merely distributing paper certified to the youth including its impact on Jaunpur Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
  
(e) whether the Government is considering to develop a more effective placement system 
for youth by linking skill training to employment as per industry demand in the country, including 
the Etah-Kasganj Lok Sabha Constituency; 
  
(f) whether the Government proposes to make policy improvements to strengthen skill 
training in accordance with the demand of industries, mandatory placement, apprenticeship and 
monitoring of employment after training and if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(g) the assessment made by the Government regarding the low employment rate under the 
said scheme and the accountability fixed to ensure the effectiveness of public funds spent on 
training?  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)       Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been successfully 
implementing its flagship scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015 
to impart skill development training through Short -Term Training (STT) and up -skilling and re-
skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country. The objective 
is to enhance the employability of youth by equipping them with industry-relevant skills. 
  

Under PMKVY, a real-time dashboard has been developed on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) 
to monitor key training indicators, including enrolment, attendance, training progress, and 
dropouts. According to SIDH data, a total of 5,22,538 candidates were re ported as dropouts 
under PMKVY during FY 2015 –16 to FY 2021 –22. Candidate dropouts occur due to various 
reasons such as academic examinations, seasonal employment opportunities, early placement 
offers, migration, and personal circumstances.  
  
(b)&(c)     Under PMKVY scheme, placements were tracked in the Short -Term Training (STT) 
component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, 
implemented from FY 2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22. In these versions of PMKVY, out of 56.89 lakh 
candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.3 lakh candidates have been reported placed 
which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%.  
 
Further, MSDE’s flagship scheme PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across 
several states. As per the study, about 94% of the employers surveyed reported they would hire 
more candidates trained under PMKVY. Further, 52% of the candidates who were placed in full 
time/part time employment and oriented under the RPL component received higher salary or felt 
that they will get higher salary compared to their un-certified peers. 
 
A third-party impact evaluation of PMKVY was also conducted by the Indian Institute of Public 
Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received 
placement in their desired skill sector. 
  
(d), (e)&(f)  The Government has undertaken various measures to strengthen the linkage 
between skill development and employment opportunities under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). Under PMKVY 4.0, training is being imparted in industry -relevant and 
future-ready job roles developed in consultation with industry -led bodies and aligned to the 
requirements of emerging sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Mec hatronics, 
Drone Technology and other Industry 4.0 domains. 
 
To ensure better alignment of training with labour market requirements, District Skill 
Development Plans (DSDPs) are prepared by District Skill Committees (DSCs) to identify local 
skill gaps and employment opportunities. Training programmes under PMKVY are  planned 
keeping in view industry demand and local economic potential. The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) 
provides an integrated digital platform for candidate registration, training management, job 
opportunities and employer connect, thereby facilitating placement of trained candidates. In 
addition, Kaushal Melas and other p lacement-linked initiatives are organised periodically to 
connect skilled candidates with prospective employers. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through the National 
Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), facilitates apprenticeship training in establishments 
across the country, enabling candidates to acquire practical workplac e experience and 
improving their employability. The Government also monitors key training outcomes, including 
certification and placement-related indicators, through technology-enabled systems and periodic 
reviews. 
 
Under PMKVY 4.0, as on 30.06.2026, a total of 8,012 candidates have been trained/oriented in 
Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituency and 10,606 candidates have been trained/oriented in Etah -
Kasganj Lok Sabha Constituency. 
  
(g) MSDE conducts periodic independent evaluations of PMKVY to ensure quality and 
accountability. More recently, an independent third -party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 
has been conducted by Arun Jaitley  National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an 
autonomous institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India, across the country. As per 
the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for 
STT candidat es. The combined share of employed and self -employed STT respondents 

increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 
percentage point increase. Income-related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% 
of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates reporting an increase in incom e following 
training and certification.  
  
The Government has undertaken comprehensive corrective measures under PMKVY 4.0, 
including Aadhaar -based e -KYC, face authentication and geo -tagged attendance, QR -coded 
digital certificates, real -time dashboards on the Skill India Digital Hub, strengthened assessor 
and training centre accreditation through NCVET, independent monitoring via Kaushal 
Samiksha Kendra, revised monitoring guidelines with clear KPIs, and a robust penalty and 
recovery framework. Disciplinary actions, including suspension, blacklisting, recovery of funds, 
and other stringent measures, have been taken wherever non -compliance was esta blished, 
thereby institutionalising stronger accountability, verification, and oversight mechanisms under 
the scheme.

3548. SHRI KALI CHARAN SINGH: 
  
            Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government proposes to redesign and update Pradhan Mantri Kaushal 
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) courses to meet the skill requirements of emerging sectors such as 
Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, green energy, electric vehicles,  drones, 
cybersecurity, robotics and advanced manufacturing and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of post -
certification employment, job retention and placement outcomes of candidates trained under 
PMKVY and if so, the details and findings thereof; 
  
(c) the number of candidates trained, certified and secured employment under the PMKVY 
during the last three years and the current year, State/UT-wise, year and sector-wise; 
  
(d) the details of funds allocated, released and utilized under PMKVY during the last three 
years and the current year, year-wise and State/UT-wise; and 
  
(e) the steps taken to strengthen industry partnerships, apprenticeships, on-the-job training 
and placement linkages to improve employment opportunities and long -term employability 
of PMKVY-certified candidates? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been implementing its 
flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting 
skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling 
through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society. Under PMKVY 
4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022 -23, the focus is on imparting training in 
emerging and new-age courses such as Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, 
green energy, electric vehicles, drones, cybersecurity, robotics, etc., as per the industry 
requirement. To meet emerging technology demands, 600+ new-age and futuristic courses 
have been introduced. As on 30.06.2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in 
new-age and futuristic job roles under PMKVY 4.0 across the country. 
  
(b) & (c) Under PMKVY scheme, placements were tracked in the Short-Term Training (STT) 
component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 

3.0, implemented from FY 2015-16 to FY 2021-22. In these versions of PMKVY , out of 56.89 
lakh candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.37 lakh candidates were reported placed 
which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is u nder 
implementation since FY 2022 -23, the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose 
their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through On-Job Training 
(OJT) embedded industry relevant skill courses. 
  
PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across several states. As per the 
study, about 94% of the employers surveyed reported they would hire more candidates 
trained under PMKVY. Further, 52% of the candidates who were placed in full time/part-time 
employment and oriented under the RPL component received higher salary or felt that they 
will get higher salary compared to their un -certified peers. Also, a third -party impact 
evaluation of PMKVY 2.0 (2016 -20) was also conducted by the Indian Institute  of Public 
Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received 
placement in their desired skill sector. 
  
Further, a third -party evaluation of PMKVY 4.0 conducted by the Arun Jaitley National 
Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) in 2025 observed that PMKVY training has led 
to a measurable improvement in employment outcomes for Short -Term Training (STT) 
candidates, with the combined share of employed and self -employed respondents 
increasing from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% post-training, reflecting a significant rise of 
18.8 % points. Moreover, 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates reported 
an increase in income following PMKVY training and certification. 
  
Year and State/UT-wise number of candidates trained and certified under the PMKVY during 
the last three years and the current year (up to 30.06.2026) are given at Annexure I and 
Sector-wise details are given at Annexure II. 
  
(d)       PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and there is no provision of State-wise fund 
allocation. The Year -wise details of funds allocated and released for implementation of

(e)       Under PMKVY , industries play a vital role in imparting quality skilling in the country. 
The training has been standardized through the National Skills Qualification Framework 
(NSQF), aligning courses with industry needs and national priorities. Industry-led Sector Skill 
Councils (SSCs) engage with industries to identify skill gaps, develop curriculum, define 
competency standards, and oversee training, assessment, and certification in alignment 
with NSQF. A major reform is the integration of On-the-Job Training (OJT) through industries, 
ensuring real-world industry exposure. Moreover, more than fifteen industries have been 
designated as Awarding Bodies (ABs) to develop job roles aligned with industry needs such 
as HCL Technologies, IBM, Bajaj Finserv, Microsoft, etc. In collaboration with industries, 

Kaushal Mahotsavs are organized to provide employment opportunities to the skilled 
candidates. Additionally, various industries have been onboarded under the Scheme to 
deliver skill training across sectors. 
  
Additionally, the Ministry has launched the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a unified digital 
platform that integrates the skilling, education, employment and entrepreneurship 
ecosystems to provide lifelong access to a wide range of services. Details of tr ained 
candidates are available on the platform, enabling potential employers to identify and 
connect with suitably skilled candidates. SIDH also facilitates access to employment and 
apprenticeship opportunities by connecting candidates with prospective emp loyers and 
establishments.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

Status of Implementation and Utilisation of the ONOS Scheme 
 
3549. Shri Abhishek Banerjee: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of institutions eligible, onboarded and actively using the One Nation One 
Subscription (ONOS) platform, State-wise and institution-category-wise; 
(b) the details of the number of registered users, active users, logins, full-text downloads and failed 
access attempts recorded under ONOS, institution-wise and publisher-wise; 
(c) the details of the amount paid or committed to publishers under the ONOS initiative, publisher-
wise and year-wise; 
(d) the number of eligible institutions that have not been onboarded under ONOS, as well as the 
number of onboarded institutions that have recorded no usage along with the reasons therefor; 
and 
(e) whether the Government has conducted any audit to assess duplication with pre-existing 
institutional subscriptions, under-utilisation, access denial or disparities in usage between 
Central institutions and State universities under ONOS and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) & (b): The One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme was launched in January 2025 
for a period of three years. The scheme envisages country-wide access to scholarly research 
articles and journal publications to all Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) of Central 
government, HEIs of State Government and Research & Development (R&D) Institutions of 
Central government. Details of institutions onboarded, registered users, full-text downloads 
state-wise and institution-category-wise and publisher-wise full-text downloads is available at 
https://www.onos.gov.in/   
(c): The details of the amount paid to publishers under ONOS, publisher-wise and year-wise is 
given at Annexure. 

(d): All Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) of Central government, HEIs of State 
Government and Research & Development (R&D) Institutions of Central government are 
eligible to access ONOS. The onboarding of these institutions is an ongoing process. As of 
now, 6,215 eligible institutions have successfully been onboarded under ONOS. To address 
issues such as dela in onboarding and lower usage, the Government of India, through the 
Information and Library Network Centre (INFLIBNET), has launched several initiatives to 
promote awareness and enhance utilisation of the scheme nationwide. These include 
conducting special lectures and organising webinars with nodal officers at the institutional 
level. In addition, offline awareness sessions have been delivered in collaboration with 
universities to reach institutions with limited digital access. To provide continuous support, 
INFLIBNET also regularly uploads Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to resolve queries and 
facilitate smoother adoption of ONOS. 
(e): The ONOS Scheme has integrated earlier initiatives of various Ministries and Departments, 
which previously subscribed to library consortia individually to provide access to research 
publications. This consolidation was undertaken to eliminate duplication of expenses and 
streamline access under a single comprehensive scheme. Access to ONOS is granted to eligible 
institutions possessing a unique AISHE code. The scheme ensures equitable access, with no 
issues of under-utilisation, denial, or disparities in usage.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3550 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
STRENGTHENING YOUTH EMPLOYMENT AND WORKFORCE 
PARTICIPATION 
 
3550.      SHRI M MALLESH BABU: 
   
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has considered the findings of the Youth 
Well-being Index 2025 highlighting that nearly 23 per cent of the 
youth population below 35 years in Karnataka is outside 
employment, education and skill training and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) the details of measures taken by the Government to strengthen 
employment opportunities, career guidance, labour market 
information and workforce participation for the youth of Kolar 
district; 
(c) the details of employment services, job fairs, National Career 
Service (NCS) centres, Model Career Centres and employment-linked 
initiatives supported by the Government in Kolar; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the employment profile, 
youth unemployment, migration for employment, women's workforce 
participation and demand for skilled manpower in the said district 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of steps taken by the Government to promote local 
employment generation, industry linkages, placement support and 
sustainable livelihood opportunities for the youth of the said 
district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017–18.  
 
 

 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated percentage of 
persons not in employment, education or training (NEET) on usual status 
was 17.1% for persons of age 15 -24 years, 20.8% for persons of age 15 -
29 years and 23.2% for persons of age 30 -59 during the year 2025 in the 
State of Karnataka. 
 
Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating 
employment on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
increased from 53.7% in 2022 to 58.0% in 2025 and the estimated 
Unemployment Rate (UR) on usual status for persons of age 15 years and 
above has decreased from 2.7% in 2022 to 2.3% in 2025 in the State of 
Karnataka. 
 
Also, the estimated UR for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased 
from 9.3% in 2022 to 8.6% in 2025 and the estimated Labour Force 
Participation Rate (LFPR) on usual status for females of age 15 years 
and above has increased from 33.9% in 2022 to 39.8% in 2025 in the 
State of Karnataka. 
 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, 
is running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information 
on skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in]. Government has approved 407 Model 
Career Centres across the country including 14 in the State of Karnataka 
and more than 67474 job fairs (of which 2643 in the State of Karnataka) 
have been organised in the country till 15.07.2026.  
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country 
(including the Kolar district in the State of Karnataka). The details of 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes being 
implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes  
 
 
 

 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission 
(SIM) to deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive 
network of skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. 
under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims 
at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry 
relevant skills. 
 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 
01.07.2020 for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government 
support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on 
Udyam Registration Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), 
providing employment to over 39 crore people across the country. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Also, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rozgar Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability 
and social security across all sectors, with special focus on the 
manufacturing sector. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore 
aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the 
country, over a period of 2 years.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
PROMOTION OF INDIAN CLASSICAL DANCES AMONGST STUDENTS 
 
†3551.  SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has issued any directions to include various forms of Indian 
classical dances in the school curriculum in the country, especially in Madhya Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c)  whether the Government has started any scholarship for meritorious students of schools in 
Indian classical dances; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e)  the details of funds utilized by the Government for promoting Indian classical dances 
among school students during the last five years, year-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
(a)&(b) The Government promotes the inclusion of Indian classical dances in school education 
in alignment with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which 
emphasizes art-integrated, experiential and multidisciplinary learning. The Centre for 
Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), an autonomous organization under the 
Ministry of Culture, conducts training programmes for teachers and students of 
Government and Government-aided schools incorporating Indian classical and folk-
dance traditions. In Madhya Pradesh, these programmes include dance forms such as 
Kathak, Rai, Matki, Karma and Grida. CCRT also has a Regional Centre at Damoh 
(Madhya Pradesh) for promoting local and regional art forms. 
  
Further, the Sangeet Natak Akademi organizes the Kala Dharohar series comprising 
lectures, workshops and performances to promote Indian performing arts among school 
children. 
  
(c)&(d) The Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) implements the Cultural Talent 
Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS) for meritorious students in the age group of 10-14 
years studying in recognized schools and children belonging to families practicing 
traditional performing arts. The Scheme provides specialized training in Indian classical 
dance and other cultural disciplines. Each scholarship holder receives ₹3,600 per annum 

along with reimbursement of tuition fees paid to the Guru/Teacher up to ₹9,000 per 
annum, subject to the Scheme guidelines. The scholarship is initially awarded for two 
years and is renewable based on satisfactory progress. 
  
Under the CCRT Cultural Talent Search Scholarship (CTSS) Scheme, the number of 
scholarships awarded in Indian Classical Dance during the last five years across the 
country is as follows:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3552 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Plantation under CAMPA in Uttarakhand 
 
3552. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total areas under Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority 
(CAMPA) plantation being planned by the Forest Department in Uttarakhand; 
(b) the  details of land category on which CAMPA plantations are being planned including the plant species 
planned for plantation; 
(c) whether the Annual Plan of Operations (APO) for implementation of CAMPA projects requires 
compliance with Forest Rights Act (FRA) as one of the stipulated conditions; and  
(d) if so, the details of process of consent undertaken, compliance of Forest Rights Act (FRA) and 
engagement of communities like Van Gujjars during the implementation of CAMPA projects? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH)  
 
(a) and (b): As per information received from the State Government of Uttarakhand, during the year 
2026-27, an area of 800 ha of land is being taken up for plantation. 
 
The land for raising compensatory afforestation (CA) is identified in accordance with the provisions of 
the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023, which provides that compensatory afforestation 
shall be undertaken over non-forest land or degraded forest land. Accordingly, compensatory 
afforestation is carried out on land identified and approved as part of the approval granted by the Central 
Government under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and in accordance with 
the provisions of the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, and the Rules and guidelines made 
thereunder. The Government of Uttarakhand has informed that both non-forest land and degraded forest 
land are being identified for raising compensatory afforestation using indigenous tree species. These 
plantations comprise a mix of timber, fuelwood, fodder, fruit-bearing, medicinal and other locally 
suitable species. 
 
(c) and (d): The Annual Plan of Operations (APO) for implementation of activities under the 
Compensatory Afforestation Fund is prepared and implemented in accordance with the Compensatory 
Afforestation Fund Rules, 2018. As per rule 5 of the said Rules, activities undertaken on forest land are 
carried out in consultation with the concerned Gram Sabha or Village Forest Management Committee, 
as the case may be, and in consonance with the provisions of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional 

Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, and the guidelines issued thereunder, 
wherever applicable, by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3553 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
EMPLOYER AND EMPLOYEE FACILITATION FRAMEWORK UNDER ELI 
SCHEME 
3553. SHRI P C MOHAN: 
  DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
  SHRI DULU MAHATO: 
  SHRI RAMESH AWASTHI: 
  SHRI JASHUBHAI BHILUBHAI RATHVA: 
  SHRI KHAGEN MURMU: 
  SHRI NABA CHARAN MAJHI: 
  DR. SANJAY JAISWAL: 
  SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
  SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI: 
  SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has undertaken any review of the 
implementation and effectiveness of the Employment Linked Incentive 
(ELI) Scheme and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)the details of progress achieved in onboard ing eligible establishments 
and beneficiaries along with number of employers and employees 
registered under the said scheme in the country, gender and State/UT -
wise, including Maharashtra; 
(c)whether any measures has taken by the Government to strengthen 
digital verification, claim processing and coordination with employers 
for effective implementation of the said scheme and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d)the details of the number of jobs generated under the said scheme so 
far, sector and State/UT-wise; 
(e)the manner in which the scheme is expected to promote formal 
employment generation and improve workforce participation across the 
country; and 
(f)the details of measures being taken by the Government to ensure greater 
participation of Mic ro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to 
improve formal employment generation and  enhance awareness of the 
Scheme among eligible employers and job seekers? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Union Cabinet, on 1 July 2025, approved the Employment 
Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled  the  Pradhan  Mantri  Viksit  Bharat 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment generation, enhance 
employability, and strengthen social security across all sectors including 
MSMEs, with a particular focus on the manufacturing sector. The scheme 
has a registration period of two years from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 and 
a budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 Crore for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 2031-
32. 
  The scheme comprises two parts, i.e. Part A and Part B, and 
focuses on providing support to both employees and employers by way of 
incentives. 
   Under Part A of the scheme, the first -time employees of both 
existing and new establishments shall be eligibl e for an incentive 
equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, subject to a maximum of ₹15,000. 
This incentive will be payable in two instalments during the first year of 
employment. The first instalment, up to ₹7,500, shall be disbursed after 
completion of six mo nths of continuous employment. Eligibility for the 
second instalment shall arise after completion of twelve months of 
employment and successful completion of the prescribed Financial 
Literacy Programme. This second instalment shall be credited to an 
appropriate savings instrument/savings account for a specified period.  
   Part B incentivizes employers by providing up to ₹3,000 per 
month for each additional employment sustained for at least 6 months for 
two years , with extended benefits for another two year s for the 
manufacturing sector.  
   The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 Crore 
jobs all across the country, over a period of 2 years. The scheme provides 
for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible first -time employees under Part A. 
Incentive for the creation of approximately 2.59 crore additional jobs to 
employers is provided for under Part B of the scheme. 
  Comprehensive Scheme Guidelines, outlining the eligibility 
criteria for incentives to both employees and employers, have been 
issued. The scheme and its provisions have been widely disseminated 
through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme -related processes and for real -time 
monitoring of beneficiaries and sector-wise progress. 
  For effective implementation of the scheme, a robust 
monitoring framework has been instituted. A steering Committee with 
representation from various labour -intensive and related 
Ministries/Department and an internal Executive Committee have been 
constituted to ensure effective monitoring of the scheme.  
Contd..3/- 
 
 

:: 3 :: 
  The PMVBRY is a demand -driven scheme. Since the 
implementation of the scheme, an incentive amount of ₹744.58 crore has 
been disbursed t o 13.18 lakh first -time employees under Part A, while 
₹2,068.84 crore has been disbursed to 67,369 beneficiary establishments 
under Part B of the scheme, up to June 2026, across the country. The 
incentive is payable after 6 months of sustained employment. However, 
since the implementation of the Scheme, a total of 99,92,924 first -time 
employees have been enrolled under Part A, while 5,50,972 
establishments have been registered under Part B across the country. The 
state-wise details of registrations, including the State of Maharashtra, are 
provided in Annexure-I. 
  The incentives to employees are disbursed through the 
Aadhaar Bridge Payment System (ABPS) under the Direct Benefit Transfer 
(DBT) framework to their Aadhaar -seeded bank accounts, after due 
verification, including Aadhaar authentication and validation of Aadhaar -
bank account linkage. The incentives to establishments are disbursed 
through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to their PAN -linked bank accounts 
after due verification of the establishment's credentials.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3554 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Protection and Monitoring of Saplings 
 
3554. SHRI AJENDRA SINGH LODHI:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
 (a) whether the Government is aware that despite large-scale tree plantation drives in various 
States, the expected increase in forest cover is not being achieved due to tree felling and 
inadequate protection of saplings; 
(b) if so, the details of survival rate of saplings planted across the country during the last three 
years, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to implement any new action plan for the protection and 
monitoring of saplings as well as for controlling illegal felling to ensure the effectiveness 
of tree plantation drives; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): The Government accords high priority to the conservation, protection, restoration and 
enhancement of forests and tree cover in the country, in accordance with the applicable legal 
and policy framework. Increase in forest and tree cover is a gradual ecological process 
influenced by several factors, including local climatic and edaphic conditions, species 
characteristics, genetic potential, silvicultural practices, protection from biotic and abiotic 
disturbances, and the age and growth stage of plantations. The outcomes of these afforestation 
and restoration interventions become evident gradually over time. As per the India State of 
Forest Report 2023, the total forest and tree cover of the country has increased by 1445.81 km2 
as compared to the last assessment of 2021. 
 
Further, conservation of natural forests and restoration of degraded forest landscapes are 
undertaken through assisted natural regeneration, artificial regeneration, Compensatory 
Afforestation under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 and the 
Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, the Green India Mission, Nagar Van Yojana, 
MISHTI and other afforestation and restoration programmes. The approved operational 
guidelines of these programmes provide for site-specific species selection, plantation 
maintenance, protection measures during the prescribed maintenance period and periodic 
monitoring by the implementing agencies. 
 
Protection of forests against illegal felling and other forest offences is primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
Action in this regard is taken by States/UTs under the provisions of the applicable forest and 
other relevant laws. Similarly the survival of plantations is monitored by the respective 
implementing agencies and State Governments as part of scheme implementation and project 

monitoring. The State-wise database on the survival rate of saplings across all afforestation 
programmes is not maintained centrally by the Ministry.

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Youth Affairs

MY Bharat Platform 
 
3555. DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Government has launched new initiatives under the 
MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) platform, including the 'Viksit Bharat 
Yuva Connect Programme', to promote youth participation , nation -
building and awareness against drug abuse among students and 
young citizens; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the number of youth 
registered and participating, State/UT -wise, particularly from rural, 
tribal and aspirational districts; 
(c) whether the Government has formulated any plan to strengthen 
youth engagement through educational institutions, Nehru Yuva 
Kendras (NYKs), National Service Scheme (NSS) units and sports 
organisations by integrating skill development, volunteerism and 
community service; and 
(d) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to ensure 
equitable participation of youth from remote and Left Wing 
Extremism-affected districts in such programmes along with the 
funds allocated and utilised during the last three years and the 
current year? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
(a) The Government has launched several initiatives under the MY 
Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) platform to promote youth participation 

Page 2 of 4 
 
in nation -building, volunteerism, leadership development, civic 
engagement and social awareness.  
The Viksit Bharat Yuva Connect Programme is an initiative that 
engages youth in universities, colleges, and institutions through 
interactive sessions, discuss ions, and activities aligned with the 
vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. A total of 1 75 such programs have 
been conducted till July -2026 in 1 75 universities /institutions 
nationwide engaging 34,500 students. 
The Ministry, through MY Bharat, is implementing Nasha Mukt Yuva 
for Viksit Bharat as a nationwide youth movement towards a Drug -
Free India. The campaign commenced with the Youth Spiritual 
Summit held at Varanasi during 18 –20 July 2025, where over 550 
youth representing more than 125 spiritual organisati ons 
participated, culminating in the adoption of the Kashi Sankalp. The 
campaign subsequently expanded through Nationwide Youth 
Spiritual Events at over 2,000 locations (September 2025), the 
North-East Regional Chintan Shivir at IIM Shillong (May 2026 ). A 
nationwide ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ is 
launched on 2 nd August in which events were organized at more 
than 28,000 location with participation of more than 1 crore youth 
by various spiritual organization, community-based organization, MY 
Bharat and MY Bharat – NSS.  
(b) As on date, more than 2. 50 crore youth have registered on the 
MY Bharat platform. State/UT-wise details of registered youth are at

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3556 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 10, 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
Insurance Claim Repudiation and Consumer Protection 
 
3556. SHRI SRIBHARAT MATHUKUMILLI: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the Government is aware of instances of insurance claims being rejected or delayed 
on grounds arising from ambiguous or unclear policy terms, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) The number and value of insurance claims repudiated in the country during each of the last 
five years, along with the number subsequently overturned by the Insurance Ombudsman, 
consumer forum or courts, State-wise particularly in Andhra Pradesh, including Visakhapatnam; 
(c) Whether the Government has assessed the financial impact of unjustified claim repudiation 
on policyholders and families, if so, the details thereof, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and 
Visakhapatnam; and 
(d) The steps being taken by the government to ensure clear and standardised policy language, 
prevent arbitrary claim repudiation, strengthen accountability of insurers, and provide timely 
grievance redressal to affected policyholders? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) monitors policyholder 
grievances relating to repudiation of insurance claims and delay in settlement through analysis 
of regulatory returns submitted by insurers, supervisory reviews and complaints registered on the 
Bima Bharosa Portal. Based on such analysis, IRDAI undertakes appropriate regulatory, 
supervisory and follow-up measures, wherever necessary.   
Rejection or delay generally arise due to several factors, including  non-disclosure or 
misrepresentation of material facts, incomplete, inaccurate or inconsistent documentation, 
exhaustion of the sum insured, non-fulfilment of policy conditions, applicability of waiting period, 
fraud investigations, delays in completion of loss assessment surveys, judicial proceedings in the 
case of Motor Third Party claims, and delay in submission of records or other information by 
hospitals, garages and other entities. 
(b): The data on insurance claims repudiated is maintained by IRDAI at the aggregate level and 
is not maintained State-wise or city-wise. A detail containing data of claims repudiated during last 
5 years is at Annexure-I.  The state-wise data on Reason for Grievance referred to Insurance 
Ombudsman, including any partial or t otal repudiation of claims by an insurer, as received from 
Council of Insurance Ombudsman Office is attached as Annexure-II.  

 
 
 
(c) and (d):  IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024 and t he IRDAI (Protection of 
Policyholders' Interests, Operations and A llied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024  require 
Insurers to use clear, simple and policyholder-friendly language in policy documents, disclose all 
key features, benefits, exclusions and terms through prospectuses, provide proposal forms and 
policy documents in simple language (including scheduled languages, wherever feasible), offer 
a 30-days free-look period, publish a Citizens' Charter specifying service standards, timelines 
and grievance redressal mechanisms, ensure fair and timely settlement of cla ims. Health 
insurance claims can not be repudiated without approval of the Product Management Committee 
(PMC) or Claims Review Committee (CRC) and where delay occurs in settlement of claim, the 
insurer is required to pay penal interest. If the customer is not satisfied with the service of the 
insurer they may approach Insurance Ombudsman for redressal.  Any delay in honouring the 
award of the Insurance Ombudsman attracts a penalty of ₹5,000 per day.  
In addition, the complaints can also be registered on Centralised Public Grievance Redress and 
Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal of the Government of India, which is monitored regularly 
from the appropriate level in Department of Financial Services (DFS) for redressal of grievances 
registered.  
These measures are applicable uniformly across the country, including Andhra Pradesh.

MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3557 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST 2026/SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
UPI-Favara Integration Scheme 
 
3557. SHRI ANTO ANTONY: 
            
 
 
           Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) -Favara Integration Scheme signed  between 
India and the Maldives, including its salient features; 
(b) the present status of the project and the time by which it is expected to become fully  operational; 
and 
(c) whether the scheme is likely to enable Indian nationals working in the Maldives to transfer  their 
salaries to India through it and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c) The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has informed that an agreement was signed in July 2025 between 
NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) to integrate 
India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with the Maldives’ fast payment system, Favara. Such integration 
facilitates real-time cross-border person-to-person (P2P) remittances between the two countries. Further, it 
provides instant credit to beneficiaries’ accounts, 24x7 availability, and real -time payee validation. The 
facility became operational on July 30, 2026 for remittances from the Maldives to India and enables Indian 
nationals working in the Maldives to transfer money to India subject to applicable transaction limits and 
regulations.

CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY INVESTMENT NORMS 
Question 
 
3559. Shri Tanuj Punia: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has introduced major amendments to the Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR) investment norms to allow companies to directly invest their CSR 
funds, in Non-Profit Organisations (NPOs) listed on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the primary objective behind this move; 
 
(c) whether investments made by companies under these revised norms are likely to 
be treated as valid CSR expenditure under Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the extent to 
which this policy intervention is likely to boost the inflow of institutional capital into 
the social sector and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS  AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                      [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
 
(a) to (c): Yes Sir. The Ministry has vide notification dated 27.05.2026 widened the 
ambit of Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’)  by introduction of new item 
no. (xiii) namely “Subscription to zero coupon zero principal instruments on Social 
Stock Exchange." As per the said amendment, the CSR mandated company shall not 
subscribe to ZCZP instrument for more than ten percent of the total CSR expenditure 
for that financial year. This amendment is aimed at providing significant ease of 
compliance to the companies and will also help Not for Profit Organisations to raise 
funding for public welfare projects in a transparent and regulated manner. 
 
(d) No such assessment has been conducted by the Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3560 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Illegal Tree Felling and Forest Conservation 
 
3560. DR. AMAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing incidents of illegal tree felling in various 
parts of the country; 
(b) the details of  number of cases of illegal tree felling reported during the last five years, 
State/UT-wise, along with the action taken against the offenders; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of such illegal felling on forest cover, 
biodiversity and climate resilience and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of measures taken by the Government to strengthen monitoring, surveillance, and 
enforcement to prevent illegal tree felling, including the use of technology; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to introduce any new schemes or policy measures to 
enhance afforestation, community participation and protection of forests and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): Instances of illegal tree felling are reported from time to time from different parts of 
the country. The protection and management of forest and tree resources are primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, which 
take appropriate action under the provisions of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, Van (Sanrakshan 
Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and the respective State Forest Acts, Tree Preservation 
Acts and Rules. The instances regarding the illegal felling of trees as and when detected are 
booked by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations under the relevant Acts and 
proceeded against the offenders before the competent authorities. The details in this regard are 
maintained by the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations.  
 
The Ministry through Forest Survey of India carries out biennial assessment of forest and tree 
cover of the country through the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) using satellite-based remote 
sensing and field-based ground truthing. As per the India State of Forest Report-2023 published 
by the Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, the forest cover and tree cover in the country have 
increased by 156.41 square kilometers and 1289.40 square kilometers respectively, as compared 
to the assessment published in ISFR-2021. Illegal tree felling may adversely affect forest 

ecosystems, biodiversity and the ecological functions of forests. The impact of specific incidents 
is dealt with by the concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
  
The Ministry provides technical and financial support to the States and Union Territories 
through various schemes and programmes of the Central Government for increasing forest 
and tree cover, including protection, conservation and sustainable management of forests in 
the country. These include, inter alia, the National Mission for a Green India (GIM), Nagar 
Van Yojana (NVY), Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes 
(MISHTI), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority 
(CAMPA), Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats, and forest fire prevention and 
management schemes. 
  
Further, the plantation campaign "एक पेड़ माँ क े नाम (#Plant4Mother)", launched on the occasion 
of World Environment Day 2024 and continued during the current year, promotes plantation 
activities across the country, through a "Whole of Government" and "Whole of Society" 
approach with participation of all stakeholders for increasing the green cover. 
  
The Ministry issues advisories to States/UTs to protect forests and trees as per the provisions of 
the law including prevention of illegal logging. Measures taken include survey and demarcation 
of forest land, boundary pillars, regular patrolling, legal action under extant laws and community 
participation through Joint Forest Management Committees.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
                  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
                 LOK SABHA 
                     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3561 
            TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
             Rising Wild Animal Attacks 
 
3561. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of rising human casualties in escalating wild animal attack 
in many States including Kerala; 
(b) whether the Union Government has received request from States including Kerala to make 
necessary amendments in the relevant sections of the Wildlife Protection Act to address the 
escalating man-animal conflict; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the response of the Union Government thereto; 
(d) whether the Union Government is aware that the State of Kerala has passed a Bill to amend the 
Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 to address the rising human-animal conflict in the State, if so, the 
response of the Government thereto; and 
(e) whether the Union Government is likely to convene a meeting of the State Forest Ministers to 
review the situation and prepare a national plan considering the severeness of the issue, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
       ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a):  Incidents of human-wildlife conflict have been reported from various parts of the country, 
including Kerala. Management of wildlife and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict are primarily 
the responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations, which 
maintain details of such incidents and the species involved. 
 
(b) to (e): The Ministry received the “Wild Life Protection (Kerala Amendment) Bill, 2025”, for 
amendment of certain provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, which was not agreed to, 
as the existing provisions of the Act already provide a regulatory framework for addressing human-
wildlife conflict.   
     
The Ministry engages with the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations including with 
the State Forest Ministers/public representative on the issue and has recently set up Centre of 
Excellence for Human–Wildlife Conflict Management at the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and 
Natural History (SACON), WII–South India Centre, Coimbatore, to strengthen the scientific and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3562 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
STATUS OF EMPLOYMENT IN BHUBANESWAR LOK SABHA 
CONSTITUENCY 
 
3562.      SMT. APARAJITA SARANGI: 
   
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of total number of registered unemployed youth in the 
Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency as on June 2026; 
(b) the details of steps taken by the Government to boost local job 
creation in the said Constituency; 
(c) the details of central welfare schemes currently implemented for 
the safety, health and social security of unorganised and migrant 
construction workers in Khordha district; and 
(d) whether the Government plans to establish a new National Career 
Service (NCS) Centre or mega -skill hub in Bhubaneswar to bridge 
the industry -academic employability gap and if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017–18.  
 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Unemployment Rate 
(UR) for youth of age 15 -29 years has decreased from 17.2% in 2022 to 
10.6% in 2025 in the State of Odisha (including Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha 
Constituency). 
 
Further, the estimated Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating 
employment on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
increased from 55.1% in 2022 to 61.3% in 2025 in the State of Odisha 
(including Khordha district of Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency). 
 

 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country 
(including Khordha district of Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha Constituency). 
The details of various employment generation schemes/ programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes.  
 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission 
(SIM) to deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive 
network of skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. 
under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims 
at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry 
relevant skills. 
 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 
01.07.2020 for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government 
support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on 
Udyam Registration Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), 
providing employment to over 39 crore people across the country. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Also, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rozgar Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability 
and social security across all sectors, with special focus on the 
manufacturing sector. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore 
aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the 
country, over a period of 2 years.  
 
 
 

Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information 
on skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in]. Government has approved 407 Model 
Career Centres across the country including 32 in the State of Odisha. 
 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram – 
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024 which entails integration of 
different social security/ welfare schemes at single portal and enables 
unorganised workers registered on eShram to access social security 
schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
 
Till date, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central 
Ministries/Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the 
eShram to extend benefits and access to social security schemes to 
eShram cardholders including Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors 
Atmanirbhar Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana 
(PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit 
Bharat- Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB -G RAM 
G), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – 
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB -PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY -U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY), Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One Nation 
One Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana 
(PMMVY), etc. 
 
Apart from the above, eShram has linkages with National  Career 
Service (NCS) for Job Opportunities, Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) for 
Skill Development, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -dhan (PM-SYM) for 
Pension and convergence portal of MoHUA, enabling eShram cardholders 
to avail additional services.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3563 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
E-SHRAM REGISTRATION IN BAHRAICH AND GONDA DISTRICT 
 
3563. SHRI KARAN BHUSHAN SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of the number of unorganised sector workers registered 
on the e-Shram portal, based on district-wise data from July 2023, 
in the Bahraich and Gonda districts of Uttar Pradesh; 
(b)the details of number among the said workers whose registration 
has been verified and updated during the year 2024 and 2025; 
(c)whether an assembly constituency -wise breakup of the said 
registrations is maintained and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d)the details of the steps being taken by the Government to improve 
registration and profile -updation among migrant and agricultural 
workers in the said districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 thAugust, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal 
registers the unorganised workers including gig and platform workers 
and provides them a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self -
declaration basis. 
 
  Over 31.84 crore unorganised workers have already been 
registered on eShram portal including 8.46 crore unorgan ised 
workers in Uttar Pradesh. 
 
  Since July 2023, a total of 48,532 unorganised workers 
have been registered in Bahraich district and 22,595 unorganised 
workers have been registered in Gonda district. 
 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  In the eShram portal, registrati ons are undertaken only 
after successful Aadhaar -based eKYC authentication. This process 
ensures that duplicate or fraudulent registrations are effectively 
eliminated. Further, key fields such as Name, Gender, Date of Birth, 
Permanent Address, and Photograph are directly fetched from UIDAI 
to maintain data authenticity and accuracy. These measures 
collectively safeguard the integrity of the portal and prevent any 
misuse. 
 
  The eShram portal contains State/UT-wise and district -
wise details of registrations of unorganised workers across the 
country. Further, the details are also available occupation-wise, 
gender-wise, and age-wise on eShram portal. 
 
  To enhance registrations under the eShram initiative and 
ensure wider coverage of u norganised workers, including migrant 
and agricultural workers, across all States/UTs, including the 
Bahraich and Gonda districts of Uttar Pradesh, the Government has 
adopted a comprehensive strategy. In addition to enabling self -
registration through the web portal and mobile application, assisted 
registration modes have been introduced via Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), State Sewa Kendras (SSKs), and the UMANG 
platform to facilitate easy access for workers. eShram also allows 
provisions where registered wo rkers can update their profiles 
through eShram portal or Common Service Centres (CSCs).  The 
Ministry of Labour and Employment is conducting targeted 
awareness campaigns comprising registration drives, community 
outreach programs and locally tailored commun ication efforts. To 
further strengthen outreach, the Ministry leverages social media 
channels to disseminate videos, tutorials, and other informative 
content, making the initiative more accessible and engaging. 
 
  To further enhance the availability and ac cessibility of 
eShram and its associated services to unorganised workers, the 
Ministry of Labour and Employment officially launched the eShram 
mobile application on 24th February 2025. This application facilitates 
real-time access to welfare schemes integr ated with the eShram 
platform, thereby significantly strengthening both accessibility and 
user convenience.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3564 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026/ Shravana 19, 1948 (Saka) 
Impact of Rising Inflation on Household Consumption 
3564. Dr. Raj Kumar Chabbewal: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has taken note of the recent Monthly Economic Review, which observed that 
inflation developments warrant continued vigilance and that household consumption may face headwinds, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government is aware that retail inflation has recently exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's 
medium-term inflation target, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of rising food, fuel and wholes ale prices on household 
purchasing power and private consumption, if so, the details thereof;  
(d)  the details of the fiscal measures proposed or undertaken by the Government to protect low and middle -
income households from inflationary pressures; and 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to review indirect tax rates on essential commodities in view of the 
prevailing inflationary outlook and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): The May 2026 edition of the Monthly Economic Review  stated that “… overall consumption demand 
may face headwinds in the coming months” as the forecasts at that time were pointing “…to a below-normal 
monsoon and a likely moderation in economic activity ”. The statement, “The inflation outlook warrants 
vigilance”, was made against the backdrop of a hike in pump prices of petrol and diesel in mid-May, as well 
as the possibility of some pass-through of upstream cost pressures, as signalled by the build-up in wholesale 
prices consequent to the war in West Asia. 
(b): The average retail inflation had declined steadily from 5.4 per cent in 2023 -24 to 2.1 per cent in 2025 -
26. However, owing to the commodity price shock and elevated global energy prices stemming from the 
West Asia Crisis and the expected unfavourable El Niño conditions, retail inflation rose to 4.38 per cent in 
June 2026, still within the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI)  inflation target of 4±2 per cent. The quarterly 
average for Q1 of 2026-27 stands at 3.9 per cent, which is below the inflation target of 4 per cent and RBI’s 
earlier forecast of 4.2 per cent for the said quarter.  

(c) and (d): The wholesale inflation rate declined from 1.7 per cent in 2024 -25 to 0.4 per cent in 2025 -26, 
but rose to 9.3 per cent in Q1 of 2026-27 owing to the global supply shock . Though the retail inflation also 
followed a similar path, the price pressures at retail level were much moderate and stable. The recent uptick 
in retail inflation  was largely driven by the unfavourable weather conditions that were exerting upward 
pressure on food inflation, especially on prices of protein-rich foods and select vegetables. The fuel inflation 
was relati vely modest, reflecting only a partial transmission of elevated global fuel prices to the energy 
commodities at the retail level. In Q1of 2026-27, the food and fuel inflation were 4.8% and 1% respectively. 
The Government continuously monitors the price sit uation in the country and undertakes fiscal, 
administrative and supply -side measures, as warranted by evolving economic conditions, to protect the 
purchasing power of households, particularly low- and middle-income households. Some of the recent fiscal 
measures include, reduction of Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on crude palm oil, crude soybean oil and crude 
sunflower oil from 20 per cent to 10 per cent in June 2025; on whole Tur to Nil with effect from 4 March 
2023; extension of duty rationalization for the imp ort of Tur and Urad under the 'Free Category' till 
31.03.2027; reduction of Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess (AIDC) on Masur to Nil from 13 
February 2022 to 7 March 2025; distribution of food grains free of cost to around 81 crore beneficiaries under 
the National Food Security Act;  reduction in the Central excise duty on petrol and diesel by ₹10 per litre in 
March 2026; rationalisation of the Goods & Services Tax (GST) rates in September 2025, especially on items 
consumed by the common man, such as food products, household articles, medicines, medical equipment, 
agricultural goods and specified automobiles etc. ; and increasing the disposable income of individuals by 
exempting annual incomes up to ₹12 lakh (and ₹12.75 lakh for salaried individuals with standard deduction) 
from income tax. These measures have supported household consumption, as evidenced by the share of 
private final consumption expenditure in GDP remaining broadly stable at 56.5 –56.7 per cent (base year 
2022-23). Moreover, as p er the latest GDP estimates released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation, per capita Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) recorded a robust growth of 6.8 
per cent in 2025-26, up from 4.8 per cent in 2023-24.  
(e): The Governm ent keeps the indirect tax structure under continuous review in consultation with 
stakeholders and, in the case of GST, on the recommendations of the GST Council. Decisions regarding tax 
rates on essential commodities are made from time to time, as indicat ed above, after considering various 
factors, including inflationary trends, revenue implications,  and overall macroeconomic conditions.  Any 
proposal to rationalise GST rates or to grant exemptions  for essential goods or services requires the 
recommendation of the GST Council, a constitutional body comprising representatives of the Union and the 
States/UTs. The last rationalisation, including for many mass -consumption goods, was undertaken in 
September 2025.
