GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3636 
 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 10 AUGUST, 2026/ SHRAVANA 19, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Restoration of OPS 
 
3636.   SHRI ADITYA YADAV 
 
Will the Minister of Finance be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the official stance, fiscal calculations, and policy analysis conducted by the Central Government 
regarding the growing demands from Central and State Government employees for the restoration 
of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS); 
(b) the core structural infirmities, market risks, and annuity deficits identified by employee federations 
within the current National Pension System (NPS); 
(c) whether any high-level review committee has been constituted to modify the NPS to guarantee a 
defined, inflation-linked minimum pension to employees without burdening State finances and if 
so, the status of its report; and 
(d) the total corpus accumulated under the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority  
(PFRDA) from Central employees' contributions as of date? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c) The Government had moved away from Old Pension Scheme (OPS) due to its unsustainable fiscal 
liability on the Government exchequer. The restoration of OPS in the States falls exclusively under State 
policy discretion. However, Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), in its recent State Finance Audit 
Reports, has highlighted the fiscal implications of reversion to OPS by the States. The National Pension 
System (NPS) is a defined contribution -based scheme which was introduced for Central Government 
employees (except armed forces) joining service on or after 01.01.2004.  With a view of improving upon 
the pensionary benefits for such employees, a Committee was constituted under the chairpersonship of the 
then Finance Secretary to suggest measures to modify the NPS. Based on the deliberations of the Committee 
with stakeholders, Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) has already been introduced, w.e.f. 01.04.2025, as an 
option under NPS with the objective of providing inflation linked defined benefits with a minimum assured 
payout of Rs. 10,000/- per month, after retirement to the Central Government employees covered under the 
NPS. The UPS is a fund -based payout system that relies on the regular and timely accumulation and 
investment of applicable contributions made by both the employee and the employer (Central Government) 
to provide an assured monthly payout after retirement.  
 
(d) The total Asset under Management under NPS for Central Government employees as on 26.07.2026 is 
Rs. 3.65 lakh crores.

state:  
 
(a)the details of revisions made by the Labour Bureau in the 
methodology adopted for compilation of rural wage statistics and 
labour market indicators in the country; 
(b)the details of measu res taken by the Government to ensure that 
wage trends across the  States and Union Territories, including 
Puducherry are adequately reflected in official labour statistics; 
(c)the details of rural wage growth recorded in Puducherry and other 
States/Union Territories during the recent period and the factors 
contributing to variations therein; 
(d)the manner in which the Government utilises wage data for 
formulation of employment, skill development and social protection 
policies; and 
(e)the details of steps ta ken or proposed to be taken by the 
Government to strengthen labour market data systems and support 
income growth and livelihood security for rural workers across the 
country?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e): Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of 
Labour & Employment,       revised the methodology,  from July 2025,

including Puducherry, within the sample,    in line with the 
corresponding change in the sample villages for the revised 
Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers and Rural Labourers 
(CPI-AL/RL) 2019=100.

Government and the State Governments are empowered to fix, review 
and revise minimum wages. Further, minimum wages for most  
categories of workers are determined and implemented by the  
respective State Governments in accordance with the provisions of  
the Code on Wages, 2019 and the earlier Minimum Wages Act, 1948  
(now subsumed under the Code).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3640 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Projects under National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change 
 
3640.  SHRI GAURAV GOGOI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has commissioned any study attributing the rising frequency and 
intensity of floods in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Majuli districts to climate change, if so, the 
findings thereof and if not, whether the same is proposed; 
(b) whether climate vulnerability and flood-risk assessments have been completed for Assam and if 
so, the districts covered and their current risk classification, district-wise; 
(c) the details of wetland restoration, floodplain conservation and ecosystem-based flood mitigation 
projects sanctioned for Assam under the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change, including 
any project covering Majuli or the affected Upper Assam districts; and 
(d) the details of funds released, utilised and outcomes achieved thereunder? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) Under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), the Department of Science 
and Technology (DST) implements the National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem 
(NMSHE). Under the Mission, the Assam State Climate Change Cell has been established to provide 
assistance to the State for undertaking vulnerability and risk assessment, human capacity building 
programmes, public awareness programmes and institutional capacity building. The objective is to 
address the sustenance of the Himalayan ecosystem and for implementation of actions identified by 
the State as part of its State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC). 
 
Further, DST has supported a study on vulnerability and risk mapping of Indian States and published 
the reports titled "Vulnerability Profiles for India: State and District Level using a Common 
Framework" and "District-Level Climate Risk Assessment for India: Mapping Flood and Drought 
Risks Using Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Framework". 
 
The vulnerability report identifies Assam as the 5th most climate-vulnerable State in India with a 
vulnerability index of 0.62. Additionally, 15 of the 25 most vulnerable districts in India are from 
Assam, with Karimganj being the most vulnerable district in India with a vulnerability index of 0.753. 
 
The risk assessment study reports that Assam has very high to high flood hazard-prone districts, and 
24 districts fall under the 'Very High' flood as well as drought risk category. Further, according to the 

 
 
   
 
study, 11 districts are at dual risk of flood and drought, including Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Sibsagar, 
South Salmara-Mankachar and Golaghat in Assam. 
 
Under the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC), the Government of India 
sanctioned a project titled "Management of Ecosystem of Kaziranga National Park by Creating 
Climate Resilient Livelihoods for Vulnerable Communities through Organic Farming and Pond-
based Pisciculture" with total grant assistance of Rs. 24.57 crore. The entire amount of Rs. 24.57 
crore released for the project has been utilized. The project was implemented in the peripheral areas 
of Kaziranga National Park across the districts of Golaghat, Nagaon and Sonitpur in Assam.  
 
The major outcomes of the project include rejuvenation of selected beels (wetlands), resulting in 
enhanced water-holding capacity and improved ecosystem resilience; creation of climate-resilient 
livelihood opportunities for vulnerable communities residing in the vicinity of Kaziranga National 
Park through the promotion of organic farming and pond-based pisciculture; and improved watershed 
management through the implementation of various water conservation measures, contributing to 
sustainable natural resource management.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3641 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Performance Grading Index for States and Districts 
 
3641. Shri Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives of the Performance Grading Index for States/UTs (PGI-S) and Performance Grading 
Index for Districts (PGI-D) and the key outcomes achieved through their implementation; 
(b) the details of performance of Andhra Pradesh under PGI-S and the district-wise performance 
under PGI-D, particularly for Palnadu district, during the last three years; 
(c) whether the Government has identified key areas requiring improvement based on the PGI 
assessments and if so, the details thereof with respect to Andhra Pradesh and Palnadu district; 
(d) the corrective measures, technical assistance and financial support provided by the Central 
Government to States and districts with lower performance to improve learning outcomes, 
governance, infrastructure and digital learning; and 
(e) whether any targets or timelines have been fixed by the Central Government to improve the PGI 
rankings of States and districts including Andhra Pradesh, particularly Palnadu district, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and (b): The Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education has 
prepared 70-indicator based Performance Grading Index (PGI) 2.0 for States/UTs to measure key 
driving performance and critical areas of school education at State/UT level. Most of the States/UTs 
has improved their score in 2025-26 as compared to 2024-25 including Andhra Pradesh. The domain-
wise performance of the States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh in PGI 2.0 reports for last three years 
can be accessed at https://spgi.udiseplus.gov.in. Similarly, domain-wise performance of districts in 
PGI-D report has been released for last 3 years can be accessed at https://dpgi.udiseplus.gov.in. Total 
of 473 out of 782 districts improved their PGI score in 2025-26 as compared to 2024-25. 
 
 
(c) to (e): Indicators of PGI 2.0 and PGI-D have been aligned to policy initiatives and interventions 
introduced post implementation of National Education policy (NEP) 2020 for proper tracking the 
progress.  
 
The DoSEL, Ministry of Education has shared the findings of PGI 2.0 report and PGI-D report 
with all the States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh to suggest the gaps at the disaggregated level and 
for further improvement by prioritizing areas of intervention to ensure that the school education 
system is robust at every level. PGI-D also provides insight into intra State comparison of progress 
of School education which is useful to assess the intervention required at district level and to take 
mid-course correction, wherever required for the holistic development of district as a whole in school 
education. 
 
 

 
The Performance Grading Index of all States and UTs has been discussed during the Project 
Approval Board (PAB) meetings. Based on the performance of the States, the activities suggested to 
the States/UTs in such PAB meetings, includes teacher training in assessment as learning, State text 
book analysis, use of early language kit and early mathematics kit developed by NCERT, training in 
child friendly assessment practices for teachers, documentation of best practices in the States/UTs for 
improvement in learning levels, etc. 
 
Further, Central Government helps States and UTs under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha, which is an overarching scheme of school education covering all levels from pre-
primary to senior secondary. Financial assistance is provided to the States and UTs for various 
activities to improve enrolment in Govt. schools, which include opening/strengthening of new schools 
up to senior secondary level, strengthening school infrastructure, setting up, up gradation and running 
of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) upto class 12, setting up of residential schools/hostel 
named Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, transport allowance, undertaking enrolment 
drives, seasonal hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in 
schools, etc, financial assistance is also provided for aids and appliances for children with special 
needs hostels/residential camps, provision of vocational education and ICT facilities in schools, 
providing free text books and free uniform, transport/escort facility, etc.

(a) the details of schemes being implemented by the Government for the conservation and development 
of eco-tourism in National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary; 
(b) the details of steps taken to increase the participation of local communities in such Schemes; 
(c) the details of funds sanctioned and utilised for the said purpose during the last five years; and

CHANGE

Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats, which comprises the components of Project Tiger & 
Elephant and Development of Wildlife Habitats for the conservation and management of Protected

3643. Dr. Shrikant Eknath Shinde: 
Shri Naresh Ganpat Mhaske:

Smt. Bharti Pardhi: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the National Credit Framework (NCrF) has achieved full horizontal and vertical 
mobility between general and vocational education in July 2026, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether a formal "Equivalence Mechanism" has been established to treat years of industrial 
experience as academic credits, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether this framework has allowed Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and Polytechnic 
graduates to enroll directly into the third year of degree programmes during the current 
academic session, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether this "Skill-Degree Integration" has led to a significant increase in the Gross 
Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education, if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether the industry has formally recognized these "Credit-Based Skill Certifications" for 
senior-level hiring, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) whether this unified credit system is now being benchmarked against the European Credit 
Transfer System (ECTS), if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (f): The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with an aim to provide holistic, multidisciplinary, flexible and student-centric education. It encourages integration of skill education & envisions a detailed National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) as the basis for Recognition of Prior Learning.  

 
In alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020, the Government has approved National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) as a comprehensive credit framework encompassing elementary, school, 
higher, and skill education. The NCrF provides for creditisation of all learning and assignment, 
accumulation, storage, transfer & redemption of credits, subject to assessment; and establishes 
academic equivalence between skill, general and experiential education while enabling 
mobility within & between them. As reported in AISHE 2023-24, more than 700 Universities 
and over 7500 affiliated colleges have adopted NCrF. 
 
The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified “SOP for Operationalisation of 
National Credit Framework in Higher Education” as a practical guide for implementation of 
NCrF. The SOP allows up to 50% of the total credits for a program to be earned from the skill-
based courses.  
 
The All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) in its Approval Process Handbook 
(APH) 2023-27, sets norms for Entry Level Qualifications for the Technical Programmes in 
accordance with NCrF. It allows 10th + 2-year ITIs students to be eligible for admission to 
Second Year Diploma course(s) in any branch of Engineering and Technology. Further, lateral 
entry to Third Year is available for candidates possessing a 2-year UG Diploma in Engineering 
(NCrF Level 5.0). 
 
Further, the National Council of V ocational Education and Training (NCVET) has developed 
“Guidelines for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)”. The guidelines delineate a roadmap for 
the seamless implementation of RPL, and empower the industrial bodies to conduct RPL 
assessments for their workforces. This aligns the assessment process in a manner that meets 
the industry's needs. Credits are awarded based on assessment of learning outcomes of the 
specific skills, competencies and knowledge acquired. 
 
Due to concerted efforts by the Government, India’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher 
education increased from 23.7 in 2014–15 to 30 in 2023–24. Female GER rose from 22.9 to 
31.2 during the same period. The rise in GER has been accompanied by significant growth in 
student enrolment, with total higher education enrolment increasing from 3.42 crore in 2014–
15 to 4.50 crore in 2023–24, adding more than 1.08 crore students to the higher education 
system. 
 
NEP 2020 envisions an education system rooted in Indian ethos that contributes directly to 
transforming India, into an equitable and vibrant knowledge society, by providing high-quality 
education to all. NCrF aims to contribute to vision this by establishing equivalence and mobility 
between general and skill education so that lifelong learning, recognition of prior learning, 
multiple entry and exit, and continuous professional development is encouraged in the 
education ecosystem.

NPAs in Gold Loans 
3648. DR. C M RAMESH:  
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is true that five Southern States account for 75% of outstanding gold loans of Rs. 
18.62 lakh crores in the country as on March, 2026, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also true that Andhra Pradesh, with Rs. 3.09 lakh crores stood second and 
 Telangana, with Rs. 1.6 lakh crores, stands at fourth position, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the rapid growth in gold lending poses any systematic or financial stability risks, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(d) whether it is also true that gold loans have become the second largest product in retail lending 
after home loans, if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the details of Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) in gold loans and whether there is any increasing 
trend of NPAs in gold loans during the last 4-5 years, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) the measures taken by the Government and the RBI to regulate gold loans and to protect 
borrowers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a)and(b): The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has informed that it does not maintain the State-wise 
information on outstanding gold loans. However, as per the information received from Public Sector 
Banks (PSBs), the State-wise details of gold loans outstanding of PSBs on 31st March, 2026, is 
provided at Annexure-I. 
(c): RBI has informed that, as noted in the Financial Stability Report (FSR), June 2026, the rapid 
growth in gold loans has been supported by rising gold prices. Loan-to-value (LTV) ratios across 
Banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) have declined despite growth in gold 
lending, thereby strengthening collateral buffers and enhancing lenders' resilience to movements in 
gold prices. It has further informed that asset quality in the gold loan portfolio remains stable, 
reflecting the sound collateral position of lenders.  
 
Loans against gold have been instrumental in promoting financial inclusion and providing access to 
credit, particularly to rural, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and underserved 
segments of the population by bringing new-to-bank or new-to-credit customers amongst that 
segment under the ambit of formal lending channels, including banks and NBFCs, and by protecting 
such borrowers who could otherwise have moved to unorganized channels and been susceptible to 
usurious and prejudiced loan covenants. 
 
(d): As per the information received from RBI, as on 31st March 2026, the largest product in retail 
lending is Housing Loans followed by Personal Loans and Vehicle Loans. 
 

 
(e): The number of defaults in gold loans has declined during the last five years. The Gross Non-
Performing Asset (GNPA) ratio for gold loans of SCBs has declined from 0.19% as on 31st March, 
2023 to 0.12% as on 31st March, 2026. Similarly, the GNPA ratio for gold loans of NBFCs has 
declined from 2.32% to 0.81% during the same period. The details are provided at Annexure-II. 
 
(f): RBI has issued Directions on Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral in June, 2025 to 
harmonise lending norms against gold collateral across banks, co-operative banks and NBFCs, 
while strengthening responsible lending, collateral valuation and consumer protection. The 
Directions provide for prudent Loan-to-Value (LTV) norms, standardized valuation of gold collateral.  
 
Further, to safeguard borrowers from distress sales during recovery, RBI has prescribed measures, 
inter-alia, adequate prior notice before auction, a reserve price of at least 90% of the current 
collateral value, refund of any surplus realised after adjustment of dues, and transparent assaying, 
valuation, auction and recovery practices. The regulatory framework also requires upfront disclosure 
of charges, standardized documentation and compensation for delays in the release of pledged 
collateral, thereby strengthening consumer protection and ensuring fair treatment of borrowers.

Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana 
†3650. SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
   Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)     the total number of bank accounts opened in the country so far under the Pradhan Mantri Jan 
Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), along with the details of beneficiaries belonging to women and rural 
areas; 
(b)      whether significant success has been achieved through this scheme in strengthening financial 
inclusion and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), if so, the details thereof; 
(c)     whether the banking and social security facilities available to Jan Dhan account holders have 
been expanded, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)     the new steps being taken by the Government to further strengthen financial inclusion? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d) As on 22.07.2026, a total of 58.84 crore Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)

in rural/semi-urban areas and 32.79 crore PMJDY accounts are of women beneficiaries. 
PMJDY guidelines envisage channeling Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from the Government to

India (RBI) since 2017 with an objective to adopt community -led innovative and participatory 
approaches to financial literacy. A total of 2,421 CFLs have been set up across the country, with 
one CFL covering three blocks on an average. 
Banks regularly organise camps, to create awareness about the various schemes, basic banking, 
digital financial literacy, consumer protection etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
        UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3651 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Environmental Degradation due to Illegal Sand Mining 
 
3651. DR. PRASHANT YADAORAO PADOLE: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the reported large-scale illegal sand mining at several 
sand ghats in Bhandara district, Maharashtra, involving the use of prohibited heavy machinery 
and causing damage to river ecosystems and the environment; 
(b) if so, whether the Government has sought any report from the State Government of 
Maharashtra regarding the environmental impact of such illegal sand mining and the action 
taken to prevent it, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to issue directions or advisories to the State Government 
to strengthen enforcement against illegal sand mining and ensure protection of river 
ecosystems; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to promote the use of technologies such as drone 
surveillance, remote sensing, GPS tracking and real-time monitoring to prevent illegal sand 
mining and improve environmental compliance, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): The Section 23C of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) (MMDR) 
Act, 1957 empowers the State Government to frame rules to prevent illegal mining, 
transportation and storage of minerals and for purposes connected therewith. Therefore, the 
control of illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals and purposes connected 
therewith is the primary responsibility of the State Government. 
 
As per the information received from the District Mining Officer, Bhandara, Government of 
Maharashtra, complaints regarding illegal sand mining have been reported. In this regard, the 
State Government of Maharashtra has directed all Sub-Divisional Officers to inspect the sand 
ghats in Bhandara District for taking appropriate action. In addition to this, joint squads have 
been constituted at the District, Sub-Divisional and Taluka levels comprising of officials of the 
Revenue, Police and Regional Transport Office (RTO) to strengthen enforcement against 
illegal sand mining and transportation.  
 
As per the information provided by the State Government, during the year 2025-26, action was 
taken in 672 cases of illegal activity and fines amounting to ₹585.17 lakh were imposed, out 
of which ₹282.57 lakh has been recovered, and criminal cases were registered against 106 
persons. During 2026-27 (till date), action has been taken in 93 cases and fines amounting to 

 
 
₹86.76 lakh have been imposed, ₹50.65 lakh has been recovered, and criminal cases have been 
registered against 54 persons. 
 
Further, the Government of Maharashtra has made GPS-based tracking mandatory for vehicles 
transporting sand , periodic survey of sand ghats by Maharashtra Remote Sensing Application 
Centre (MRSAC) and usage of 'Mahakhanij' software platform for monitoring sand extraction 
and transportation. 
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has also issued the Enforcement & 
Monitoring Guidelines for Sand Mining, 2020, supplementary to the Sustainable Sand Mining 
Management Guidelines, 2016, which provide a framework for scientific and sustainable sand 
mining through the use of remote sensing, GIS, GPS, drones and other IT-enabled technologies 
for effective monitoring, enforcement and prevention of illegal sand mining.

CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): Government has launched the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) in 2019 as a long-term, 
time-bound, national-level strategy to address air pollution in 130 cities across 24 States/UTs, including 
metropolitan cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Pune 
and Surat.  
 
City Specific Clean Air Action Plans have been prepared for all 130 cities under NCAP to implement 
air quality improvement measures in respective cities to target air pollution sources like soil & road dust, 
vehicular emissions, waste burning, construction & demolition activities and industrial pollution. 
 
Air quality performance based incentive grant of ₹ 16,423.56 crore has been released to targeted cities 
under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) as a critical gap funding to implement air pollution 
mitigation measures, during FY 2019-20 till 2025-26. 
 
Details of air quality improvement in terms of reduction in PM10 concentrations of metro cities under 
NCAP in FY 2025-26 as compared to FY 2017-18 has been provided at Annexure-I. 
 
To identify various factors contributing to air pollution and prioritise the air quality improvement 
measures under city action plans under NCAP, Source Apportionment (SA) studies have been carried 
out in NCAP cities including Delhi. Sources of air pollution as per source apportionment studies 
conducted in metro cities are enclosed at Annexure-II. 
 
Details of various steps taken by the Government for air quality improvement are enclosed at Annexure 
III.

Annexure-III 
 
Measures taken by the Government to address air pollution 
 
1.0 Measures for control of vehicular emissions: 
 Leapfrogging from BS-IV to BS-VI fuel standards from 1st April, 2020 for the rest of the 
country. 
 Introduction of BS VI compliant vehicles across the country since April, 2020. 
 Installation of Vapor Recovery System (VRS) in new and existing petrol pumps selling 
gasoline >100kl per month in million plus cities and those selling >300kl per month in 
cities with population between 1 lakh to 1 million to control vehicular refuelling emissions. 
 Promotion of electric vehicles through Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024 (EMPS 
2024) scheme of Ministry of Heavy Industries, Government of India  
 Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) has been launched 
as an initiative to set up Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) production plants and make CBG 
available in the market for use in automotive fuels. 
 Establishment of charging infrastructure for E-vehicles as per guidelines issued by Ministry 
of Power.  
 Synchronization in traffic movements/Introduction of Intelligent Traffic System (ITS) for 
lane-driving. 
 Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) has issued notifications on the 
establishment of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facility (RVSFs) and Automated Testing 
System (ATS) to create an enabling framework for implementation of Vehicle Scrapping 
Policy.    
 Improving and Strengthening of Pollution Under Control (PUC) Certificate System 
programme across the country by MoRTH. 
 
2.0 Measures for control of industrial emission: 
 MoEF&CC notified “Standards for Emission or Discharge of Environmental Pollutants 
from various Industries” under Schedule-I of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986. 
So far, more than 79 industrial specific environmental standards have been notified. In 
respect of the industrial sectors, for which specific standards are not available, general 
standards as notified under Schedule-VI of the Environment Protection Rules, 1986 are 
applicable. 
 For strengthening monitoring mechanism and effective compliance through self-regulatory 
mechanism, CPCB directed all 17 categories of highly polluting industries to install Online 
Continuous Emission Monitoring System (OCEMS). 
 CPCB vide direction dated 12.02.2025 classified a total of 419 sectors and sub-sectors in 
Red (125), Orange (137), Green (61), White (87) and Blue (9). 
 The Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of 
India notifies industry specific discharge standards under Schedule-I: ‘Standards for 
Emission or Discharge of Environmental Pollutants from various Industries’ of 
Environment Protection Act, 1986. So far, industry specific environmental standards, for 
79 industrial sectors (including emission standards for 56 sectors) have been notified. 
Industrial sectors, for which specific standards are not available, general standards as 
notified under Schedule-VI of Environment Protection Rules, 1986 shall be applicable. 
 Ban on use of imported pet coke in the country since July 26, 2018, with exception for use 
in permitted processes. 

 CPCB has come out with System and Procedure for Emission Compliance Testing of 
Retro-fit Emission Control Devices (RECD) for Diesel Power Generating Set Engines up 
to Gross Mechanical Power 800 kW. 
 In 2022, CPCB mandated new brick kilns must use zig-zag technology, vertical shaft, or 
piped natural gas, and adhere to specific standards. Also, Existing kilns must also convert 
to these technologies or use approved fuels. 
 In 2023, CPCB introduced stricter emission standards (CPCB IV+) for diesel generators 
(DG sets) up to 800 kW, mandating dual-fuel systems (70% gas, 30% diesel) where gas 
infrastructure is available and requiring Retro-fit Emission Control Devices (RECD) with 
a minimum PM capturing efficiency of 70%. 
 
3.0 Air Quality Monitoring and Network 
 National Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched in 2015. Information is being disseminated 
to public through daily air quality bulletins. 
 Ambient Air Quality Network: The country has a network of 1646 ambient air quality 
monitoring stations (593 continuous and 1053 manual) covering 603 cities in 28 states and 
7 UTs.  
 A centralized air quality monitoring portal is operated by Central Pollution Control Board 
wherein, tracking of various information such as hourly PM concentrations, Live Air 
Quality Data of Monitoring stations and Live Air Quality Index is being carried out. 
 Daily AQI Bulletin is published on CPCB website giving AQI information for cities across 
India. 
 
4.0 C&D Waste & MSW 
 CPCB published following guidelines (available on website of CPCB) 
1. Environmental Management of Construction & Demolition (C & D) Wastes’ in 
March, 2017 
2. ‘Guidelines on DUST Mitigation Measures in Handling Construction Material & 
C&D Wastes’ in November 2017. 
3. Disposal of legacy waste by bio-mining and bio-remediation to address open 
burning and landfill fires 
 MoEFCC notified the Construction & Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025, in 
force from 1st April, 2026. These rules emphasize the roles and accountability of waste 
generators at source and various stakeholders focusing on segregation, recovery, reuse, and 
recycling. In the said revised rules, various provisions have been introduced for better 
management of waste generated by bulk waste generators due to Construction and 
Demolition activities including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for recycling of 
such waste generation. 
 CPCB has issued direction to all SPCBs/ PCCs for deployment of Anti-Smog Gun and 
implementation of adequate dust mitigation measures at construction projects/ sites having 
area more than 20,000 sq. meters. CPCB has issued guidelines/ mechanism for use of anti-
smog guns in Construction and Demolition projects.  
 MoEFCC notified the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, notified under the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and effective from April , 2026. The revised rules 
integrate the principles of Circular Economy and Extended Producer Responsibility, with 
a specific focus on efficient waste segregation and management. The rules provide for the 
levy of environmental compensation based on the ‘Polluter Pays’ principle for non-
compliance, including cases of operating without registration, false reporting, submission 
of forged documents or improper solid waste management practices.  

 CPCB issued directions to all SPCBs/PCCs for enforcement of provision of SWM Rules-
2016 regarding bio-mining of legacy waste during Jan-2021.  
 CPCB issued directions to all SPCBs/PCCs for implementation of SWM Rules-2016 
regarding fire incidents at MSW dumpsites during May 2022.  
 
5.0  Measures for control of Crop Residue Burning 
 
• A Central Sector Scheme on Crop Residue Management has been 
implemented by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoAFW) since 2018-19. 
Under the scheme, from 2018-19 to 2026-27 (as on 29.07.2026), cumulative amount of Rs. 
4550.451 crores have been provided to the concerned States (Punjab – Rs. 2206.28 crores, 
Haryana – Rs. 1220.42 crores, Uttar Pradesh – Rs. 911.03 crores, Madhya Pradesh – Rs. 
90.218 crores, NCT of Delhi – Rs. 7.405 Crores, ICAR– Rs. 107.378 crores & others Rs. 
7.7205 Crores). States have distributed more than 3.54 lakh machines to the individual 
farmers and established more than 43,508 Custom Hiring Centers (CHCs) in these States. 
• Ministry of Power has issued a policy for co-firing of biomass in Coal based Thermal 
Power Plants on 7th November, 2025. The policy mandates Coal based Thermal Power 
Plants outside the National Capital Region to co-fire 5 per cent (by weight) of biomass 
pellets or torrefied MSW charcoal from 2025-26. 
• A Standard Protocol for Estimation of Crop Residue Burning Fire Events using Satellite 
Data was developed by ISRO in consultation with State Remote Sensing Centers & Indian 
Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and issued by CAQM in August, 2021. The said 
protocol is used for monitoring crop residue burning fire events and IARI through its 
CREAMS Laboratory, publishes daily fire event data for the States of Haryana, Delhi, 
Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, based on this protocol during paddy 
and wheat harvesting seasons. 
• CAQM has issued directions for co-firing of 5-10% biomass with coal in thermal power 
plants located within 300 kms of Delhi, and, in captive power plants of industrial units 
located in NCR. 
• CAQM has issued directions to State Governments of Punjab and Haryana to mandate use 
of paddy straw-based biomass pellets / briquettes in all brick kilns located in the districts 
beyond NCR, as one of the means towards elimination of the practice of open paddy 
stubble burning, aiming for 50 % co-firing of paddy straw based, pellets /briquettes with a 
target of at least 20 % w.e.f. 01.11.2025, 30 % w.e.f. 01.11.2026, 40% w.e.f. 01.1.2027 
and 50 % w.e.f. 01.11.2028. 
• Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has framed Guidelines for grant of one-time 
financial support under Environment Protection Charge funds for establishment of 
pelletization and Torrefaction plants to promote utilisation of paddy straw.  
• 32 pelletisation plants have been sanctioned so far (25 in Punjab, 07 in Haryana) at a cost 
of Rs. 34.72 crore. Total production capacity of 32 sanctioned plants is 137TPH and these 
are expected to utilise 6.36 lakh tonnes paddy straw annually for production of 4.93Iakh 
tonne pellets. 
6.0 Regular Stakeholder Consultation, Public & Media Outreach 
 CPCB has developed a mobile app i.e. SAMEER, where Real-time Ambient air quality 
data of various parameters including AQI is also given. Sameer app also facilitates the 
public in lodging of air pollution related complaints in NCR region and such complaints 
are assigned to various local agencies.  
 Dedicated media corner, Twitter and Facebook accounts have also been created for public 
outreach.  
 Complaint redressal on SAMEER app and social media platforms is monitored and 
redressal status is shared with respective agencies. 

 Daily AQI status is shared on social media platforms. Various campaigns as well as 
informative posts related to air pollution, firecrackers, vehicular pollution, stubble burning, 
sustainable lifestyle, etc. are also posted regularly on social media platforms.

RTE Admission 
 
3653. Dr. D Ravi Kumar: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Central Government has taken note of the reports that RTE admissions in Tamil Nadu 
private schools have been affected due to delay/withholding of Central reimbursement support under the 
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is a fact that thousands of economically weaker section children in Tamil Nadu depend on 
the 25 per cent RTE quota in private schools for access to education, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of RTE reimbursement funds due, released and pending to Tamil Nadu during 2023-24, 2024-
25 and 2025-26; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure uninterrupted admissions and timely reimbursement to 
private schools under the RTE Act? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates the 
appropriate Government to provide free and compulsory elementary education to every child of the age 6 
to 14 years in a neighborhood school. Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act mandates unaided private schools to 
reserve at least 25% of seats at the entry level for children belonging to economically weaker sections and 
disadvantaged groups from the neighbourhood and provide them free education and later claim 
reimbursement from the respective State/Union Territory Government/Administration. The amount so 
reimbursed to the private schools can be claimed under the Samagra Shiksha scheme by the State/Union 
Territory Government/Administration. As per the RTE Act, 2009, State/Union Territory 
Government/Administration, including the State Government of Tamil Nadu is the ‘appropriate 
government’ for the implementation of Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act. 
 

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided 
to States/Union Territories for various interventions including ‘RTE Entitlements’ component. Under the 
scheme lump sum funds are released to the States/Union Territories, including Tamil Nadu and further 
distribution of funds component-wise, including ‘RTE Entitlements’ component, is done by the respective 
States/Union Territories including Tamil Nadu.  In respect of Tamil Nadu, the details of amount approved

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 3655 
ANSWERED ON – 10/08/2026 
 
Lack of Educational Infrastructure in Aspirational Districts of Uttar Pradesh 
 
 
†3655. Shri Ram Shiromani Verma: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that many Government schools in the aspirational districts 
like Shravasti and Balrampur in Uttar Pradesh lack smart classrooms, science laboratories, 
computer laboratories and digital education resources, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether any concrete steps have been taken by the Government to provide digital and quality 
education in the said districts under the National Education Policy-2020, if so, the details thereof; 
and 
 
(c) whether the Government is considering implementing any special scheme to provide modern 
educational resources in all Government schools and if so, the details thereof along with the 
proposed timeline therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): Education being in the concurrent list with majority of the schools under the 
domain of the State and UTs, the primary responsibility of providing accessible, 
affordable, equitable, inclusive and quality education lies with the State/UT Governments. 
As reported on UDISE+ 2025-26, there are 71 ICT/Computer Labs, 462 Smart Classrooms, 6 
Physics Labs, 6 Chemistry Labs and 5 Biology Labs in Government Schools of the district of 
Shravasti. There are 132 ICT/Computer Labs, 357 Smart Classrooms, 5 Physics Labs, 5 
Chemistry Labs and 4 Biology Labs in Government Schools of the district of Balrampur. 
 
Ministry of Education has taken several initiatives to provide digital and modern 
educational resources in the country. More specifically, besides ICT and Smart Classes,  
the Ministry implements digital initiatives such as PM eVidya, DIKSHA and SWAYAM 
under Samagra Shiksha to enhance digital learning in Government schools across the 
country. These initiatives aim to enhance the quality of education by integrating 
technology into teaching and learning processes.  
 
Under the centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is 
provided to all States/UTs including aspirational districts of State of Uttar Pradesh for 
setting up of ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms in Government Schools having classes VI 
to XII. The financial assistance is provided based on proposals submitted in the Annual 
Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) by the State/UT. These proposals then 
appraised/approved by PAB in consultation with the States and UTs as per the 
programmatic and financial norms of the scheme and availability of budgetary and  
 

 
financial resources. The proposals of State of Uttar Pradesh under Samagra Shiksha are 
approved as per norms of the scheme. 
 
Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation’s One 
Nation, One Digital platform for providing quality e-content for school education in 
States/UTs along with QR coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. As a 
participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs/Autonomous Bodies (ABs) have generated and 
contributed over 3.67 lakh content in mother tongue/local/regional languages enabling 
multilingualism. Details of e-content available in regional languages can be accessed at 
https://diksha.gov.in/data/. Overall, 579.41 crore learning sessions for 2.29 crore users 
have been completed on DIKSHA by students, teachers and other stakeholders. The 
stakeholders also have access to more than 836 Virtual Labs on DIKSHA that help them 
with simulation of real-world laboratory environment. The platform supports both online 
and offline access, enabling learners to download content and continue learning without 
internet connectivity. In 2025-26, DIKSHA platform was used by more than 2.24 lakh 
students, 11 lakh teachers and 0.13 lakh parents in the State of Uttar Pradesh. Uttar 
Pradesh has 26.89 lakh registered users, 254 energised textbooks and contributed more 
than 17,000 e-content on the DIKSHA platform. 
 
A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya has been launched, which unifies all 
efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education 
across the country. The key components of PM eVidya are also aligned towards enhancing 
digital literacy and include 200 DTH TV channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all 
States/UTs to provide supplementary education in various Indian languages for classes 1-
12. Under the PM eVidya 200 DTH TV Channels initiative, the State of Uttar Pradesh has 
been allotted five (UP PM eVidya 173-177) dedicated channels. 
As informed by State of Uttar Pradesh, to enhance the quality of education and 
classroom teaching-learning practices, structured pedagogy-based Teaching-Learning 
Materials (TLMs), including Teacher Guides, Workbooks, Mathematics Kits, and Teacher 
Diaries, have been provided. Annual face-to-face teacher training is conducted to 
strengthen pedagogical practices, supplemented by continuous on-site academic support 
through supportive supervision. Further, to promote peer learning and continuous 
professional development among teachers, Shikshak Sankul meetings are organised every 
month at the Nyaya Panchayat level. 
 
Further, PM SHRI schools envisages to showcase all the initiatives of National 
Education Policy (NEP) 2020, be the exemplar schools, and also offer benchmarking 
leadership to other schools in the neighbourhood. Presently, there are 19 PM SHRI schools 
functional in the district of Balrampur (including 1 Kendriya Vidyalaya and 1 Navodaya 
Vidyalaya) and 13 PM SHRI in the district of Shrawasti (including 1 Kendriya Vidyalaya 
and 1 Navodaya Vidyalaya).

Measures to Curb Air Pollution in Chandrapur 
 
3656. SMT. DHANORKAR PRATIBHA SURESH 
  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of air quality in Chandrapur, Maharashtra city which has 
been recorded in the 'moderate to polluted' category for 26 out of 30 days in the month of April 
due to which the respiratory diseases are increasing among the Citizens; 
(b) the details of concrete steps taken by the Government and the quantum of funds sanctioned by 
the Union Government so far for improving the quality of Chandrapur city under the National 
Clean Air Programme; 
(c) the details of strict actions being taken by the Government to make it mandatory for local 
thermal power plants and other industries in Chandrapur to install state-of-the-art pollution control 
technology;  
(d) whether the Union Government proposes to appoint a special environmental task force to 
monitor quality in real-time and reduce the concentration of particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5) 
in coal mines and industrial corridor areas; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): Air quality of Chandrapur city was recorded as Good during April 2026, comprising 03 
Satisfactory days (AQI: 51-100) and 27 Moderate days (AQI: 101-200).  To provide better air 
quality in urban areas, the Government has launched the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) 
as a long-term, time-bound, national level strategy to address air pollution in 130 Non-Attainment 
and million plus cities/urban agglomerations including Chandrapur. Emission Inventory and 
Source Apportionment Study for Chandrapur has been conducted by IIT Bombay and NEERI for 
identification of key sources of pollution. City Action Plan for Chandrapur City has been prepared 
for prioritization of various air pollution reduction measures to address various sources of air 
pollution such as road dust, solid waste management, vehicular emissions, construction activities 
and industrial pollution.  
Air quality performance linked grant of ₹ 18.25 crore has been released to Chandrapur city during 
FY 2019-20 till 2025-26 to implement air quality improvement measures as part of City action 
plan. 

NCAP is implemented and monitored through three tier institutional structure by involving 
Central, State and city level Departments and stakeholders. This is backed by regular review and 
monitoring by Committees at various levels including DISHA Committee. 
Comprehensive Environment Pollution Index (CEPI) for industrial areas is monitored by CPCB. 
During 2018, the CEPI score of Chandrapur Industrial area was 76.41 and categorized as 
Critically Polluted Area (CPA). During 2020, the Action Plan was prepared and submitted by 
Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) for improvement of environmental quality in 
Chandrapur Industrial area. 
Further, CPCB developed CEPI Action Plan Review portal for monitoring the progress of Action 
plan of CPA and SPA area. As reported by the MPCB on the said portal, the CEPI score of 
Chandrapur Industrial Area was 60.72 during the July, 2025 (Pre-monsoon period) and has moved 
from Critically Polluted Area to Severely Polluted Area. 
In addition, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has notified 
“Standards for Emission or Discharge of Environmental Pollutants from various Industries” under 
Schedule-I of the Environment Protection Rules, 1986 including Thermal Power Plants. The 
general standards as notified under Schedule-VI of the Environment Protection Rules, 1986 are 
applicable where specific standards are not available for the industrial sectors.  
For strengthening real time monitoring and effective compliance through self-regulatory 
mechanism, CPCB directed 17 categories of highly polluting industries to install Online 
Continuous Emission Monitoring System (OCEMS). 
As per the Environment Impact Assessment Notification 2006, all new projects or activities listed 
in the Schedule to the notification as well as the Expansion, modernisation or any change in the 
product mix or raw material mix in existing projects or activities including Thermal Power Plants 
and Coal mines, listed in the Schedule to the notification, resulting in capacity beyond the 
threshold limits specified for the concerned sector in the schedule are required to obtain prior 
Environmental Clearance (EC). The process of grant of EC, inter alia, involves preparation of a 
comprehensive Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Report as well as Environmental 
Management Plan addressing the environmental concerns related to the project inter-alia provide 
for appropriate mitigation measures including installation of pollution control devices. Further, 
Consent to Operate issued by State Pollution Control Board/Pollution Control Committee 
prescribes for implementation of pollution control measures including installing appropriate 
pollution control equipment.

GIRLS TRAINED UNDER NAVYA 
  
3657.  SHRI B K PARTHASARATHI: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)        the details regarding the number of girls trained under the NAVYA (Nurturing 
Aspirations through Vocational training for Young Adolescent Girls) programme, State/UT -
wise; 
(b)       whether the Government proposes to expand the NAVYA programme to cover 
Aspirational Districts beyond the 27 districts already covered; 
(c)        if so, the details regarding the target districts, timeline and resources planned for 
expansion; and 
(d)       the measures taken by the Government to monitor and evaluate the impact of NAVYA 
on skill development, employability and economic participation of adolescent girls?  
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)  Under Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls 
(NAVYA) programme 1,060 girls have been trained from 15 States/UTs . Details are provided 
at Annexure. 
(b) and (c) The Government has decided to expand the NAVYA programme to 100 aspirational 
districts across the country with effect from 27 May 2026. 
(d)       NAVYA programme is being implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0). The programme focuses on empowering trained candidates to pursue 
diverse career pathways by providing industry-relevant skill courses with embedded On-the-Job 
Training (OJT). Under NAVYA, special emphasis is placed on training in futuristic job roles, 
along with a mandatory Holistic Development Module covering digital literacy, financial literacy, 
career readiness, and entrepreneurship orientation etc. These interventions enhance the 
employability, economic participation, and overall career preparedness of adolescent girls. 
The Government monitors and evaluates the implementation and outcomes of the Nurturing 
Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls (NAVYA) programme 

through a robust monitoring framework under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY). The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) is leveraged for real -time tracking of beneficiary 
registration, attendance, training progress, certification and other key perf ormance indicators. 
Regular review meetings are conducted with Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), State Skill 
Development Missions (SSDMs) and other stakeholders to assess progress and address 
implementation-related issues. 
Further, the Ministry has advised State Skill Development Missions (SSDMs) to facilitate 
placement and apprenticeship opportunities for certified candidates through industry linkages 
and employer outreach, with a view to enhancing their employability and s upporting their 
economic participation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3658 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
DNA Sequencing Facility at Wildlife Institute of India 
 
3658. SHRI SUKANTA KUMAR PANIGRAHI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has strengthened technology-based wildlife conservation systems 
through the establishment of the Next-Generation DNA Sequencing (NGS) facility and digital 
databases at the Wildlife Institute of India; 
(b) if so, the manner in which advanced genetic research and forensic capabilities are aiding 
biodiversity protection, disease surveillance and curbing illegal wildlife trade; 
(c) the current status, nationwide outcomes and public participation milestones achieved under the 
'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign for large-scale afforestation and for social auditing; and 
(d) the details of institutional mechanisms and digital portals established to ensure survival 
assessment, monitoring and long-term maintenance of plantations? 
 
         ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) and (b): Advanced Sequencing and Automation Infrastructure has been installed in the Wildlife 
Institute of India, Dehradun, an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change. Next-generation sequencing facility provides faster genetic analysis thereby 
improving research in species conservation, forensic investigation of illegal wildlife related articles, 
disease surveillance, ecological and evolutionary studies, and evidence based biodiversity protection 
and population monitoring across the country. 
 
(c) and (d): The Government has launched the nationwide campaign ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ to 
encourage citizens to plant trees as a tribute to their mothers and promote mass participation in tree 
plantation activities. Tree plantation is also undertaken across sectors by various Central 
Ministries/Departments, State/UT Governments, NGOs, private sector entities, institutions and other 
stakeholders. ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign recorded a total of 291 Crore saplings planted since 
its launch in  June 2024. This campaign employs Meri LiFE portal, a real-time digital platform to 
facilitate recording and tracking of plantation-related activities. Monitoring of plantations by the State 
Governments follow a multi-tier mechanism, including field inspections, inter-circle verification by 
concerned State officials, submission of physical and financial progress reports, geo-tagged 
photographs and kml files, and third-party audits, wherever applicable. Awareness activities  for 
citizen are also undertaken to promote post-plantation care and maintenance of saplings.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3659 
TO BE ANSWERED ON Monday, August 10, 2026/ 19 Shravana, 1948 (Saka) 
 
Safeguarding India's Fiscal Stability 
 
3659.  Smt. Pratima Mondal: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has developed any contingency framework to safeguard 
India's fiscal stability, exports and investment flows against prolonged external shocks arising 
from global tariff disputes, supply -chain realignments and geopolitical conflicts, if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has put in place any safeguards to ensure that tax 
compliance becomes simpler and more predictable for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs), in view of the expanding tax base through greater digitalisation and formalisation, 
if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the impact of declining 
household financial savings and the sharp rise in retail partici pation in equity and derivative 
markets on household financial stability, if so, the findings thereof along with the measures 
being considered to strengthen investor protection and financial literacy? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDAHRY) 
 
(a): The Government follows a coordinated, multi -pronged approach to safeguard fiscal 
stability, exports and investment flows against external geopolitical uncertainties. Fiscal 
buffers, including the newly constituted Economic S tabilisation Fund, will provide the fiscal 
space to effectively respond to global headwinds and unforeseen events with significant fiscal 
implications. 
To support industry  and exports , measures such as the RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics 
Intervention for Export Facilitation) Scheme, Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool, restoration of 
RoDTEP benefits, targeted customs duty relief and the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee 
Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 have been introduced. The Government is also strengthening trade 
resilience through Free Trade Agreements and Comprehensive Economic 
Partnership/Cooperation Agreements, while an investor -friendly FDI policy continues to 
attract long-term investment. These efforts are complemented by measures of the Reserve Bank 
of India to streng then external sector resilience  and attract foreign investment  through 
liberalisation of the External Commercial Borrowing framework, facilitation of foreign 
investment and promotion of local currency settlement.  

 (b): The Government has put in place several measures to simplify and make tax compliance 
more predictable for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. Under the Goods and Services Tax 
(GST) regime, exemption from registration has been provided to small suppliers up to the 
prescribed turnover thresholds. Eligible taxpayers may opt for the Composition Levy Scheme 
with concessional tax rates and simplified compliance requirements.  Further, businesses with 
turnover up to ₹5 crore are permitted to furnish GST returns on a quarterly basis while paying 
the monthly tax.  
Direct tax compliance has been simplified through digital initiatives such as e-filing of income 
tax returns, pre-filled returns, faceless assessment and digital taxpayer services. The Income -
tax Act, 2025 also provides simplified presumptive  taxation schemes with higher turnover 
thresholds for businesses undertaking digital transactions, thereby reducing compliance 
requirements. 
(c): As per data published by the RBI, net household financial savings increased from ₹13.9 
lakh crore in 2022-23 to ₹21.5 lakh crore in 2025-26. The retail participation in the securities 
market has also increased significantly in the recent years , with the total number of demat 
accounts rising to about 22.5 crore by end -March 2026. The RBI's Financial Stability Repor t, 
June 2026, indicates that the household sector remains resilient, with improving borrower 
profiles and healthy repayment performance.  
To strengthen investor protection, the Securities and Exchange Board of India has put in place 
a robust risk management and surveillance framework and introduced regulatory measures in 
the equity derivatives segment during 2024 –25 to curb excessive speculation and strengthen 
market integrity. 
The Securities and Exchange Board of India, in collaboration with Marke t Infrastructure 
Institutions, namely Stock Exchanges and Depositories, conducts investor awareness 
programmes through physical and digital platforms. During 2025–26, it, along with the Market 
Infrastructure Institutions, conducted 44,834 investor awarenes s programmes across 774 
districts in 36 States and Union Territories. 
The Reserve Bank of India has also undertaken measures to strengthen customer and investor 
protection, including regulation of financial product marketing by regulated entities, a 
'Verified' badge for stock trading applications of Securities and Exchange Board of India -
registered entities, and Project SUDARSAN, an artificial intelligence-based platform to detect 
fraudulent online investment activities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3660 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Jawahar Navodaya and Kendriya Vidyalaya in Telangana 
 
3660. Shri Godam Nagesh:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that there are districts in Telangana not covered 
under the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (JNV) scheme and if so, the details thereof along 
with the timeline for establishing JNVs in those districts; and  
 
(b) whether the Government has received any proposals for sanctioning new Kendriya 
Vidyalayas (KVs) in Telangana and if so, the action taken thereon along with the timeline 
for sanctioning the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs in uncovered districts 
is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned State 
Government/UT administration to make available requisite suitable land, free of cost, for 
construction of the permanent building and making available required temporary building, 
free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is constructed. Sanction and 
opening of new NVs depends on approval by the competent authority as per extant 
procedures. At present, 16 NVs have been sanctioned in 16 districts in the State of 
Telangana. District-wise list of sanctioned NVs is Annexed. 
Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs are 
opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable Central 
Government Employees including Defence & Para-military personnel, Central 
Autonomous Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central Institute of 
Higher Learning (IHL) by providing a common programme of education throughout the 
country. Proposals for opening of new KVs may be sponsored by Ministries or 
Departments of the Government of India / State Governments / Union Territories (UTs) 
Administrations, with commitment to provide requisite resources including land and 
temporary accommodation for setting up a new KV as per norms. The Government of 
India sanctioned 57 new KVs in October 2025, including 04 KVs in the State of Telangana. 
At present, 37 KVs are functional in the State of Telangana.

records.ls|LS18_S8_U_3661:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3661 
ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
Promotion of Digital Education in Jammu 
 
†3661. Shri Jugal Kishore:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) the steps taken by the Government to promote digital education in Jammu Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
(b) the details of the number of schools which have been equipped with digital facilities; 
(c) whether the Government has any special scheme to increase the availability of internet and 
digital resources in remote and hilly areas, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of long-term strategy of the Government to modernize the education system in 
future? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d): The Government has been promoting digital education in school education through 
various initiatives under Samagra Shiksha, in alignment with the objectives of the National 
Education Policy (NEP), 2020. Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to States and 
Union Territories (UTs), including the UT of Jammu & Kashmir, based on their Annual Work 
Plan and Budget (AWP&B), as approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation 
with the respective State/UT. The assistance supports the strengthening of Information and 
Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure, including ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms, in 
Government and Government-aided schools having classes VI to XII, including those located in 
rural, remote and hilly areas. 
To enhance digital connectivity and access to digital resources in remote and hilly areas, 
the Government has announced broadband connectivity to all Government Secondary Schools in 
rural areas under the BharatNet project in the Union Budget 2025. 
In addition, the Ministry implements digital education initiatives such as DIKSHA and PM 
eVidya to provide equitable access to quality digital learning resources. Digital Infrastructure for 
Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the national digital platform for school education, providing 
curriculum-aligned e-content, including QR-coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs), teacher 

resources and other learning materials. The platform supports both online and offline access, 
enabling learners to download content and continue learning without internet connectivity, thereby 
ensuring wider and equitable access to quality educational resources.  
PM eVidya, launched on 17th May, 2020 as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan, 
integrates digital, online and on-air education initiatives to enable multimode access to education 
across the country. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to contextualize, monitor and evaluate 
these initiatives, while NCERT provides continuous academic support and guidance. Further, 
ePathshala, developed by NCERT, provides free access to NCERT textbooks (Classes I to XII), 
audio-visual resources and teacher training modules through its website and mobile application, 
enabling learners and teachers to access educational content anytime and anywhere. 
As reported by the UT of Jammu & Kashmir, in the Jammu Lok Sabha Constituency, 711 
Government schools at the Elementary, Secondary and Senior Secondary levels have been 
approved for ICT Labs and further, 530 schools have been approved for Smart Classrooms. 
The long-term strategy of the Government is to modernize the school education system 
based on the NEP, 2020. Towards this, saturation of ICT labs, smart classrooms, science labs in 
Government Secondary Schools have been undertaken under Samagra Shiksha.

OIH           
       GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
                  MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
                 LOK SABHA 
                     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3662 
            TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
         Review of Environmental Clearance System 
 
3662. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is reviewing the existing system of Environmental Clearance; 
(b) if so, the main objectives thereof and the timeline set in this regard; 
(c) whether the Government has constituted groups related to environmental evaluation for 
consultation on matters pertaining to Environmental Clearance for major projects; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
        ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) and (b): The review and reform of the existing system of Environmental Clearance (EC) is 
a continuous process. The Ministry periodically reviews the legal, policy and administrative 
framework governing the EC process with a view to strengthening environmental governance 
while facilitating sustainable development. Such reviews are undertaken to ensure that the 
provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Environmental Impact Assessment 
(EIA) Notification, 2006, and the Rules, Notifications, Guidelines, Office Memoranda and 
other instructions issued thereunder remain responsive to emerging environmental challenges, 
operational requirements, judicial pronouncements, technological advancements and 
stakeholder feedback. Based on these reviews, the Ministry undertakes legislative and 
procedural reforms, including amendments to the EIA Notification, 2006, and issuance of 
appropriate guidelines and Office Memoranda, to enhance the efficiency, transparency and 
effectiveness of the EC process while ensuring environmental safeguards. 
 
(c) and (d): In accordance with the provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006, the Central 
Government has constituted sector-specific Expert Appraisal Committees (EACs) for appraisal 
of projects and activities requiring prior Environmental Clearance under the Schedule to the 
Notification. Such projects are required to undertake environmental impact assessment studies 
covering site-specific environmental aspects, including land use, water resources, air quality, 
ecology, energy, waste management and suitable mitigation measures. Further, Public 
Consultation, wherever applicable, is conducted to provide the likely affected persons and other 
stakeholders an opportunity to raise their views, concerns and suggestions regarding the 
project. A final Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report, incorporating the issues raised 
during public consultation, together with the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and 
other required documents as submitted by the Project Proponent, is appraised by the sector-

specific EACs at the Central level. Based on the recommendations of the EAC, the proposal is 
considered by the Ministry for grant or otherwise of Environmental Clearance in accordance 
with the provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006.

records.ls|LS18_S8_U_3663:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
    MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3663 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2026 
 
 
FORMULATION OF NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR CULTURAL DIPLOMACY 
 
 
3663. Shri Jagdambika Pal: 
         Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to formulate a National Framework for Cultural 
Diplomacy to strengthen India's global cultural presence and civilizational outreach;  
 
(b) whether the proposed framework envisages expanding cultural exchanges, international 
festivals, museum collaborations, heritage exhibitions, academic partnerships and digital cultural 
platforms; 
 
(c) whether the framework is proposed to support India's diplomatic engagement through 
greater participation in multilateral cultural initiatives and people-to-people exchanges; and 
 
(d)      if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
   MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d) The Ministry of Culture promotes India's cultural relations with other countries 
through the Global Engagement Scheme (GES), an umbrella scheme aimed at strengthening 
India's international cultural engagement and cultural diplomacy. The Scheme seeks to promote 
India's civilizational heritage, cultural diversity and contemporary creative traditions through 
structured bilateral and multilateral cooperation. It supports cultural exchanges, heritage 
conservation, documentation, capacity building and engagement with international cultural 
organizations. 
The Global Engagement Scheme comprises four components, namely the International Cultural 
Exchange Programme (ICEP), Project Mausam, Brihattar Bharat and the Scheme for 
Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India. Under 

the International Cultural Exchange Programme (ICEP), the Ministry undertakes Festivals of 
India, cultural exchanges, deputation of artists and cultural troupes, and implements Cultural 
Exchange Programmes (CEPs), Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and other bilateral 
cultural cooperation mechanisms. The Ministry currently has valid Cultural Exchange 
Programmes (CEPs) with 98 countries, providing an institutional framework for cooperation in 
the fields of culture, museums, heritage, performing arts and other related sectors. The Scheme 
also facilitates India's participation in multilateral cultural forums, including BRICS, G20, SCO 
and BIMSTEC. 
The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), an autonomous organisation under the 
Ministry of External Affairs, complements these initiatives by promoting India's cultural heritage 
and strengthening people-to-people contacts through its network of Indian Cultural Centres and 
cultural programmes abroad. ICCR actively projects India's diverse culture in foreign countries 
by facilitating artistic exchanges through the organisation of flagship international cultural 
festivals in India, where foreign artists are invited to perform. It also organises visual arts 
exhibitions, hosts Art Residencies to showcase India's rich civilizational heritage, and 
commemorates national and international occasions in foreign countries, including the 
International Day of Yoga.
