ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
  
AWARENESS PROGRAMMES FOR LIVESTOCK FARMERS 
 
3724: SHRI RAJESH NARANBHAI CHUDASAMA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has recently organised a virtual awareness program for livestock farmers in 
country through Common Service Centres (CSCs); 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with aims and objectives of organising said program; 
(c) the total number of livestock farmers participated in this event from across country, State-wise; 
(d) whether any initiatives are being implemented by the Government to promote scientific breeding 
and improve fodder quality in the country, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the other steps/measures taken/being taken by the Government to create awareness among 
livestock farmers regarding diseases of livestock, vaccination to livestock breed improvement, 
zoonotic disease control and sanitation practices? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
 
(a) to (b): Yes Sir. The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying  (DAHD), Government 
of India, has organised five virtual awareness programs for livestock farmers in the country 
through Common Service Centers (CSCs) during  the Financial Year 2025-2026. Aims and 
Objectives of the awareness programmes through Common Services Centres is for creating 
awareness of schemes of Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying and to serve as a 
platform for knowledge sharing, policy awareness, and promoting entrepreneurship, 
highlighting the vital role of livestock farmers in rural development.  
The details of the five Virtual awareness programmes conducted through CSCs during 2025-
2026 on the following topics were as under: 

 
i. “Improving Livestock Productivity" organized on 11th July 2025 through 2000 CSCs location. 
ii.  “Enhancing Livestock Productivity” organized on 23rd July 2025 through 4000 CSCs location  
iii. “Enhancing Livestock Productivity” organized on 20th August 2025 through 2 000 CSCs 
location. 
iv.  “Ethno Veterinary Medicine (EVM) for livestock farmers” on the occasion of 10th Ayurveda 
Day was organized on 23rd September 2025 through 2000 CSCs location.  
v.  “Animal Husbandry and Animal Welfare Awareness Month” organized on 5th February 2026 
through 2500 CSCs location.  
(c) A total 6,41,250 livestock farmers participated in five virtual awareness programmes conducted 
through 12,500 CSCs locations across the country  during 2025 -2026. State wise details of 
participation of livestock farmers in the five virtual awareness programmes is annexed at Table 1 to 
5. 
(d) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying is supporting the States/Union Territories  
(UTs) to promote scientific breeding and improve fodder quality through the implementation of 
following schemes:  
1. Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM): To supplement the efforts of the States and UTs in promoting 
scientific breeding, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India  (GoI) 
is implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since December 2014 for development and 
conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population and enhancement of 
milk production and productivity thereby making milk production more remunerative to farmers.  
2. National Livestock Mission (NLM): In order to promote scientific breeding and improve fodder 
quality in the country, the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India is 
implementing the scheme of National Livestock Mi ssion since the financial year 2014 -15. The 
scheme of National Livestock Mission (NLM) aims towards employment generation, 
entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased 
production of meat, goat milk, egg and  wool under the umbrella scheme Development 
Programme. The concept of NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the 
forward and backward linkage for the produce available at the unorganized sector and to link with 
the organized sector. 
 
The Sub Mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry of realigned National Livestock 
Mission aims to bring sharp focus on genetic breed improvement of sheep, goat, pig, camel, 
donkey, horse and mule by providing the financial assistance to the State Governments for breed 
conservation and establishment of breed improvement infrastructure. 
 
The Department of Animal Husbandry  & Dairying, Government of India  (GoI) under the sub 
mission on Feed and Fodder Development aims towards strengthening of fodder  seed chain to 
improve availability of certified fodder seed required for fodder production and encouraging 
entrepreneurs for establishment of fodder Block/Hay Bailing/Silage Making Units through 
incentivisation. 

(e) In order to complement and supplement the efforts of the State and UTs to create awareness 
among livestock farmers regarding diseases of livestock, vaccination, breed improvement, zoonotic 
disease control and sanitation practices, the Department has made awareness generation as integral 
part of the various schemes and details are given as under: 
i. Under Rashtriya Gokul Mission, fertility camps, milk yield competition, calf rallies, farmers 
training programme, seminars and workshop, conclaves etc. to create a wareness among the 
farmers about importance of indigenous bovine breeds have been organized across the 
country. 
ii. Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP ) S cheme, financial 
assistance is provided to the States/UTs for training and awareness on Good Animal 
Husbandry Practices, Biosecurity/Sanitary measures, vaccination against animal diseases, 
disease surveillance and monitoring and capacity building which supports animal health and 
productivity. 
iii. Under National Livestock Mission,  in order to create awareness among livestock farmers, 
the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying,  Government of India  under the Sub 
Mission on Innovation and Extension is carrying out extension services including promotional 
activities for animal husbandry and schemes, seminars, conferences, demonstration activities 
and other Information, Education, and Communication ( IEC) activities for awareness 
generation. The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India  has 
observed "Animal Husbandry and Animal Welfare Awareness Month” from 14th January to 
13th February every year, with the goal of raising awareness about the importance of modern 
animal husbandry practices and improving the welfare of livestock across the country. 
 
iv. The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying conducted a National Workshop on 
“Poultry Disease Free Compartments: World Orga nisation for Animal Health ( WOAH) 
Framework & Indian Perspective” on 8 May 2026 at Hyderabad to strengthen capacity among 
State Veterinary Services, research institutions, the poultry industry and farmers for 
establishing and maintaining disease free poultry compartments. “Mastitis Awareness Month 
– June 2026” campaign  was also conducted where States /UTs organized farmer awareness 
camps, training programmes, demonstrations, and IEC dissemination in local languages, 
thereby strengthening livestock health awareness, disease control, and clean milk production.  
v. In addition to above, t he Department enhanc es outreach  for creating awareness amongst 
livestock farmers through collaboration with agencies like Press Information Bureau (PIB) , 
Prasar Bharati and Central Bureau of Communication, running media and social campaigns, 
organizing exhibitions, National Milk Day, Pashu Melas and supporting state governments in 
extension services. During vaccination drives, Department broadcasts TV and radio spots on 
various platforms, including YouTube and social media. Department develops and distributes 
IEC materials such as booklets and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to raise awareness 
on livestock health, vaccination, breed improvement, zoonotic disease control and sanitation 
practices. 
vi. Further, with an objective to recognize and encourage all individuals like Farmer s rearing 
indigenous animals, AI Technicians and Dairy cooperative societies / Milk Producer 
Company/Dairy farmers Producers Organizations working in livestock sector, National Gopal 
Ratna Award is also given by the Department every year.

  ANSWERED ON 11/08/2026 
 
INTEGRATED MASTER PLAN FOR RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
3726. Smt. Sandhya Ray: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has formulated any national policy to 
prepare an integrated master plan for rural infrastructure and 
livelihood development for each Lok Sabha Constituency of the 
country; 
(b)  if so, the details of the projects approved, State and district-
wise including Bhind and Datia; and 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to implement an annual 
evaluation system of rural development outcomes of the 
system, if so, the details thereof, district level? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
(a) & (b): Under its broad policy framework, Ministry of Rural 
Development (MoRD) has been undertaking various targeted 
interventions for integrated and sustainable development rural areas 
of the country. With the main focus on infrastructure development, 
increasing livelihood opportunities, empowering rural women and 
expanding livelihood opportunities, MoRD is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana(PMGSY), Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for 
Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) and Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) 
across the country including Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya 
Pradesh. As per the implementation framework of the programmes, 
States/UTs are conceiving the project proposals for infrastructure 
including roads and sustainable assets, identification of beneficiary, 
generation of demand for employment, livelihood programmes, 
keeping in view the actual requirement of interventions for improving 
the quality of life of rural population. The above programmes are 

Page 2 of 2 
 
implemented in convergence with various central and state schemes 
to optimize the pace of rural development in the country. However, at 
present, there is no proposal in this Ministry for an integrated master 
plan for rural infrastructure and livelihood development for each Lok 
Sabha Constituency. 
(c): MoRD has evolved a comprehensive multilevel and multi format 
system of periodic assessment and review of progress and outcome 
of its rural development schemes, through Performance Review 
Committee Meetings, National Level Monitors (NLMs), Area Officers 
Schemes, Common Review Mission, Mid-Term Review, Labour Budget 
meetings, Labour Budget Revision meetings, Programme Review 
meetings, Concurrent Evaluation and Impact Assessment Studies. 
Specific reviews of States/UTs are also undertaken from time to time 
and action is taken on the basis of their findings. In addition, MoRD 
constitutes District Level Development Coordination and Monitoring 
Committees (DISHA) under the chairpersonship of the respective 
Members of Parliament to foster better coordination among elected 
representatives of Parliament, State Legislatures, and Local 
Governments (Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies) to 
ensure the effective and timely implementation of key Central Sector 
and Centrally Sponsored Schemes including the 
schemes/programmes of MoRD at district level.

(b)  the details of the total central financial funds disbursed and the

(b): The details of the total central share of the programme  funds 
disbursed and the expenditure incurred including matching state 
share for constructing all-weather rural roads during the last one 
year, State-wise including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and 
Andhra Pradesh are given in Annexure-I.  
 
(c): Unlike PMGSY-I, which targeted single all-weather connectivity 
to unconnected habitations, PMGSY-III focuses on consolidating 
existing Through Routes and Major Rural Links to facilitate seamless 
access to key socio-economic growth centers. Nationally, PMGSY-III 
has facilitated connectivity to over 6.96 lakh socio-economic 
facilities including 1.38 lakh agricultural markets (GrAMs), 1.46 lakh 
educational institutions and 82,806 medical facilities. 
 
State-wise mapping of candidate roads under PMGSY-III 
includes routes connecting major market centers, educational 
institutions and healthcare hubs. The details of facilities connected 
across the country including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar 
and Andhra Pradesh are monitored digitally on the Online 
Management, Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS) and can 
be viewed @ (https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in > other reports > facility 
reports. The State wise details of habitations provided all weather 
road connectivity under PMGSY-I are given in Annexure-II. 
 
(d): Quality inspections are conducted by independent National 
Quality Monitors (NQMs) who identify road construction works 
requiring improvement or rectification, which are graded as 
"Unsatisfactory". State Governments are mandated to rectify 
identified defects through the contractor before final bill clearance. 
The State and District-wise abstract of NQM gradings (including for 
Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh) is 
dynamically maintained on the OMMAS portal at 
https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in (Quality > 3rd Tier (National Quality 
Monitor) Reports  > Grading Abstract.  
 
(e): Under PMGSY, maintenance of roads is the responsibility of the 
State Governments. However, the Government of India has put in 
place a structured contractual, financial and digital monitoring 
framework to ensure long-term maintenance of the assets created 
under the programme.  The following steps have been taken: 

Page 4 of 7 
 
1. Mandatory five-year maintenance obligation: PMGSY 
construction contracts provide for a five-year Defect Liability 
Period (DLP) from the date of completion, during which the 
same contractor is responsible for routine maintenance and for 
keeping the road and associated structures in 
serviceable/defect-free condition. The contractor is required to 
rectify defects within the period specified by the engineer. 
2. Performance-based maintenance through eMARG: Maintenance 
during the five-year DLP is monitored through eMARG 
(Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads) on the principles of 
Performance-Based Maintenance Contracts (PBMC). Contractor 
performance is assessed against prescribed service levels 
rather than merely the quantity of maintenance work executed. 
PIU inspections, geo-tagged photographs, performance 
evaluation, bill processing and payments are carried out 
through the platform. 
3. Payment linked with maintenance performance: Under eMARG, 
maintenance payments are linked to the Performance 
Evaluation (PE) of the road. Where the performance score is 
below 80 per cent, payment is not released, while for scores 
between 80 and 100 payment is made corresponding to the 
performance achieved. This provides a direct financial 
incentive to contractors to maintain prescribed standards. 
4. Regular inspection and accountability: Contractors are required 
to inspect roads under maintenance regularly and report the 
condition/rectification of defects. PIU officials independently 
assess maintenance performance through eMARG using geo-
tagged photographs. The system also uses AI-assisted scrutiny 
of photographs to flag possible inconsistencies in performance 
evaluation, thereby, strengthening transparency and 
accountability. 
5. Post-DLP maintenance: To ensure sustainability beyond the 
initial five-year DLP, a Post-DLP module of eMARG has also been 
introduced for monitoring subsequent maintenance. The 
Standard Bidding Document for Post-DLP maintenance provides 
for Performance-Based Maintenance for a period of not less 
than five years, with performance security and provisions for 
recovery/penalty where the contractor fails to undertake the 
stipulated maintenance. 
6. State maintenance policies and fund monitoring: States/UTs are 
required to provide adequate maintenance funds and their 
maintenance commitments and expenditure are monitored 
through OMMAS/eMARG. A Rural Roads Maintenance Policy 
framework has also been provided to States/UTs for adoption of 
appropriate State-specific maintenance policies. 

Page 5 of 7 
 
  
These provisions are applicable to PMGSY works across the 
implementing States/UTs including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, 
Bihar and Andhra Pradesh.

AVERAGE MONTHLY INCOME OF AGRICULTURAL HOUSEHOLD 
 
3732. SHRI BALASHOWRY VALLABHANENI: 
 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare(कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण मंýी)  be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the average monthly income of agricultural 
household in the State of Andhra Pradesh as per the latest available agricultural year is not 
even Rs. 900 per month; 
(b) the details of the average monthly income of agricultural households in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh as of March, 2024; 
(c) whether the Government is also aware that the percentage of agricultural households 
indebted has also gone up from 92.9% in 2012-13 to 93.2% in 2018-19; 
(d) the percentage of agriculture households indebted in 2024-25 and 2025-26; and 
(e) the manner in which the Government ensures that agricultural household income goes 
up and indebtedness comes down to 50% from the present 90%+? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
(कृिष एवं िकसान कÐयाण मंýी) (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (d):The average monthly income & indebtedness of agricultural households in the 
country is periodically estimated through the “Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of 
Agricultural Households”, conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of 
Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). As per the latest Situation Assessment 
Survey (January, 2019 – December, 2019) conducted by MoSPI (through NSS 77th round) 
in the rural areas of the country, the average monthly income per agricultural household in 
the State of Andhra Pradesh is Rs. 10,480.  
As per the last two Situation Assessment Surveys conducted by NSO, the percentage 
of indebted agricultural households in Andhra Pradesh in 2012-13 and 2018-19 are 92.9 % 
and 93.2 % respectively. Since the last survey conducted in 2019, the extent of average 
monthly income per agricultural household and the percentage of indebted agricultural 
households for the years 2024-25 and 2025-26 are not available. 
(e): Agriculture is a state subject. Government supports the efforts of States through 
appropriate policy measures, budgetary support and various schemes/programmes to 
enhance the welfare of farmers and make agriculture more remunerative across the country. 
The Government has implemented several policies and developmental programmes to 
increase agricultural productivity, reduce the cost of cultivation, promote crop diversification, 
ensure remunerative returns and provide income support to farmers. These initiatives cover 
the entire spectrum of agriculture including credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, 
crops including horticulture, seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, 
farmer collectives, irrigation, extension activities, procurement of crops etc.  

To improve credit access over the long term, the government is implementing a 100% 
centrally funded Central Sector Scheme known as the Modified lnterest Subvention Scheme 
(MISS) across various States/UTs in India. This scheme aims to provide concessional 
interest rates on short-term agricultural loans obtained by farmers through Kisan Credit 
Cards (KCC) for their working capital requirements. Due to KCC-MISS scheme, access to 
easy and affordable credit has increased significantly to farmers to meet their operational 
needs. Under this scheme, farmers receive KCC loans at a subsidized interest rate of 7%. 
To facilitate this, an upfront interest subvention (IS) of 1.5% is provided to financial 
institutions. Additionally, farmers who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% Prompt 
Repayment Incentive (PRI), effectively reducing the interest rate to 4% per annum. From 
2014-15 onwards, the overall flow of institutional agricultural credit has increased from ₹8.5 
lakh crore to over ₹28 lakh crore during 2025-26 (provisional) while, the annual institutional 
credit flow to Small and Marginal Farmers has increased from ₹3.47 lakh crore to ₹14.77 
lakh crore during 2024-25. 
 
Further, to provide assured income support and reduce financial stress among small 
and marginal farmers, the Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman 
Nidhi (PM-KISAN) Scheme, a 100% Central Sector Scheme. Under the scheme, eligible 
farmer families receive income support of ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments through 
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Under PM-KISAN scheme, the Government has disbursed 
over Rs 4.47 lakh Cr. through 23 installments since inception. 
  Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY) provides comprehensive risk insurance 
against crop damage from pre-sowing to post-harvest for crops and area notified by the 
concerned State Government. All willing farmers, including sharecroppers, tenant and 
women farmers are eligible to enrol under the scheme. Since inception of the scheme in 
2016 till 2025-26, claims amounting to Rs. 2.02 lakh crore have been settled under PMFBY, 
providing safety net to farmers against crop losses.  
Additionally, Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and 
other Commercial crops with a minimum return of 50 percent over cost of production from 
2018-19 onwards. The several Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes are being 
implemented by Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is given in the Annexure.

3733.     SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of funds sanctioned and utilised under the School Safety 
Programme, State-wise and year-wise; 
 
(b) the number of schools covered, teachers trained, and students sensitised 
under the programme in last five years; 
 
(c) whether any evaluation of the programme has been conducted and if so, 
the details and findings thereof; 
 
(d) the details of school disaster management plans prepared, mock drills 
conducted and structural and non-structural safety measures implemented 
under the School Safety Programme  during the last five years, State -wise 
and year-wise; 
 
(e) Whether the School Safety Programme has been coordinated or 
integrated with the  National School Safety Programme of the National 
Disaster Management Authority and with  State Disaster Management 
Authorities; and 
 
(f) if so, the details thereof, including guidelines issued, training modules 
developed and steps taken to mainstream school safety into the education 
system? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a): National School Safety Programme (NSSP) implemented by National 
Disaster   Management   Authority  (NDMA)  was  a  demonstration  project  

 
-2-

approved in June 2011 with total outlay of ₹48.47 crore. It was implemented 
in 8,600 schools across 43 districts in 22 States/ Union Territories(UT) and 
concluded in March 2019. State/UT -wise and year -wise details of funds 
released, and utilized are given in the Annexure.  
 
(b) Since the NSSP concluded in March 2019, no schools, teachers or 
students were covered under that project during the last five years. NDMA 
has, however, undertaken separate school -safety awareness initiatives 
during 2025–26. These include campaigns in 2,082 schools in NCT of Delhi, 
reaching approximately 12.02 lakh students and 58,570 teachers, and pilot 
programmes in 1,793 schools across six districts in six States, reaching 
approximately 2.60 lakh students and 54,000 teachers. In addition, National 
Disaster Response Force ( NDRF) has conducted approximately 13,000 
School Safety Programmes benefiting over 43 lakh students. Teachers are 
also sensitized during these programmes to strengthen disaster 
preparedness and response at the school level. 
 
(c) The NSSP was evaluated by  United Nations Development Programme  
(UNDP). The evaluation recommended extension of the programme up to 31 
December 2015.

implemented in collabor ation with the then Ministry of Human Resource

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3734  
ANSWERED ON 11.08.2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF SCHEMES BY PRIs 
  
3734. DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of administrative, financial and 
governance challenges faced by Panchayati Raj Institutions in implementing Central and State 
Government schemes; 
  
(b) the details of capacity-building programmes, digital governance initiatives and training 
interventions undertaken for elected representatives and Panchayat officials during the last five 
years; 
  
(c) whether the Government has evaluated the effectiveness of e-Gram Swaraj and other digital 
platforms in improving transparency, accountability and service delivery at the grassroots level; 
  
(d) if so, the measures taken to address staff shortages, technical capacity gaps and delays in 
implementation of development projects at the Panchayat level; and 
  
(e) whether any special initiatives have been sanctioned for strengthening governance capacity 
and digital service delivery in Panchayats of Karnataka, including Davanagere district, and the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a): Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj implements the Centrally Sponsored Scheme 
of the revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) for capacity building and training of 
the elected representatives of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). This Ministry has 
undertaken an assessment of the impact of institutional and capacity gaps in local planning, 
implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes through an independent third-party evaluation 
of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), 
conducted by the Institute of Rural Management Anand (IRMA). The evaluation assessed the 
design, implementation strategies, outcomes, and impact of capacity-building interventions 
undertaken for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). The findings indicate that structured, multi-
layered capacity-building interventions, including classroom and thematic training, exposure 

2 
 
visits and digital learning, have significantly enhanced the capacities of PRIs in Gram Panchayat 
Development Plan (GPDP) preparation, implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes, digital 
governance, financial management and citizen participation.  
  
(b): This Ministry has implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the Revamped 
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the objective of 
supporting Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives 
(ERs), Panchayat officials and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby 
enabling Gram Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs. Under the scheme, 
capacity-building support is provided to elected representatives, Panchayat officials, and other 
stakeholders of Panchayats under different categories, viz. basic orientation and refresher 
programmes, thematic interventions, specialized training, and Panchayat Development Plan-
related programmes, etc.The scheme also supports exposure visits to facilitate experiential 
learning and replication of best practices for strengthening Panchayat governance, as well as 
development of training modules and materials,etc. A total of 1,92,17,145 elected representatives 
and Panchayat functionaries have been trained under this scheme during the last five years. 
  
This Ministry has taken several initiatives for governance, capacity building and digital 
service delivery in Panchayats of all States/Union Territories (UTs). 
  
To enhance skills and knowledge, a major step has been taken to build capacity and train 
elected representatives and Panchayat officials through Institutes of excellence such as IIMs/IITs 
under the Leadership/Management Development Program (MDP). Under the Specialised Module 
of MDP, 3,490 participants have been trained since year 2024 till 10.07.2026 
  
This Ministry in collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad, has also developed a training 
module on Own Source Revenue (OSR) to strengthen the financial self-reliance of Gram 
Panchayats. Under the Specialised Module of OSR, 2,75,893 participants have been trained since 
year 2025 till 10.07.2026. 
  
The Ministry has launched a Specialized Training Module as a part of “Shashkta 
Panchayat Netri Abhiyan” for the capacity building of Women Elected Representatives (WERs) 
of Panchayati Raj Institutions. Under the Specialised Module of WERs, 1,53,616 participants 
have been trained since year 2025 till 10.07.2026. 
  
This Ministry has developed the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) as a composite 
assessment framework to measure the performance of Gram Panchayats/Equivalent across nine 
themes aligned with the Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs). The Index 
intends to support the Gram Panchayat in the preparation of an evidence-based plan by 
formulating local actions through the convergence of funds & schemes.  
  
This Ministry has implemented the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under 
Revamped RGSA, which has significantly enhanced transparency, efficiency, and digital 
governance at the grassroots level. The eGramSwaraj application, developed as part of the e-
Panchayat MMP, has facilitated digital planning, accounting, monitoring, and online payments at 
the Panchayat level. The integration of eGramSwaraj with the Public Financial Management 

3 
 
System (PFMS) enables real-time payments to vendors and service providers, ensuring seamless 
fund flow and reducing delays. The Ministry has strengthened the e-GramSwaraj platform 
through integration with other national digital platforms. Integration with the Government e-
Marketplace (GeM) facilitates transparent, efficient and rule based procurement by Gram 
Panchayats.  
  
‘AuditOnline’, an application has been developed for online audits of Panchayat 
accounts and their financial management. AuditOnline for transparent auditing of Central 
Finance Commission funds utilization to strengthen financial management of Panchayats 
launched in April 2020.  
  
Furthermore, applications developed by this Ministry like Meri Panchayat have 
endeavoured to bring transparency in Panchayat Governance by making information on 
planning, activities and progress of works in Panchayat accessible to public. Similarly, 
Panchayat NIRNAY is an online application that aims at bringing transparency and better 
management in the conduct of Gram Sabhas by Panchayats. 
  
(c): Under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), the Ministry continuously reviews the 
implementation and utilisation of the e-Panchayat applications through system-generated reports, 
dashboards, periodic review meetings and interactions with States/UTs. These reviews facilitate 
identification of operational and technical issues relating to digital governance and support 
continuous enhancement of the e-Panchayat applications. Further, the Ministry has undertaken 
assessments of the digital governance initiatives implemented under the e-Panchayat Mission 
Mode Project (MMP) through an independent assessment carried out by the Institute of Rural 
Management Anand (IRMA), who has observed that the e-Panchayat initiative has strengthened 
transparency, accountability, planning, financial management, auditing and citizen participation 
in Panchayati Raj Institutions through digital platforms and emerging technologies. 
  
(d): “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List of Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operated through the respective 
State Panchayati Raj Acts. States have made their own Panchayati Raj Act, subject to the 
provisions of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, Panchayat related all matters, including 
measures taken to address staff shortages, technical capacity gaps and delays in implementation 
of development projects at the Panchayat level, etc., are the responsibility of the States/UTs. 
  
(e): The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has taken several initiatives for strengthening governance 
capacity and digital service delivery as highlighted in para-(b) above in respect to all States/UTs, 
including the State of Karnataka.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3737 
ANSWERED ON 11TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
ANIMAL HEALTHCARE SERVICES 
 
3737.  SHRI C N ANNADURAI:  
SHRI SELVAM G:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
 be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the major initiatives undertaken by the Government under the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and the 
Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) to promote livestock development and strengthen 
animal healthcare services in Tamil Nadu during the last five years; 
 
(b) the details of assistance provided to Tamil Nadu under the National Animal Disease Control Programme 
(NADCP), Assistance to States for Control of Animal Diseases (ASCAD), Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) and 
the strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals and Dispensaries during the said period;  
 
(c) the details of livestock vaccinated, Mobile Veterinary Units deployed and veterinary infrastructure strengthened 
in Tamil Nadu, district-wise;  
 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to improve disease surveill ance, livestock healthcare and breed 
productivity in the State; and 
 
 (e) whether the Government has any proposals to expand the coverage of these programmes and strengthen 
veterinary healthcare infrastructure in Tamil Nadu to enhance livestock productivity and farmers' income, if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
(a) The major initiatives undertaken by, Government of India (GOI)  under the National Livestock Mission 
(NLM) and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP)  to promote livestock development and 
strengthen animal healthcare services in Tamil Nadu during the last five years are as below:-  
i. 50% capital subsidy provided under NLM-EDP to individuals, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Self-
Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Farmer Cooperative Organisations (FCOs), and Section 
8 companies. The  NLM scheme focuses on Breed Development of Livestock & Poultry , Feed and Fodder 
development, Research & Development, Livestock Insurance and Extension.   
ii. 100% financial assistance is provided  under LHDCP to all the States/UTs for prevention of economically 
important livestock diseases namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants 
(PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is provided to 
States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritised activities such as vaccination against other livestock diseases, 
control o f emergent and exotic diseases,  strengthening of laboratory, disease surveillance, training and 
awareness.  
iii. Financial assistance is provided  to the State  of Tamil Nadu  on sharing basis for operation of 245 Mobile 
Veterinary Units (MVU) to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s doorstep. 
 

(b) As Animal Husbandry is a State subject, establishment & strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals and 
Dispensaries is under the domain of the State. However, the details of assistance provided to Tamil Nadu under the 
National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP), Critical Animal Disease Control Programme (CADCP), 
Assistance to States for Con trol of Animal Diseases (ASCAD) and  Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) during the 
last five years is as follows:  
i. Financial assistance of Rs 2,023.84 Lakh provided to the States under NADCP and CADCP for vaccination.  
ii. Total number of 61.88 lakh large sized ear tags and 144.58 Lakh small sized ear tags supplied under NADCP 
and CADCP for animal identification.   
iii. Financial assistance of Rs. 7,565.36 Lakh provided for procurement and operations of 245 MVUs.  
iv. To implement State prioritised activities related to livestock health, a sum of Rs. 1667.01 Lakh provided 
under ASCAD.  
v. Assistance was provided to the State for vaccination.  Around 8.66 crore vaccinations was done during the 
period. 
 
(c) Based on the report of the State of Tamil Nadu, the district-wise details of livestock vaccinated during 2025-
26 and 2026-27 (till 5 August 2026), Mobile Veterinary Units deployed and veterinary infrastructure strengthened 
is placed as Annexure I (a, b and c). 
 
(d) In addition to  (a to c)  above, Government of India (GOI)  is supporting the State  to improve disease 
surveillance, livestock healthcare and breed productivity as under:  
i. Financial support provided to Central Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (CDDL) , Indian Veterinary Research 
Institute (IVRI), Bareilly, five Regional Disease Diagnostic Labo ratories (RDDLs) of States for disease 
surveillance and other related activities.   
ii. Financial assistance provided to Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Institutes, namely National 
Institute of Foot and Mouth Disease (NIFMD), Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI) Bengaluru, IVRI 
Bareilly and National Institute on Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease Informatics (NIVEDI) Bengaluru 
for carrying out animal disease surveillance and other related activities.  
iii. National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases ( ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal undertakes surveillance of 
emerging and exotic transboundary animal diseases through laboratory-based surveillance.   
iv. Surveillance of animal diseases are also undertaken with help of Bharat Pashudhan portal developed by 
Department of AnimaL Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India (GOI).   
v. ICAR- NIVEDI, Bengaluru forecasts possible animal disease risk at district level around two months in 
advance through NADRES 2.0.  
vi. Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) is implemented for development and conservation of indigenous bovine 
breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population, enhancement of milk production and productivity of 
bovines across the country. Nationwide Artificial Insemination programme, Accelerated Breed Improvement 
programme using sex-sorted semen and In-vitro Fertilisation (IVF) Technology, Genomic chip for genomic 
selection, Progeny Testing and Pedigree Selection programme and Training and equipping Multi -Purpose 
Artificial Insemination Technicians (MAITRIs) are the key components.  
vii. A 3% interest subvention is provided  for infrastructure development  to individual entrepreneurs, private 
companies, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises  (MSME), Farmers Producers Organizations (FPOs), 
Section 8 companies. 
 
(e) Animal Husbandry  is a State subject . However, all schemes as (a) to (d) above is implemented by  
Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India (GOI)  across India including Tamil Nadu 
for livestock health care, livestock productivity and enhancing farmers' income.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3738 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 11th  AUGUST 2026 
 
NATIONAL FARM MECHANISATION POLICY 
 
3738. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to formulate a comprehensive National 
Farm Mechanisation Policy, drawing upon global best practices from South 
Korea, Japan, the United States, Israel and Australia including 
establishment of a national institutional mechanism for research; 
(b) whether the Government intends to promote intelligent agricultural robots, 
women-friendly farm implements, skill development and encourage 
domestic and foreign private investment to accelerate mechanisation 
particularly for marginal farmers; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish collaborative research, 
technology transfer and commercialization partnerships with South Korea 
and other technologically advanced countries to strengthen domestic farm 
mechanisation ecosystem and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): A Centrally Sponsored Scheme ‘Sub-Mission on Agricultural 
Mechanization’ (SMAM) under the umbrella of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana 
(RKVY) is already being implemented by the Department of Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) at the national level through the respective State 
Governments.  It has the major objectives of increasing the reach of farm 
mechanization to small and marginal farmers and to the regions where 
availability of farm power is low and promoting ‘Custom Hiring Centers’ to offset 
the adverse economies of scale arising due to small land holding and high cost 
of individual ownership of agricultural machines.  
The scheme provides financial assistance @ 40-50% of the cost of machines 
to farmers for the purchase of agricultural machinery and equipment. It also 
supports the establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) with financial 
assistance @ 40% of the project cost for the projects costing up to Rs. 250 
lakhs. Establishment of Farm Machinery Banks (FMBs) are supported with 
financial assistance @ 80% of the project cost for the projects costing up to Rs. 
30 lakhs. The financial assistance towards FMBs for the North Eastern States 

is @ 95% of the project cost. Adoption of modern farm machinery, including 
precision agriculture tools, drones and other advanced mechanization 
technologies and women-friendly farm implements are encouraged under 
SMAM. The SMAM also supports testing and certification of agricultural 
machinery, capacity building, demonstrations and training to encourage the 
adoption of advanced technologies.  
Along with the SMAM, the Crop Residue Management (CRM) Scheme is also 
implemented in the State of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh 
and NCT of Delhi to promote sustainable crop residue management through 
the provision of subsidized agricultural machinery, establishment of Custom 
Hiring Centres (CHCs), and other measures aimed at reducing stubble burning. 
Since 2023–24, the CRM Scheme is integrated with SMAM under the RKVY on 
a 60:40 Centre–State funding pattern. Horticulture mechanization is promoted 
under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) to improve 
farm efficiency and reduce drudgery of farm work force. Assistance under MIDH 
is provided for activities such as procurement of power operated machines and 
tools including plant protection equipments including import of new machines. 
Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), support is provided in the form 
of interest subvention, credit guarantee coverage, and medium to long term 
debt financing for eligible agriculture infrastructure projects like CHCs and 
FMBs. 
Research and development in agricultural mechanization are undertaken 
through the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).  It has seven 
institutes, which include six All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRP) 
with 105 Centres across India, two All India Network Projects and four 
Consortia Research Platforms.  The Government continuously reviews global 
technological developments and adopts suitable innovations and best 
practices, wherever appropriate, to improve the efficiency, productivity and 
sustainability of Indian agriculture.  
The Government permits 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) under the 
automatic route in the agricultural machinery manufacturing sector, 
encouraging global Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to establish 
domestic production units. This promotes domestic manufacturing, strengthens 
the agricultural machinery ecosystem and facilitates the induction of advanced 
technologies in Indian agriculture.  Participation of domestic and private sector 
enterprises in manufacturing, innovation, and mechanization services are also 
encouraged to accelerate the adoption of modern agricultural technologies. The 
Agri Startups developing innovative agricultural machinery and digital 
mechanization solutions receive support through incubation, innovation 
challenges and funding under RKVY- Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture 
and Allied Sector Rejuvenation (RAFTAAR) programme. The Government 
promotes private-sector-led mechanization service delivery through CHCs and 
machinery rental platforms, allowing farmers to hire equipment instead of 
purchasing it. The Government has also simplified testing and certification 
procedures for agricultural machinery to promote quality standards and ensure 
faster market access for manufacturers. 

(c): At present, there is no specific proposal to establish collaborative 
research, technology transfer, and commercialization partnerships with South 
Korea or other technologically advanced countries exclusively for agricultural 
mechanization. However, international cooperation in the field of agriculture, 
including agricultural mechanization, is undertaken through bilateral and 
multilateral collaborations with various countries under existing institutional 
mechanisms. Such cooperation encompasses collaborative research, 
technology transfer, capacity building, exchange of expertise, and other 
mutually agreed activities in accordance with the provisions of the respective 
agreements.

JOB CREATION IN MANUFACTURING AND SERVICES SECTORS 
 
3739.  SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the details of Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) of manufacturing and services 
sectors since 2014 till 2025–26, year-wise; 
 
(b)  the details of jobs created in manufacturing and services sectors during the 
same period, year-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government considers the level of job creation in these sectors 
sufficient in view of their growth performance and if so, the justification therefor; 
 
(d)  if not, the reasons for inadequate job creation despite growth in these sectors; 
and 
 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to increase employment generation in 
manufacturing and services sectors? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) is a monthly economic indicator 
compiled by HSBC India and S&P Global, private entities. The monthly details 
of PMIs for manufacturing and services in respect of India from FY 2014 -15 to 
FY 2025-26 is at Annexure I. 
(b): The details of worker population ratio (WPR) i.e . the percentage of persons 
employed among the persons in the population, and the distribution of workers 
in manufacturing and services sector during the period from July 2017 onwards, 
as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by Ministry of  
Statistics and Programme Implementation are given at Annexure II. 
(c) to (e): Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a priority of the 
Government. Various steps to expand job opportunities through various  
employment generation schemes/ programmes (non-exhaustive list at 
Annexure-III) have been taken, along with an increase in capital expenditure, 
to boost employment creation, increase production and productivity. Illustrative 
examples of Government interventions to generate empl oyment are as 
follows:- 
 

 
In Manufacturing sector, 892 applications approved under the Production 
Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes (as of 31 March 2026), have generated 
employment of over 14.15 lakh. Under the National Industrial Corridor 
Development Programme (NICDP), as of 30th June 2026 a total of 469 plots 
have been allotted. Of these, 376 plots (5,047 acres) are industrial plots, with a 
committed investment potential of approximately Rs. 2.20 lakh crore and an 
estimated employment potential of 1.29 lakh persons, as declared by investors 
at the time of allotment. 
Further, under the Startup India initiative, the Government constantly 
undertakes various eﬀorts for the development and growth of startup 
ecosystem and to enhance job creation in the country. As a result, a total of 
2,40,092 entities have been recognised as startups by Department for 
Promotion of Industries and Internal Trade (DPIIT) as on 30th June 2026. 
These recognized startups have reportedly created over 24.62 lakh direct jobs 
across more than 55 varied industries which include areas beyond technology 
as well. 
Additionally, the High -Powered 'Education to Employment & Enterprise' 
Standing Committee (HPSC -EEE) announced in the Union Budget 2026 -27 
was constituted on 22nd April 2026 to recommend measures that focus on the 
Services Sector as a core driver of Viksit Bharat to make us a global leader in 
services, with a 10% global share by 2047. It prioritises areas to optimise the 
potential for growth, employment and exports, while assessing the impact of 
emerging technologies, including AI, on jobs and skill requirements and 
proposing measures thereof. 
Also, the Ministry of Labour and Employment is running the National Career 
Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop solution for providing career related 
services including information on jobs from private and government sectors, 
online & offline job fairs, job search & matching, career counselling, vocational 
guidance, skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform.

CONTRIBUTION OF MANUFACTURING SECTOR TO GDP 
 
3740.  SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  the details of the contribution of the manufacturing sector to India’s Gross 
Domestic Product (GDP) along with the growth rate of the sector during the last 
five years, year-wise; 
 
(b)  whether the Government has assessed the reasons for the changes in the 
share of manufacturing in GDP and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  the details of measures taken under initiatives such as Make in I ndia, 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes and other industrial development 
programmes to increase  manufacturing capacity, attract investment and 
generate employment; 
 
(d)  whether the Government has fixed any targets to enhance the share of 
manufacturing in GDP and if so, the details thereof along with the progress 
achieved; and 
 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to address challenges faced by the 
manufacturing sector, including high input costs, infrastructure constraints, 
availability of skilled manpower, technology adoption and competitiveness of 
domestic industries? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): India’s manufacturing sector has experienced an increase in the contribution to 
India’s Gross Value Added (GVA). As per the National Accounts Statistics 
released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, the 
contribution of manufacturing sector to country’s GVA along with the growth is 
as follows: 
 
 
 

Year-wise contribution of manufacturing sector in GVA at constant prices 
(Base Year 2022-23) 
Year Contribution of Manufacturing 
in GVA (in %) 
Growth Rate (in %) 
2022-23 14.65 - 
2023-24 15.40 12.7

(FRE) 
15.69 9.3

FRE- First Revised Estimate; PE- Provisional Estimate 
Note: The figures of GVA for the revised base of the national accounts (2022–23) 
are available from 2022 –23 onwards, while the corresponding growth rates are 
available from 2023–24 onwards. 
The increase in the share of manufacturing sector is due to change in the level 
of manufacturing activity in the country supported by various 
Schemes/initiatives announced by the Government of India. 
(c) to (e): Government of India has taken several measures to increase manufacturing 
capacity, attract investment and generate employment. The ‘Make in India’ 
initiative was launched on 25th September 2014 to facilitate Investment, foster 
Innovation, build best in class Infrastructure, and make India a hub for 
manufacturing, design, and innovation. Presently, Make in India 2.0 focuses on 
27 sectors including 15 manufactur ing sectors, implemented across various 
Ministries and Departments and State Governments.  
 
As part of Make in India initiative, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes 
have been implemented across 14 key sectors, namely Large-Scale Electronics 
Manufacturing (LSEM), IT Hardware, Pharmaceuticals, Bulk Drugs, Medical 
Devices, Automobiles and Auto Components, Advanced Chemistry Cell 
Batteries, Solar PV modules, Telecom & Networking Products, Food Processing, 
Textiles, Specialty Steel, White Goods, Drones & Drone Components by 
incentivizing incremental production and sales. The PLI schemes have facilitated 
fresh investments in the identified sectors and supported the expansion of 
manufacturing capacities. To further the Make in India initiative, Government of 
India has announced the National Manufacturing Mission (NMM) in the Union 
Budget 2025-26, which envisages increasing the share of Manufacturing in GDP 
to 25% by 2035.  
 
Additionally, under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme 
(NICDP), a total of 469 plots, admeasuring 5,347 acres have been allotted, as of 
30th June 2026. Of these, 376 plots (5,047 acres) are industrial plots, with a 
committed investment potential of approximately Rs 2.20 lakh crore and an 
estimated employment potential of 1.29 lakh persons, as declared by investors 
at the time of allotment. 
The Government promotes Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) through an investor-
friendly policy that allows up to 100% FDI under the automatic route in most 

sectors, accounting for over 90% of FDI inflows. The National Single Window 
System (NSWS) provides a single online platform for approvals and permissions. 
To maintain India as an attractive investment destination, the Government 
regularly reviews and liberalises the FDI policy through stakeholder 
consultations. Reforms have simplified FDI norms across sectors including 
defence, insurance, telecom, space, pharmaceuticals, retail, civil aviation, digital 
media, e-commerce, coal mining, and financial services. 
To support Startups across sectors, the Government is undertaking taking 
various measures under the Startup India initia tive. The flagship Schemes 
namely, Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), Startup India Seed Fund Scheme 
(SISFS) and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) support startups 
across sectors at various stages of their business cycle. The Government  also 
implements periodic exercises and programs including States’ Startup Ranking, 
National Startup Awards, Innovation Week, and TEJAS (Transforming 
Entrepreneurial Journeys Across States & Districts) which play an important role 
in the holistic development of the s tartup ecosystem including non -metro and 
rural startup ecosystems. The Government also encourages and supports 
ecosystem led initiatives to improve market access and enable public 
procurement to scaling up their businesses. The Government has also taken 
various measures to enhance ease of doing business including starting up of 
business, raising capital, and reducing compliance burden to simplify the 
regulatory environment and create a conducive business environment. Activities 
to encourage corporates to su pport startups by way of mentorship, access to 
infrastructure, sharing resources and knowledge, assistance in market linkages, 
and investor connect are also undertaken. 
 
The other major initiatives include National Single Window System, GIS enabled 
Land Ba nk, PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan for integrated planning of 
multimodal infrastructure, Project Monitoring Group to remove bottlenecks in 
setting up of major infrastructure projects, setting up of industrial parks, 
interventions to improve ease of do ing business, measures for reduction in 
compliance burden, rationalization of labour laws, introduction of Goods and 
Services Tax, policy measures to boost domestic manufacturing through public 
procurement orders, Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) and Q uality 
Control Orders (QCOs), to name major ones. 
 
Recently, the Government has notified the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana 
(BHAVYA) Scheme, with a financial outlay of ₹ 33,660 crore for a period of 6 
years. The objective of the Scheme is to develop investme nt-ready industrial 
parks for enabling investors to ground investment with ease, thereby adding to 
the manufacturing capacity in the country. Under the Scheme, financial 
assistance is to be provided for development of 100 industrial parks.

(a):  The sum insured is determined on the basis of the Scale of Finance (SoF) declared

hectare for all crops including horticultural crops, as selected by the State/UT Government 
concerned. This is the maximum claim amount payable per hectare under the Pradhan 
Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)/Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
(RWBCIS).  
 
(b):  Since inception of RWBCIS in Kharif 2016, total 213.19 lakh farmer applications, 
growing horticultural crops, have been enrolled in the country.  State Government of 
Madhya Pradesh has not notified horticulture crops under these schemes.  
 
(c):  Scale of Finance for all crops including horticultural crops, for advancing of  crop 
loans under Kisan Credit Card (KCC) are declared by the State Level Technical Committee 
(SLTC) for each district in the respective State. 
 
(d):  Horticulture crop producing farmers are covered under the crop insurance schemes 
implemented by the Government, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS), subject to notification of 
the crop and area by the concerned State/UT Government.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a to (d) The Export Promotion Mission, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 and 
approved by the Union Cabinet in November 2025 with an outlay of over ₹25,000 
crore for the period 2025 -26 to 2030 -31, is being jointly implemented by the 
Department of Commerce, Ministry of MSME and Ministry of Finance. The Mission 
proposes to address the challenges faced by MSME exporters in  accessing 
international markets by way of extending support for access to trade finance capacity 
enablement through support for market access, capacity building, and quality 
certifications. 
EPM operates through two integrated sub-schemes: 
 
i. Niryat Prothsahan: Focused on expanding access to aﬀordable trade 
finance through instruments such as Interest Subvention for  pre- and post- 
shipment export credit, Export Factoring support, Collateral Guarantees for 
export credit, Credit Guarantee  for e-commerce exporters, and Credit 
Enhancement support for the 
MSME exporters. 

 
2 
 
ii. Niryat Disha: Focused on critical non -financial trade enablers, including 
export quality and compliance support, logistics and overseas warehousing, 
Market Access Support, global branding and packaging, Facilitating Logistics 
Interventions for Freight & Transport, support for trade intelligence and 
capacity building activities. 
 
 Under the Developing Districts as Export Hub (DEH) initiative, exportable 
products (including agricultural and MSME/artisanal products) have been identified 
across districts of the country. The institutional architecture includes State Level Export 
Promotion Committees, District Export Promotion Committees. The capacity building 
programs under the DEH initiative are aimed at creating linkages between district-level 
producers, including MSME clusters, SHGs and e -commerce exporters to global 
markets by leveraging the interventions of EPM. Outreach programs are held in 
collaboration with e -commerce platforms to on -board producers to e -commerce 
platforms and enter international markets. 
 
Under EPM, support is extended to eligible entities involved in setting up 
overseas warehousing facility, overseas fulfilment centres, display facilities and e -
Commerce Export Hubs (ECEH). E -Commerce exporters are also provided credit 
guarantee cover for credit availed by them for exports to global markets through postal 
or courier or holding inventory in ECEHs, overseas warehouses for e-commerce sales. 
 
The Government has taken steps to promote exports of products made by 
SHGs, including: 
 SARAS Aajeevika Melas to showcase SHG products having export potential to 
prospective international buyers. 
 Capacity building through training on product quality, design, packaging and 
international market requirements, along with facilitation of certifications such as ISO, 
organic and Fair Trade, and support for collaborative export consortia among SHG 
federations. 
 The Government, through the National Handloom Development Programme 
(NHDP), organises domestic and international marketing events fo r handloom and 
handicraft artisans, many of whom are organised as SHGs/producer collectives. 
 
Periodic stakeholder consultations and continuous assessment of 
implementation challenges are undertaken through interactions with exporters, Export 
Promotion Councils, industry associations and State Governments. 
 
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) has established 
65 Export Facilitation Centers (EFCs) in its field offices across the country with the aim 
of providing requisite mentoring and handholding support to MSMEs in exporting their 
products and services. EFCs support MSME exporters  by providing comprehensive 
assistance across key areas. These include dissemination of information on export -
related schemes and benefits, training and workshops on export compliance, 
handholding in export documentation and procedures,  engagement with industry 
associations, State Governments, and Central Government Departments to facilitate 
MSMEs.

E-FIR UNDER BNSS  
 
†3743.      SHRI TANUJ PUNIA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the legal timeline and mandatory rules laid down for registering an e-FIR 
in the country under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita;  
(b) whether the rule specifying a three -day timeline for issuing an 
acknowledgment to the complainant after the registration of an e -FIR and 
obtaining his/her formal signature by the police is being strictly implemented 
across all States; and  
(c) whether an e-FIR is cancelled in case the complainant is unable to reach 
the police station within the stipulated time limit and whether any other 
digital alternative is available to proceed with the investigation and if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (c): Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 
2023, inter-alia,  provides  that every information relating to the commission  
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 3743 FOR 11.08.2026 
 
of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is 
committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer 
in charge of a police station, and if given orally, it shall be reduced in writing 
by him which shall be signed by the person giving it. In case information is 
given by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record by the officer 
incharge of Police Station on being signed within three days by the

through electronic communication needs to be signed by the informant

(a) the details and total amount allocated by the Government as grants to startups in technical 
textiles in the current fiscal year and the criteria used for selecting these startups in Telangana 
State;  
(b) the anticipated economic impact of these grants on the technical textiles sector, supported by 
projected growth figures and employment generation estimates;  
(c) the number of startups that have received grants under this initiative so far along with the

develop in Telangana State; and  
(d) the  Government’s strategy to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of these grants in

performance indicators tracked annually? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a):  Under the Ministry of Textile's  National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the 
scheme of "Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Techni cal 
Textiles (GREAT)" aims to support the start -up ecosystem in the technical textiles sector across 
the country, including Telangana, by providing assistance to young innovators, scientists, 
technologists, and start -up ventures in translating their ideas into commercial technologies and 
products. The total budget allocated to the NTTM for the current financial year (2026 -27) is Rs. 
256 crore, which includes the provision for releasing grants to start -ups under the GREAT 
scheme.  
Under NTTM, 15 research pro jects and 01 application from an educational institution under the 
"General Guidelines for Enabling of Academic Institutes in Technical Textiles Education in 
India: For Private and Public Institutes" have been approved from the State of Telangana. 
An Evaluation and Monitoring Committee (EMC) has been constituted under NTTM to evaluate, 
monitor, and review the technical and financial parameters of the start -up proposals. Based on 
the criteria laid out in the GREAT guidelines, the EMC submits its recommendati ons to the 

Empowered Programme Committee (EPC) under NTTM for approval of start -up proposals. 
GREAT guidelines are available at https://nttm.texmin.gov.in.

commercialization of indigenous technologies, and the development of value -added technical

fostering strong synergies between innovators and industry stakeholders for prototype 
development, field trials, and market launches, the scheme ensures mark et-ready 
commercialization. This active industry engagement is anticipated to successfully scale these 
start-ups, significantly strengthen the overall technical textiles ecosystem in the country, and 
thereby catalyze broader sustainable industry growth and employment generation. 
  
(c):  Under NTTM, a total of 31 start -ups have been approved at a total cost of Rs 15.40 
crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India share, details of which are given at 
Annexure-I. 
  
(d):  Under NTTM, a Review and M onitoring Committee has been constituted to assess and 
oversee the progress of the approved start -ups, with the authority to recommend for release of 
subsequent instalments of grant and closure of projects to the Empowered Programme 
Committee. Further, various public events, workshops, seminars and outreach activities are being 
organized nationwide to disseminate information about the scheme and facilitate industry
